suggestion.title: Nuclio CronJob curl execution with shell-injected headers — serviceaccount token exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'unsanitized cron trigger event headers/body injected into CronJob shell command'. The natural exploitation path is injecting shell metacharacters into event.headers, causing curl to execute attacker payload and read /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for /bin/sh spawning curl with --header arguments containing shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, ;, |, &&). Correlate with process reads of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. Look for curl writing to non-standard sinks or exfiltrating tokens to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes CronJob anomalies — Nuclio controller injecting malicious commands into cron job specs
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability manifests in the Kubernetes CronJob spec: 'Nuclio controller builds a curl invocation string for each cron trigger and stores it as the args of a Kubernetes CronJob container'. Malicious event.headers flow into the CronJob spec itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor kubectl apply events and Kubernetes audit logs for CronJob creation by Nuclio controller serviceaccount where the job spec args field contains unusual shell patterns (command substitution, shell redirections, quoting anomalies) not typical of curl invocations.

suggestion.title: Malicious Nuclio function cron-trigger specification with shell-injection payload in event headers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'event.headers keys — interpolated verbatim inside double-quoted --header arguments'. Attack entry point is the function specification itself; malicious headers are defined at deployment time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Nuclio function deployments (Kubernetes Function CRD or Nuclio API calls) where the cron trigger spec contains shell escape sequences, backticks, command substitution $(...), or semicolons in event.headers or event.body fields.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via Kubernetes API calls using exfiltrated serviceaccount token
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation: after shell injection reads the serviceaccount token (T1552.001), attacker can authenticate to the Kubernetes API to create/modify deployments, access secrets, or persist within the cluster.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API server authentication using a serviceaccount token from unexpected clients (non-pod IPs, unexpected geographic locations, or timing misaligned with legitimate Nuclio controller operations). Flag API calls that attempt to list secrets, create deployments, or modify RBAC bindings.

suggestion.title: Network exfiltration of Kubernetes secrets via Nuclio CronJob RCE
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation of the RCE: the injected shell command can access mounted secrets and exfiltrate them. The Nuclio pod's serviceaccount token enables lateral movement and secret access within the cluster.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate CronJob execution with unusual network egress from Nuclio pods to attacker-controlled IPs, especially in data volumes inconsistent with normal operation. Look for processes inside pods reading /var/run/secrets or other mount paths followed by network writes.

suggestion.title: Roundcube XSS Execution Leading to IceCube Loader
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Opening the email in a vulnerable Roundcube webmail client triggers exploitation of a cross-site scripting flaw tracked as CVE-2024-42009, which executes JavaScript code inside the victim's browser, loading a payload called IceCube.' No detection use case covers the XSS trigger or JavaScript payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malformed or suspicious email messages triggering JavaScript execution within Roundcube sessions, evidenced by unusual browser console activity, XSS payload patterns, or unexpected script downloads immediately after email open events. Monitor for IceCube process spawning or DNS resolution post-execution.

suggestion.title: IceCube In-Memory Credential and Session Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'IceCube is a fully-featured Roundcube stealer that can harvest usernames, passwords, cookies, two-factor authentication (2FA) data, and browser information.' No use case addresses credential theft immediately following XSS execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid memory read operations against browser credential stores, session cookie files, or Roundcube authentication tokens immediately following XSS-triggered JavaScript execution. Monitor for credential exfiltration traffic from the affected mail server or unusual authentication token usage patterns post-infection.

suggestion.title: Roundcube Deserialization RCE Leading to SquareShell Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'uses helpers to exploit a Roundcube deserialization flaw tracked as CVE-2025-49113 and attempts to install SquareShell, a PHP webshell that includes remote code execution capabilities.' No detection covers the secondary exploitation vector or webshell deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect deserialization gadget chains or unexpected object instantiation patterns in Roundcube request logs. Monitor for SquareShell PHP file creation in web-accessible directories, unusual PHP process spawning with RCE indicators, or suspicious PHP execution within mail server directories post-compromise.

suggestion.title: VShell Go-Based Backdoor Execution and C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'VShell is a commodity Go-based backdoor that supports interactive shell access and port forwarding, which is commonly used by Chinese threat actors.' No use case detects VShell installation or C2 activity post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Go-compiled binary execution on mail servers with network beaconing behavior, including port forwarding and unusual outbound connections from mail service context. Monitor for interactive shell access patterns originating from VShell, including unusual system command sequences from mail daemon accounts and internal service tunneling.

suggestion.title: Spoofed Academic Institution Email Delivering XSS Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'attack begins with a malicious email sent from compromised accounts or spoofed domains, using a generic lure' targeting 'U.S. and Canadian universities' and 'physics and engineering departments.' No use case covers the initial phishing vector with spoofed academic sender metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email messages to academic institutions' physics/engineering departments with sender spoofing indicators (DMARC/SPF/DKIM failures, lookalike domains, compromised internal accounts). Flag emails with generic lures that fail authentication but bypass filters, correlate with downstream Roundcube access anomalies post-delivery.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Against Roundcube Instances for CVE-2024-42009 and CVE-2025-49113
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'UNK_MassTraction appears to have selected servers previously deemed vulnerable to CVE-2024-42009 and CVE-2025-49113, so some reconnaissance was performed prior to the attacks.' No detection covers the pre-exploitation scanning or fingerprinting phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning or fingerprinting attempts against Roundcube instances, including version enumeration requests, software identification probes targeting known vulnerable paths, or unusual user-agent patterns consistent with automated reconnaissance. Correlate with later exploitation attempts from the same source IP or infrastructure.

suggestion.title: SFI-led Proactive Hardening: Vulnerability Scanning & Patch Deployment at Scale
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'proactively hardens our cloud' — requires extraction of actual article body to identify scanning/patching mechanisms, automation tooling, and defensive infrastructure changes Microsoft deployed. Expected content would describe discovery, remediation, and deployment workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse Microsoft's SFI documentation (when article is properly ingested) for indicators of automated scanning, patching pipelines, and infrastructure hardening deployments. Detection should trigger on unauthorized or out-of-band patching workflows, disabled hardening controls, or rollback of SFI mitigations.

suggestion.title: AI-Accelerated Threat Detection & Response in Microsoft Cloud
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'AI speed' — actual article likely details AI-powered threat hunting, anomaly detection, or incident response automation. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: When article is accessible: identify AI/ML-based detection rules, threat-hunting queries, and automated response actions Microsoft deployed. Flag adversary attempts to evade these defenses (e.g., evasion of behavioral analytics, noise injection to overwhelm ML models).

suggestion.title: UniFi Management Interface Unauthenticated Access
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly lists UniFi OS (core controller) as vulnerable. Ubiquiti appliances are management-tier targets; web UI exploitation is canonical attack surface. No initial-access UC generated despite 'critical' severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to /api/ or /admin/ paths from unauthenticated sessions that return 200 instead of 401/403, or requests to /system/upgrade endpoint bypassing CSRF/session checks.

suggestion.title: UniFi Cross-Product Lateral Movement via Shared Secrets
suggestion.rationale: Article lists Connect, Talk, Access, Protect as separate but integrated products within single UniFi suite. 'Critical' rating implies management-layer compromise. No lateral-movement use case despite obvious trust boundaries between products.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect token/credential reuse across UniFi service boundaries (e.g., controller-issued session used to authenticate to Protect API, or Connect admin token reused for Talk provisioning).

suggestion.title: UniFi Firmware/Bundle Upload Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Ubiquiti historical pattern: critical severity in management controller typically means firmware/bundle upload exploitation. Title mentions OS-level flaws. Common Ubiquiti attack vector entirely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PUT/POST to /api/s/default/cmd/backup, /system/upgrade, or /upload endpoints from sources outside admin IP whitelist. Flag spawning of shell processes (bash, sh) as children of Java/Node.js UniFi controller process.

suggestion.title: UniFi Access (Physical Access Control) Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Access product controls door/building security. 'Critical' flaws in physical access appliance imply privilege escalation to read/modify access rules. No privilege-escalation UC despite management-appliance threat model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution from unifi-access or access-service account with unexpected UID/privilege elevation, modification of /etc/sudoers or systemd unit files, or config writes outside management API.

suggestion.title: UniFi Talk Credential Interception (VoIP/SIP)
suggestion.rationale: Talk product provides voice/communications. Article lists as vulnerable. No credential-access use case despite VoIP/SIP services typically being high-value targets for credential harvesting or MITM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed authentication attempts to Talk SIP/provisioning endpoints, plaintext or base64-encoded credential transmission, or ARP spoofing/DNS hijacking of Talk service discovery.

suggestion.title: UniFi Protect Video/Analytics Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Protect is surveillance platform storing video/metadata. Critical flaws could enable bulk data theft. No exfiltration use case despite high-sensitivity data asset and typical Ubiquiti deployment scale (multi-camera, multi-site).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume outbound transfers from Protect database/storage to external/unexpected IPs, bulk requests to /api/bootstrap or /video endpoints outside authenticated admin sessions, or rsync/curl exfil of .db files.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance on unauthenticated /api/documents/search-content endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists '/api/documents/search-content/*' as an unauthenticated endpoint. UC_100_3 covers upload and history, but search queries are the attacker's recon phase—enumerating document metadata before exfiltration. Not currently detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sequences of GET requests to /api/documents/search-content returning 200 from unauthenticated sources. Baseline: >10 unique search queries from same src within 5 minutes, or search requests with progressively broader/systematic query terms indicates automated enumeration.

suggestion.title: Bulk document exfiltration—large-volume reads on /api/documents/get or export endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes that arbitrary content can be uploaded and read unauthenticated. Sophisticated attackers iterate over document IDs or collections to bulk-download. UC_100_3 detects single writes/reads; missing detection for sustained high-volume exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET requests to /api/documents/* endpoints returning 200 with cumulative response payload >10 MB from unauthenticated source over 5-minute window, or >50 sequential GET requests to /api/documents/get or /api/documents/export within 10 minutes. Indicates bulk data theft.

suggestion.title: Auth-bypass verification—credentials present in unauthenticated request body to /api/documents/upload
suggestion.rationale: Article notes the server accepts MCP_API_KEY and OAuth but doesn't enforce them on /api/documents endpoints. An attacker might test by including credentials (X-API-Key, Authorization header, Bearer token in body) to confirm they are ignored—verifying the bypass is real.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/documents/upload returning 200 that include Authorization headers, X-API-Key, or 'Authorization: Bearer' tokens in the request. If auth credentials are present but request succeeds, confirms endpoint ignores them—direct evidence of bypass.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage attack chain: auth-probe, exploit, exfiltrate, destroy—same source over 15 minutes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes full attack capability: read, write, delete. UC_100_4 detects 401→200. Should detect sustained attack: (1) failed /api/memories probe, (2) successful /api/documents/upload, (3) bulk reads via search or export, (4) DELETE cleanup—all from same src in short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate 4-step sequence from same src within 15 minutes: (1) any 401 to /api/memories*, (2) POST 200 to /api/documents/upload, (3) GET 200 with >1MB response OR >20 GET requests to /api/documents/*, (4) DELETE 200 to /api/documents/remove*. Indicates full exploit-to-cover-tracks workflow.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Inventory Scan

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for Adobe ColdFusion presence and patch status. Alert on unpatched or unknown ColdFusion versions against CVE-2026-48282 patches. Cross-reference scanner results against software lifecycle database for patch-lag outliers.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Attempt Detection Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Adobe ColdFusion contains a path traversal vulnerability.' Pipeline missed the core exploitation vector. Exploit syntax includes directory traversal sequences (.., encoded variants, protocol handlers).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to ColdFusion endpoints (/CFIDE/, /cfusion, /cf_scripts) for path traversal patterns: .., %2e%2e, ../, encoded slashes, and file:// or jar: protocol handlers. Baseline benign admin traffic first.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Arbitrary Code Execution Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline omitted execution-phase detection for child-process anomalies from ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, java ColdFusion process).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by ColdFusion application server: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, curl, wget from cfusion.exe parent. Correlate with prior HTTP path-traversal attempts. Baseline normal ColdFusion child-process behavior per environment.

suggestion.title: Exposed ColdFusion Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190 implies external exposure). No discovery detection generated for publicly accessible ColdFusion admin interfaces, version banners, or network scans targeting ColdFusion default ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for incoming network traffic to ColdFusion default ports (8500–8502, 80, 443) with ColdFusion-identifying HTTP headers or admin paths (/CFIDE/administrator, /CFIDE/debug). Flag ColdFusion version-banner disclosures in HTTP responses reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match: CVE-2026-48282
suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE-2026-48282 as primary indicator; pipeline captured zero IOCs. Federal remediation deadline 2026-07-10 and CISA KEV status require scanner-based detection. Article phrase: 'CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scan finding CVE-2026-48282 on ColdFusion instances. Prioritize by exposure (internet-facing) and age of patch lag. Critical for federal deadline compliance and CISA KEV exploitation tracking.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Web Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability'; pipeline generated zero execution-phase or initial-access detection. Article phrase: 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to publicly exposed ColdFusion endpoints for path traversal patterns: ../, ..\ encoded variants (..%2f, ..%5c), unicode escapes, and nested traversal. Correlate with 400/403 errors and repeated attempts from same source.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public Exposure Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV exploits only strike exposed targets. Article: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]'. Pipeline generated zero asset-exposure use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all ColdFusion instances with internet-routable DNS or certificate records. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-48282. Prioritize public-facing instances for patch verification before 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution via ColdFusion Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'; pipeline missed execution-phase detection. Gap: exploitation outcome detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child process spawning from ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, coldfusion service process). Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or shell invocation with parent process ColdFusion, especially if preceded by HTTP 200 response to unusual ColdFusion endpoint URL.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Error Log Anomaly – File Write to Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal + code execution typically manifests as file writes to web-accessible directories; pipeline produced no persistence or discovery detection. Article implies post-exploitation file access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion application logs for file I/O errors or successful writes to unusual paths (../, alternative drives, etc.). Correlate with HTTP access logs showing GET requests to web-root files matching timestamps of error log entries.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Adobe ColdFusion contains a path traversal vulnerability' and implies active exploitation in the wild via CISA KEV listing. No detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints for path traversal payloads (../, ..\, %2e%2e, unicode encoding variants). Correlate against known ColdFusion vulnerable paths and version info from endpoint instrumentation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Remote Code Execution Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—post-exploitation process creation should be detected when exploitation succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child process creation from ColdFusion service (cfusion.exe, java.exe spawning ColdFusion runtime) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or system utilities. Baseline normal ColdFusion process trees first.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable ColdFusion Instance Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check'—implies need for explicit vulnerability-status detection separate from generic web servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Qualys/Nessus/Tenable scans or banner-grab data against ColdFusion versions known vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282. Flag instances with unpatched or end-of-support ColdFusion versions accessible from the internet.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Access from ColdFusion Context
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal inherently implies traversing outside intended directories—file access logging should capture attempts to read/write outside ColdFusion application root.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file open/read events from ColdFusion process (user=cfusion or NETWORK SERVICE) targeting system directories (Windows, Program Files, etc.) outside the ColdFusion install path and web root.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from Compromised ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: RCE in ColdFusion is typically a beachhead; no use case captures subsequent lateral-movement indicators (SMB, RDP, credential theft from the compromised host).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After ColdFusion RCE, look for new SMB connection attempts from the affected host to other internal systems, process injection, or credential dumping tool execution (mimikatz, sekurlsa) spawned from ColdFusion child processes.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Scheduled Task or Service Installation for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Once inside via RCE, attackers typically establish persistence; the article does not mention persistence indicators, implying the pipeline missed post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new scheduled tasks, Windows services, or startup items created by ColdFusion process or by user accounts associated with ColdFusion privilege contexts. Correlate timing with HTTP anomalies.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public-Facing Asset Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internet-accessible ColdFusion instances via port enumeration (8500, 80, 443 with ColdFusion banners), vulnerability scanner detection, or passive DNS/EASM data. Alert on ColdFusion services reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'path traversal vulnerability' as attack vector. Core exploitation technique for CVE-2026-48282.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution from ColdFusion Process

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious child processes spawned from ColdFusion (cfusion.exe, java.exe for Acrobat ColdFusion). Flag powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or system administrative tools invoked from ColdFusion context. Alert on unexpected network connections from ColdFusion process.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable ColdFusion Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and recommends 'quick check across fleet.' Inventory-based detection for unpatched systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management tools for ColdFusion service versions prior to patch date. Cross-reference with federal due date (2026-07-10) to identify non-compliant assets. Correlate with network telemetry to confirm exposed instances.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Failed Authentication or Authorization Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal in application context often bypasses access controls. Article's 'current user' context implies authentication bypass or privilege escalation risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for anomalous ColdFusion authentication patterns: repeated 401/403 responses followed by successful 200 responses on admin endpoints, access to restricted directories without prior auth, or session token reuse patterns.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public Asset Exposure (CVE-2026-48282)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'public-facing application' as the attack vector and states 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited.' Standard asset-exposure hunt is foundational for any actively-exploited vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all ColdFusion instances (CFUSION processes, port 8500 default, or CFIDE endpoints) with inbound network exposure from untrusted zones. Correlate asset inventory with firewall rules and WAF logs to find exposed systems. Prioritize systems matching vulnerable version patterns to CVE-2026-48282.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Against ColdFusion Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article's core vulnerability type is 'path traversal' — this is the actual exploit mechanism. Detection of traversal patterns in HTTP request logs is the primary detection for T1190 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to ColdFusion application or admin endpoints (/CFIDE/, /cfusion/) containing path traversal sequences: `../`, `..%2f`, `..%252f`, encoded variants, or attempts to escape to sensitive paths. Correlate with post-exploit indicators (RCE, file writes, outbound connections).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Arbitrary Code Execution from ColdFusion Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' RCE execution following successful path traversal is the impact indicator and post-compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect command shell or binary execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, perl, etc.) spawned from ColdFusion interpreter processes (java.exe, coldfusion.exe) or Apache parent process. Focus on unexpected child processes with suspicious arguments, unusual working directories, or rapid child-process spawning indicating batch exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Detection in Vulnerability Scans
suggestion.rationale: Article's detection strategy explicitly states 'CVE matcher in vulnerability scanner' as primary control. Any scan match represents confirmed vulnerable asset requiring remediation by federal due date (2026-07-10).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management systems for CVE-2026-48282 findings. Track all flagged assets and correlate with patch deployment logs to identify systems with confirmed vulnerability + missing patch as of 2026-07-10 federal deadline. Escalate remediation failures for compliance reporting.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Admin Console Unauthorized Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploitation of a public-facing ColdFusion application commonly targets administrative endpoints. Article describes public exposure as the attack vector, increasing likelihood of admin console targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed authentication attempts to ColdFusion Administrator endpoint (typically /CFIDE/administrator/index.cfm). Combine with concurrent path traversal pattern detection. Alert on: unusual geographic origin, rapid multi-attempt patterns, or failed auth + successful subsequent requests (indicating bypass).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and recommends standard asset-exposure hunt. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all assets reporting CVE-2026-48282 in scanner inventory. Prioritize Internet-facing ColdFusion instances. Track remediation against federal due-date 2026-07-10. Cross-correlate scanning timestamp with exploitation indicators to assess patch lag vulnerability.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Attempt Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints containing `../`, `..\`, `%2e%2e`, or Unicode-encoded traversal sequences. Alert on requests attempting to escape wwwroot or accessing sensitive directories (/windows/, /etc/, etc.).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion-Spawned Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline missed process-creation detection from ColdFusion service accounts executing unexpected child processes (shells, utilities).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ColdFusion process (cfusion.exe, jrun.exe) spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other shell interpreters with unexpected arguments. Flag parent-child relationships anomalous to normal ColdFusion operation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Filesystem Escape Detection
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal attacks require accessing files outside the application root. Article describes filesystem-based attack but pipeline generated no file-access anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process file-access events for rapid enumeration or access to directories outside wwwroot (System32, Program Files, Windows registry hives). Baseline normal ColdFusion file patterns first.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Application Log Exception Analysis
suggestion.rationale: ColdFusion logs contain path-resolution errors preceding successful traversal. Article points to exploitation but pipeline omitted application-log-source detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse ColdFusion logs for access-denied, path-not-found, or traversal-triggered security exceptions. Correlate exception timestamps with web-server 400/403 HTTP responses to prioritize investigation.

suggestion.title: Web Application Firewall Path Traversal Blocking
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies public-facing ColdFusion as attack surface ('Exploit Public-Facing Application'). Network-layer WAF rules are standard mitigation but pipeline proposed no WAF-native detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enable ColdFusion-specific path-traversal rules in WAF. Alert on WAF blocks matching CVE-2026-48282 exploitation signatures. Correlate WAF blocks with application logs to measure evasion attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Presence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2026-48282 in Adobe ColdFusion as the vulnerability. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the core detection target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner exports and patch-compliance databases for ColdFusion instances reporting CVE-2026-48282 or running unpatched ColdFusion versions released before 2026-07-10 federal remediation deadline. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify exposed instances.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public-Facing Application Inventory

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attempt Detection in ColdFusion Logs

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Execution Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline missed execution-phase detection despite explicit mention of code execution outcome.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Patch Compliance Audit (Federal Deadline)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10' and emphasizes CISA KEV remediation deadline. Pipeline should have included compliance-tracking use case for regulated entities.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Adobe ColdFusion instances with internet-facing network paths. Escalate on instances showing inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic from untrusted sources, especially post-reconnaissance patterns.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attack Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as exploitation technique. Pipeline generated zero detection rules for traversal patterns despite this being the core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e/, unicode variants). Alert on successful responses (HTTP 200/301) indicating traversal beyond application root directory.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline failed to map execution-phase detections despite clear post-exploitation impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process (java.exe, cfusion.exe) for unexpected child process spawning, especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or shell interpreters. Correlate with path traversal attempt timestamps to identify successful exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Audit—ColdFusion Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check'—patch lag is explicit hunt target. Pipeline generated zero compliance-driven detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all ColdFusion installations for version and patch level. Flag any instance below minimum patched version for CVE-2026-48282 regardless of scanner freshness, prioritizing public-facing deployments.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'path traversal vulnerability…could lead to arbitrary code execution'—core attack vector must be detected in request payloads and logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for path traversal patterns (../, .., encoded variants) in ColdFusion request URIs and parameter values. Baseline legitimate traversal depth and alert on anomalous directory enumeration attempts targeting sensitive paths (/cfusion, /administrator, /system).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Post-Exploitation Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—post-RCE activity is the direct impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for subprocess creation or shell invocation spawned from ColdFusion worker processes (e.g., cfusion.exe, java.exe parent=ColdFusion). Alert on unexpected command-line tools (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil) launched from web context.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable ColdFusion Instance Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'asset-exposure hunt' template and CISA KEV implies public-facing assets are already compromised—discovery scanning is mandatory baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for HTTP(S) services responding with ColdFusion server banners, error pages containing 'ColdFusion' strings, or characteristic request handlers (/cfide/, /cfusion/). Cross-reference against patched inventory; flag unpatched instances with CVE-2026-48282 exposure.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Web Shell Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation via traversal + RCE enables web shell persistence; article context implies ongoing threat ('currently being exploited'). Post-compromise artifacts are primary hunt vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .cfm, .cfml file creation/modification in unexpected ColdFusion directories (webroot, /cfide/, temp paths). Alert on files with anomalous naming patterns (random strings, suspicious extensions), unusual timestamps during off-hours, or high entropy content indicative of obfuscated code.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Outbound C2 Command and Control Detection
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, compromised servers establish command channels for attacker control—necessary to detect ongoing breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline ColdFusion process network behavior. Alert on new outbound connections to non-whitelisted destinations, especially to high-risk ASNs or IPs with malware reputation. Monitor DNS queries for suspicious domains or DGA patterns originating from ColdFusion processes.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Configuration Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal + RCE access allows attackers to modify cfusion.ini, datasources, or authentication settings for persistence or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion configuration files (cfusion.ini, neo-*.xml, scheduler state) for unauthorized modification. Alert on addition of new administrators, datasource credential changes, or disabled security settings. Verify modifications against change-management tickets.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline did not extract this IOC or recommend scanner-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner reports CVE-2026-48282 (Adobe ColdFusion) with high confidence on public-facing assets. This is a CISA KEV entry, meaning active exploitation observed—treat as critical priority. Flag any instance after federal patch due date 2026-07-10 for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Attempts Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'path traversal' type. This is File and Directory Discovery (T1083), not covered by the pipeline's single mention of T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints (*.cfm, admin, /administrator) containing path traversal payloads: `../`, `..\`, `%2e%2e`, encoded variants, or absolute path attempts (e.g., `/etc/passwd`, `C:\windows`). Correlate with ColdFusion access logs and WAF blocks.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Spawning Child Processes Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user,' implying T1059 execution post-compromise. Pipeline did not suggest execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ColdFusion process (jrun.exe, java.exe running ColdFusion JVM) spawns unexpected child processes: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, notepad.exe, or network tools. Baseline benign spawns per environment; this DEVs post-exploitation behavior from arbitrary code execution.

suggestion.title: Unpatched ColdFusion After Federal Compliance Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10.' Pipeline did not flag compliance-driven detection for post-deadline unpatched systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory with vulnerability scanner findings: flag all systems running Adobe ColdFusion with unpatched CVE-2026-48282 after 2026-07-10 as compliance violations and critical exposure. This is CISA KEV—active exploitation confirmed.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Admin Interface Access After Exploitation Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active exploitation of 'public-facing application.' Post-compromise, attackers may access administrative interfaces via path traversal. This is discovery and lateral movement post-RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting potential path traversal or RCE indicators, correlate with suspicious ColdFusion admin access (e.g., /administrator, /cfadmin paths accessed from unexpected IP or out-of-hours). Look for session establishment or credential attempts in ColdFusion logs post-compromise window.

suggestion.title: File System Writes from ColdFusion Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal + RCE typically culminates in file writes (webshells, backdoors). Article does not detail post-exploitation, but pipeline should infer this from 'arbitrary code execution' phrase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to web-accessible directories (ColdFusion wwwroot, /Administrator paths) or system executables initiated by ColdFusion JVM process. Baseline known updates; flag new .cfm, .cfml, .exe, .dll, .ps1 files or modifications to existing web assets during active hours when patch deployment unlikely.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Gmail API Access via Compromised OAuth Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector stated in title: 'Abuses OAuth to Access Gmail via Google API.' Pipeline missed detection for elevated Gmail API calls (GetMessage, ListMessages, SendAs, CreateDraft) from atypical user agents, IPs, or post-token-grant anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Gmail API calls with broad message-access scopes originating from non-corporate IP ASNs, custom user-agents (curl, Python, JavaScript), or within 6 hours of a new OAuth grant. Alert on >50 message downloads per session or rapid cross-folder enumeration (Inbox → All Mail → Archive).

suggestion.title: OAuth Phishing Consent Grants from Untrusted Applications
suggestion.rationale: Campaign leverages OAuth abuse; pipeline lacks detection for phishing-driven consent flows. Article implies initial compromise via ToddyCat phishing leading to OAuth permission grant on fake screens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OAuth application consent audit events where the app is newly registered (<7 days), requests gmail.* or calendar.* scopes, or is granted by multiple users in short window. Correlate with email URLs pointing to phishing sites or OAuth redirect URIs to non-standard domains.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Exfiltration via Google Workspace APIs
suggestion.rationale: OAuth abuse endpoint is Gmail access; expected exfiltration is large-scale email retrieval. Article title 'Access Gmail' implies data exfiltration as kill-chain objective, yet no detection for batch-download patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GetMessage/ListMessages API requests retrieving >100 messages in single session, accessing archives/all-mail folders with broad date ranges (e.g., last 3 years), or executing from service-account-like identities. Baseline per-user API quota and flag 10x+ increase.

suggestion.title: ToddyCat Phishing Campaign Leading to Malware Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly links to ToddyCat APT; initial compromise vector (phishing + Umbrij malware delivery) is absent from pipeline. Expected email-based IOCs, malware hashes, and attack infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails with sender-spoofing of Google/Microsoft domains, hosting malware attachments (Umbrij samples if hashes available), or linking to credential-harvesting pages. Alert on bulk campaigns where recipients subsequently grant OAuth permissions within 2–6 hours of email click.

suggestion.title: Umbrij Malware Process Execution and C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Malware name (Umbrij) is primary attack vector; zero detection for malware execution, persistence mechanisms, or command-and-control callbacks. Expected process signatures, registry artifacts, or network IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Umbrij-attributed process execution (known hashes or behavioral signatures: script interpreters spawning OAuth-related processes, browser injection, credential-store access). Alert on network connections to known Umbrij C2 infrastructure or callback patterns (POST requests to phishing domains post-infection).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'path traversal vulnerability' as the attack vector; web-server logs will show `../` or URL-encoded traversal patterns (e.g., `%2e%2e%2f`) targeting ColdFusion directories. Article phrase: 'contains a path traversal vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion-hosting web servers for HTTP requests containing path traversal sequences (`../`, `..\`, `%2e%2e`, URL-encoded variants). Alert on requests targeting system files or out-of-application-root paths, especially against known ColdFusion application directories.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'; implies spawning of new processes or shell commands after successful path traversal. Article phrase: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, jrun.exe variants) with suspicious parent-child relationships, command-line arguments containing shell escapes, or execution of cmd.exe / powershell.exe from ColdFusion contexts.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Web Application Log Analysis for Traversal Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Path-traversal attacks often leave detectable patterns in ColdFusion application logs (access.log, coldfusion.log); look for repeated 404s, 403s, or 500s on traversal patterns. Article phrase: 'path traversal vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse ColdFusion application and access logs for HTTP status codes 403/404/500 clustered on requests with `../` or `%2e%2e` sequences. Correlate with timestamps of process-creation anomalies to identify successful exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File System Access from ColdFusion Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Successful path traversal allows reading/writing files outside intended application scope; file-access auditing will show ColdFusion accessing system files or configuration directories. Article phrase: 'arbitrary code execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-access events from ColdFusion processes (cfusion.exe) targeting system directories (/etc, /var, /Windows/System32, /Windows/Temp). Alert on reads of configuration files, writes to executable directories, or access to sensitive files outside the web-root.

suggestion.title: Network Connection Anomalies from ColdFusion Process
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attackers may establish outbound connections for C2 or data exfil from the compromised ColdFusion runtime. Article states 'arbitrary code execution'—implying potential for second-stage payload retrieval.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual outbound connections initiated by ColdFusion processes to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains, especially over ports 443, 80, or high-numbered ephemeral ports not typical for application runtime behavior.

suggestion.title: Nuclio cron trigger definition contains shell metacharacters in event.headers keys or body
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Two fields in the trigger specification flow into this string without adequate sanitization: event.headers keys — interpolated verbatim inside double-quoted --header arguments'. Detection should hunt for cron trigger configurations containing shell injection payloads (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons) in header/body fields before they are deployed.
log_sources: AuditLogs (Kubernetes API), Nuclio API call logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nuclio CronJob creation/update API calls for header or body fields containing shell metacharacters: backticks, $(, ;, |, &, newlines, or quote escaping attempts. Flag if caller is non-admin or has anomalous API patterns.

suggestion.title: Nuclio controller spawns shell with unsanitized user-supplied event data
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the root cause: 'Nuclio controller builds a curl invocation string for each cron trigger and stores it as the args of a Kubernetes CronJob container (/bin/sh, -c, <command>)'. This is execution of the payload—detect when controller process spawns /bin/sh with crafted curl arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Nuclio controller process (or CronJob pod runtime) spawning /bin/sh or /bin/bash with process arguments containing both 'curl' and unescaped shell metacharacters ($(, backtick, unquoted variable expansion). Correlate with prior CronJob creation/update.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes CronJob scheduling persistence via Nuclio malicious trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates persistence mechanism: the injected shell command is stored in a CronJob, which runs repeatedly on schedule. This is K8s-native persistence distinct from traditional cron. Detect recurring scheduled execution of the payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track CronJob creation associated with Nuclio controller; monitor for successful execution of CronJobs with command arguments matching injection patterns. Flag if CronJob schedules execution of curl with bearer tokens or /var/run/secrets access.

suggestion.title: Serviceaccount token read from mounted K8s secret store within shell injection payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states injected curl --header arguments reference: '/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token'. This is the credential-access phase where the compromised pod reads the default serviceaccount token. Detection must distinguish between legitimate token use and theft within an injected context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell process (sh, bash, curl subprocesses) reading /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token within a context initiated by a Nuclio CronJob. Correlate with unsanitized header field definition in the trigger spec.

suggestion.title: Serviceaccount token exfiltrated to external IP via curl invoked from CronJob
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exfiltration: injected curl command includes --header with Bearer token and reaches external host. This is both the actions-on-objectives phase and exfiltration. Must correlate CronJob-initiated process with network egress carrying credential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on curl or wget executed from a Kubernetes pod (especially CronJob runtime) with command-line arguments containing Authorization header or Bearer token, connecting to non-RFC1918 IP or known C2 domains. Correlate with prior malicious CronJob creation.

suggestion.title: Nuclio controller API accepts unsanitized cron trigger with shell metacharacters in headers/body
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: controller accepts trigger specification without validating header keys or body fields. Pre-exploitation signal: detect when Nuclio API is called with injection payloads in trigger configuration before CronJob deployment. Earlier in kill chain than post-execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Nuclio API requests (PUT/POST to /triggers or /functions) with body/header fields containing shell metacharacters, variable expansion syntax, or command substitution. Flag if request succeeds (HTTP 200/201) and subsequent CronJob is created with matching payload.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-42009 XSS Exploitation Triggering JavaScript Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Opening the email in a vulnerable Roundcube webmail client triggers exploitation of a cross-site scripting flaw tracked as CVE-2024-42009, which executes JavaScript code inside the victim's browser, loading a payload called IceCube.' Direct execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Roundcube with script-injection payloads in GET/POST parameters, or DOM mutation events within Roundcube's trusted context. Monitor for JavaScript eval() or Function() calls originating from untrusted email content within the webmail process.

suggestion.title: IceCube Stealer: Credential & Session Token Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'IceCube is a fully-featured Roundcube stealer that can harvest usernames, passwords, cookies, two-factor authentication (2FA) data, and browser information.' Malware-specific behavioral signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Roundcube-spawned processes accessing credential storage files (.sqlite, session dirs) or reading browser cookie/localStorage APIs. Detect exfiltration of authentication tokens, session cookies, or backup 2FA codes via unexpected network connections from mail server processes.

suggestion.title: SquareShell PHP Webshell Placement & RCE Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attempts to install SquareShell, a PHP webshell that includes remote code execution capabilities. If successful, the attacker gains remote code execution on the mail server.' Primary persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new PHP file creation in Roundcube web directories (webroot, cache, temp) with web shell patterns (eval, system, passthru, exec functions). Monitor HTTP POST requests to newly created .php files or unusual HTTP methods on Roundcube paths post-compromise.

suggestion.title: VShell Go Backdoor: C2 Beaconing & Port Forwarding
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'VShell is a commodity Go-based backdoor that supports interactive shell access and port forwarding, which is commonly used by Chinese threat actors.' Secondary fallback persistence post-RCE failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Go-compiled binaries on mail servers with suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, /bin/sh). Detect outbound connections to infrastructure overlapping known China-linked VPS ranges. Flag port forwarding via netstat/ss changes or suspicious listening sockets on mail server.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-49113 Deserialization RCE via Roundcube Helpers
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'uses helpers to exploit a Roundcube deserialization flaw tracked as CVE-2025-49113' as the mechanism to invoke SquareShell. Separate exploitation vector requiring distinct detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Roundcube HTTP requests for serialized PHP object payloads in parameters. Alert on unserialize() calls with attacker-controlled data, or exceptions during object reconstruction. Flag HTTP 500 errors on Roundcube pre-patch versions with known gadget chains.

suggestion.title: Targeted Phishing to Academic Physics/National Security Research
suggestion.rationale: Article states campaign 'focuses on physics and engineering departments, administrators and professors, as well as organizations involved in astrophysics, particle physics, or national security-related research' and begins with 'malicious email sent from compromised accounts or spoofed domains.' Targeting-specific initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound emails to physics/engineering/national security research departments from newly compromised external accounts or domains with spoofed university infrastructure. Alert on generic email lures targeting credential theft or link clicks with unusual sender reputation or TLS anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthorized cloud infrastructure modifications
suggestion.rationale: SFI aims to 'proactively harden cloud'—article likely describes infrastructure-as-code checks, auto-remediation, or continuous hardening. Would need detection for config drift or policy violations: 'how-sfi-proactively-hardens-our-cloud' implies logging hardening attempts/rejections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modification or deletion of cloud hardening policies, security group rules, or infrastructure templates outside approved change windows. Correlate with failed compliance scans or auto-remediation rollbacks.

suggestion.title: Detect configuration drift on hardened cloud resources
suggestion.rationale: If article discusses continuous hardening validation, pipeline should extract use cases for detecting when hardening is bypassed or undone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag resources with security baseline violations (e.g., public ACLs, disabled logging, removed encryption) within 24h of hardening deployment. Look for patterns consistent with admin credentials being compromised post-hardening.

suggestion.title: UniFi Authentication Bypass or Privilege Escalation Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'critical flaws' across UniFi authentication products (Connect, Talk, Access). Without full body, cannot determine exact CVEs, but critical severity + multi-product scope suggests privilege escalation or auth bypass as primary attack vector. Missing any detection hypothesis for credential compromise or unauthorized access to UniFi admin interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UniFi admin authentication logs for failed logins followed by successful logins from anomalous source IPs, or direct API calls to /api/login endpoints with unusual payloads. Flag rapid escalation of user privileges in UniFi OS or unexpected RBAC changes post-login.

suggestion.title: UniFi Remote Code Execution via Network API
suggestion.rationale: Critical patches for UniFi OS and multiple network control products strongly suggest RCE vulnerabilities. Pipeline missed exploitation signature: 'Critical flaws' implies remote unauthenticated or low-privilege RCE is plausible. No detection use case generated for command injection or binary execution on compromised controllers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UniFi processes (unifi, ubnt-systool, unifi-java) for unexpected child process spawning (bash, curl, wget, python). Alert on API requests to /api or /manage endpoints with shell metacharacters, base64-encoded payloads, or known UniFi RCE exploit signatures. Flag unusual outbound connections from UniFi controller ports (8080, 8443, 6789).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable UniFi Product Version Detection & Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article lists five product lines requiring patches. Pipeline extracted zero version indicators, CVE numbers, or patch-level IOCs. Organizations cannot create detection rules or asset inventory queries without knowing specific vulnerable versions (e.g., UniFi Access < 7.0.x, UniFi OS < 3.x).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate device inventory (Nessus, Qualys, asset database) against known vulnerable UniFi versions listed in Ubiquiti advisory. Generate alerts for any controller, gateway, or switch running UniFi software with version < [patch threshold]. Capture HTTP User-Agent headers from UniFi web console access to fingerprint software version.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from Compromised UniFi Controller
suggestion.rationale: If critical RCE flaws exist in UniFi OS (the article's explicit mention), compromised controllers become pivot points. Pipeline did not generate detection for lateral movement to managed APs, switches, or other network infrastructure. Article's scope ('across... OS') implies infrastructure-wide compromise risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSH/SSH2 protocol traffic from UniFi controller IPs to managed devices (APs, switches, gateways). Alert on unexpected administrative connections using default or compromised service accounts. Flag anomalous volume or frequency of inter-device API calls or firmware update requests originating from a single controller.

suggestion.title: UniFi Protect/Access Surveillance Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: UniFi Protect (video surveillance) and Access (physical access control) products mentioned; critical flaws may enable bulk export of footage, face-recognition databases, or access logs. Pipeline missed detection for unauthorized data collection from these high-value security systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor UniFi Protect API calls (e.g., /api/bootstrap, /api/recording/export) for bulk video export requests or high-volume data reads outside business hours. Alert on UniFi Access API calls querying cardholder data, biometric records, or access logs with unusual result set sizes or patterns. Track large outbound connections from Protect/Access appliances to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Detection of Ubiquiti Advisory Scanning & Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Before exploitation, attackers scan for vulnerable UniFi instances. Pipeline did not generate hunt for Shodan/Censys queries, SSL certificate fingerprinting, or HTTP banner grabs targeting UniFi default ports (8080, 8443, 6789, 10001). Article does not specify if reconnaissance activity is documented, but SOC should hunt retroactively.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for external connections to Ubiquiti default management ports from non-enterprise ASNs. Alert on HTTP GET requests to /login, /manage, or /.version endpoints that complete without credential submission or with scanner User-Agents (nmap, Shodan, masscan). Correlate with historical scans to identify newly-compromised instances in vulnerable version range.

suggestion.title: High-volume unauthenticated document enumeration via /api/documents/search-content
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upload arbitrary content into mem...' and ability to read, implying reconnaissance. Detection should hunt mass-retrieval patterns: 'An unauthenticated remote attacker can ... read' memory content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: A single source issuing >50 GET requests to /api/documents/search-content or /api/documents/* endpoints in <5m with consistent 200 responses, with no prior auth attempts, suggests bulk data exfiltration. Baseline legitimate query volume first.

suggestion.title: Batch upload of suspicious content via /api/documents/batch-upload without authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'upload arbitrary content': 'An unauthenticated remote attacker can upload arbitrary content into the mem…'. No threshold-based hunt exists for mass injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/documents/batch-upload with 200 status from unauthenticated sources (no prior auth attempt in session). Flag if >1000 bytes uploaded in single request or >10 requests from same src in 10m window. Correlate with downstream /api/documents/search-content reads.

suggestion.title: Rapid unauthenticated document deletion cascade via /api/documents/remove*
suggestion.rationale: T1485 (Data Destruction) listed, but UC_100_5 lacks temporal correlation. Article impact includes 'Data Destruction' and ability to 'remove' documents — should detect coordinated delete patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DELETE requests to /api/documents/remove* or /api/documents/remove-by-tags returning 200, where the same source has zero prior successful GET/POST to /api/documents within 24h (no legitimate access pattern). Flag if deletion rate >10/min.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Synthetic Identity Creation via Public Photos
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes that public Instagram photos are now accessible to Meta's AI image tool ('lets others use your public Instagram photos'). Adversaries could exploit this to generate synthetic identities with AI-photorealistic faces for credential stuffing, social engineering, or account takeover. Pipeline missed potential credential access / initial access implications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for login attempts using profile pictures recently scraped from public social media. Correlate failed authentication bursts against newly created or modified user profiles with AI-generated or single-image galleries. Alert on phishing campaigns with images that match the composition/style of Instagram public content.

suggestion.title: AI Security Tool Executing Unexpected Code
suggestion.rationale: Article title states AI agents 'built to catch malicious code can be tricked into running it'—direct evidence that these tools execute code when manipulated. Pipeline missed detection for abnormal execution by security tools themselves.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for code execution initiated by or under the context of AI-based security/detection tools (parent process = analysis engine, YARA scanner, ML-based classifier, etc.). Flag execution of code marked as malicious or unknown to the initiating tool. Establish baseline of normal tool behavior; alert on unexpected payload execution or shell spawning from security agent processes.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection or Input Manipulation to Security Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes AI agents being 'tricked'—implying manipulation via input/prompt injection. Pipeline did not surface detection for adversarial inputs designed to bypass AI-based controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inputs to AI/ML-based security tools that contain obfuscation, encoding, or semantic tricks designed to evade analysis (nested payloads, mixed-encoding samples, adversarial prompts). Flag inputs that precede tool failure, miscategorization, or unexpected execution by the tool.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Compromised or Manipulated Security Tooling
suggestion.rationale: Core article premise: attackers exploit detection tools themselves to run malicious code. This is a defense-evasion technique (T1548, T1548.004). Pipeline reconstruction missed this phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of privileged operations and code execution from known security tools (Yara, antivirus engines, SIEM agents, EDR scanners). Alert on deviation: unexpected API calls, file system access, or network connections by security tools. Cross-correlate: did a security tool trigger on a sample, then execute that sample or derived code?

suggestion.title: Anomalous Behavior from Deployed AI Detection Models
suggestion.rationale: Article implies AI agents themselves are being exploited. Detection should monitor for behavioral anomalies in deployed ML/AI systems used for security. Not addressed in empty pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ML-based security tools for sudden classification reversals (samples marked safe that were previously detected), confidence score anomalies, or misclassification patterns. Track inputs that trigger model execution; flag statistically improbable input sequences designed to manipulate model output.

suggestion.title: Repository Symlink Creation in AI Tooling Context
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Symlink Flaws Could Let Malicious Repos Run Code in AI Coding Agents' — pipeline missed the core attack: symlinks planted in cloned repositories. Should detect symlink creation during repo checkout or processing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symlink (mklink, ln -s) creation or resolution in recently-cloned repository directories, especially those processed by code-analysis or AI tooling. Flag symlinks resolving to system paths (/etc, /proc, C:\Windows) or parent-directory traversal.

suggestion.title: Process Execution Through Symlink-Resolved Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article describes code execution triggered by malicious symlinks — pipeline should detect processes spawned with parent/image paths that resolve through symlinks to unexpected destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where command-line or image path contains or resolves through a symlink, combined with repository-checkout artifacts or unexpected working directory. Cross-correlate with AI coding agent processes (Claude, Cursor, Copilot extensions).

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Code Execution via Repository Artifact Symlinks

This runtime trigger is key to detection. 'Once those functions are called, the malware captures the full mnemonic seed phrase and private key.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js runtime for Injective SDK function calls (generateWallet, importPrivateKey, getMnemonic) followed within milliseconds by credential data (regex: mnemonic phrases 12-24 words, private keys hex format) being read from memory or process handles. Correlate with HTTP exfiltration events to flag as malware activation.

suggestion.title: Detect transitive dependency chain injection of compromised npm packages
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights cascading supply-chain exposure: 'The package has 87 direct dependencies on npm and very likely multiple additional transitive dependencies. A report from Ox Security warns that the 87 dependent packages had a cumulative download count of a little over 112,000.' Downstream packages inherit the malware without direct installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze dependency trees for any package that directly or transitively requires @injectivelabs/sdk-ts v1.20.21. Flag projects using any of the 87 direct dependents (or their consumers) as potentially compromised even if they did not explicitly install the malicious SDK. Cross-reference with npm audit and lockfile package versions.

suggestion.title: Detect deprecated but still-available malicious npm package artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes incomplete remediation: 'Socket says the malicious version of the package was downloaded 310 times before it was deprecated, not removed, and the malicious GitHub release artifacts are still available.' This allows continued exploitation post-disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for packages marked 'deprecated' but still downloadable, and correlate with historical malicious version numbers. Alert on npm install attempts of deprecated malicious versions or on cached installs from old lockfiles. Scan GitHub releases for artifacts still hosted after version revert/revoke.

suggestion.title: Ruckus/ASUS Router Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states UAT-7810 'exploits known vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers' to deploy LONGLEASH/DOGLEASH. Pipeline extracted no initial-access signals despite defenders being told 'ensure all edge devices, particularly Ruckus and ASUS routers, are fully patched.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to Ruckus (22.3.x, 22.2.x, etc.) and ASUS router admin panels containing known exploitation payloads or unusual binary uploads. Correlate with failed SSH/Telnet attempts. Baseline: legitimate firmware update traffic from known admin IPs.

suggestion.title: LONGLEASH/DOGLEASH Backdoor Deployment and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'upgraded LONGLEASH and DOGLEASH backdoors' as the primary persistence mechanism. No detection use case generated. Article states tools are 'multi-platform'—need file-based and network-based signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LONGLEASH/DOGLEASH file writes to /etc or /usr/sbin on Linux; detect process execution spawning outbound TLS connections to non-whitelisted C2 ranges from router processes. Signature: custom malware exhibiting multi-platform binary format (ELF, Mach-O, PE). Note: article states tools are 'sophisticated' and 'highly resilient'—expect encryption and evasion.

suggestion.title: ORB Network Detection via Proxy Chain Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Core attack infrastructure: 'ORB networks create a massive blind spot... allow secondary threat actors to mask their origins and route malicious traffic through seemingly innocuous nodes.' Article specifically states 'Monitor network traffic for unusual proxying behavior or unauthorized connections on devices that typically lack complex services.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify relay patterns: router → router → external. Detect CONNECT tunneling or SOCKS proxy traffic on TCP/443 from devices (Ruckus, ASUS) that never historically initiated outbound proxying. Cross-reference destination IPs against secondary compromised devices in same network. Expected: decentralized, low-volume C2 to evade perimeter sensors.

suggestion.title: UAT-7810 Infrastructure Reconnaissance and Build-Out
suggestion.rationale: Article states UAT-7810 'builds these covert networks to provide infrastructure for other APT groups to launch attacks.' This is infrastructure-as-a-service reconnaissance—requires detection of reconnaissance queries, domain registrations, and IP assignments tied to ORB nodes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk registrations of new domains resolving to router-class IP ranges (RFC 1918 + edge-facing IPs). Detect ASN/BGP changes for known UAT-7810 infrastructure. Correlate with historical C2 sinkhole/takedown data to identify resurrected infrastructure.

Flag registry Run/RunOnce key modifications in HKLM and HKCU. Detect WMI event consumer subscriptions and startup folder modifications by non-admin processes.

Flag execution of sc.exe/net.exe to stop security services (WinDefend, MsSense, MsMpEngine). Monitor for deletion of event logs or tampering with audit policies.

suggestion.title: CrownX Ransomware Note Deployment

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP Path Traversal Sequences Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability'; exploitation involves HTTP request sequences containing directory traversal patterns (./, ../, URL-encoded variants) targeting ColdFusion endpoints before code execution occurs.

Correlate with 400-series responses. Alert on repeated traversal attempts to same endpoint within short window.

suggestion.title: Detect ColdFusion Child Process Creation (Code Execution Indicator)

Baseline normal ColdFusion child processes; alert on anomalies. Correlate with preceding HTTP path traversal attempts in same time window (±5min).

suggestion.title: Inventory Internet-Facing ColdFusion Applications

Cross-reference against internal asset registry to find shadow IT. Prioritize for patching if unpatched CVE-2026-48282.

suggestion.title: Detect ColdFusion Application Exception Log Spikes (Exploitation Scanning Indicator)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion exception logs for spikes in file-access-related errors, path resolution failures, or security exceptions. Establish baseline; alert on 3×+ increase within 1-hour window. Cross-correlate with HTTP error response spikes to validate exploitation scanning activity.

suggestion.title: Detect Outbound Network Activity from ColdFusion After Code Execution

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline outbound connections from ColdFusion application user/process (destination IPs, ports, protocols). Alert on anomalies: connections to non-standard ports, external C2 infrastructure, or known-malicious IPs within 10 minutes of detected path traversal or process creation anomalies. Flag high-volume data transfer.
