suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Scanner Positive
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with explicit CVE and federal patch due TODAY (2026-07-10). No detection use case for scanner integration despite standard practice. Article: 'CVE-2026-48282' with federal urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CVE-2026-48282 matches in ColdFusion inventory. Rank by CVSS and CISA KEV status. Verify patch dates against due date. Escalate any positive findings with active network exposure.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion RCE Process Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploits to arbitrary code execution. No detection for post-exploitation process spawning. Article: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline ColdFusion process tree (w3wp.exe, java.exe). Alert on anomalous child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32, certutil, etc.) spawned from ColdFusion workers. Exclude administrative service restarts. Correlate with time-of-day (off-hours execution).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerable ColdFusion Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'patch lag is the silent killer' and mandates inventory check against Federal due date 2026-07-10. Requires immediate asset discovery and version validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and CMDB for Adobe ColdFusion instances. Cross-reference version/build metadata against patched release dates for CVE-2026-48282. Flag unpatched systems or those past Federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'path traversal vulnerability'—detection must monitor for directory traversal attack patterns in ColdFusion web requests, per common exploitation vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search ColdFusion URIs and parameters for path traversal indicators (../, ..\, %2e%2e/, unicode variants). Alert on sequences attempting to escape restricted directories or access system files outside intended scope.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution from ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—exploitation success triggers process execution that must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process creation spawned by ColdFusion service processes (java.exe, jrun.exe) launching cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or shell interpreters. Alert on abnormal file writes to ColdFusion directories or suspicious registry modifications.

suggestion.title: Externally-Accessible ColdFusion Service Detection
suggestion.rationale: T1190 ('Exploit Public-Facing Application') implies external attack surface. KEV entry notes active exploitation—requires network visibility into exposed ColdFusion endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for externally-routable ColdFusion services (port 8500, 8501, .cfm/.cfc endpoints). Correlate with vulnerability scanner to confirm unpatched CVE-2026-48282 exposure. Alert on external connection attempts post-publication.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Patch Compliance Deadline Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Federal due date explicitly stated as '2026-07-10' in article. Non-compliance is audit-relevant and escalatable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated daily check: compare current date against Federal patch due date (2026-07-10). Query asset inventory for unpatched ColdFusion instances. Generate escalation if any remain unpatched within 7 days of deadline.

suggestion.title: Adobe ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 Asset Inventory Check
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'path traversal vulnerability' on ColdFusion with a federal due date of 2026-07-10 and emphasizes that even patched assets should be verified. No UC for asset discovery or patch-compliance checks against this specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for ColdFusion instances matching CVE-2026-48282. Flag any unpatched or remediation-pending assets given the federal due date.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution' as the attack vector. No UC to detect traversal attempts in HTTP logs or WAF telemetry against ColdFusion endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for path traversal payloads (../, %2e%2e, backslash escapes) in HTTP requests to ColdFusion URI patterns (*.cfm, *.cfc endpoints). Correlate with known-vulnerable ColdFusion versions and external source IPs.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact as 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user' but no UC to detect post-exploitation execution of commands or scripts via ColdFusion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion logs for abnormal cfexecute or cfscript directives spawning child processes. Cross-reference with path traversal attempts in the same timeframe to establish exploit-to-execution correlation.

suggestion.title: Federated Patch Due Date Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal due date of 2026-07-10 and states 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors.' No UC to track remediation against deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish a compliance report tracking CVE-2026-48282 remediation status across all ColdFusion assets. Alert on assets still unpatched as the due date approaches.

suggestion.title: BusySnake Stealer Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'BusySnake Stealer' as the payload. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite this being the core attack tool.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BusySnake execution patterns: suspicious process spawns with stealer-typical behaviors (registry access to credential stores, LSASS injection attempts, browser process enumeration). Look for process names or command lines matching known BusySnake indicators.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Information Stealer
suggestion.rationale: 'BusySnake Stealer' designation indicates credential access mission; article targets government/power (high-value secrets). No use case for stealer-pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect stealer behaviors: enumeration of browser data directories (AppData\Local\Google\Chrome, AppData\Local\Microsoft\Edge), access to SAM/SECURITY hives, LSASS memory reads, or bulk file access to password manager databases.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Stealer Payload
suggestion.rationale: Stealers require command-and-control exfiltration. Article omits C2 indicators, but pipeline should have flagged exfiltration use case as mandatory for stealer attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious outbound connections post-stealer execution: non-standard ports, newly-registered/low-reputation domains, large data transfers to external IPs, or HTTPS traffic to infrastructure not matching user browsing patterns.

suggestion.title: Armored Likho Campaign Delivery (Initial Access)
suggestion.rationale: Article names Armored Likho as actor; no initial access detection (phishing, watering hole, supply chain). Pipeline should have reconstructed attack flow from intro.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate recent phishing/soceng campaigns targeting government/energy verticals with downstream BusySnake detection. Look for low-reputation URLs in emails to those sectors, especially with lures around infrastructure/regulatory topics.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Stealer Anti-Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated stealer malware (especially 'Armored' actor campaigns) typically employ anti-analysis, sandbox evasion, or injection. No evasion techniques surfaced by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for obfuscation indicators: code caves, unusual PE section names, reflective DLL injection, or API hooking attempts. Flag parent-child anomalies (e.g., system process spawning svchost with suspicious module loads).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-48282 and CISA KEV lists only exploited-in-the-wild CVEs. 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet' establishes the need for scanner-based inventory control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for systems flagged CVE-2026-48282 or running unpatched Adobe ColdFusion. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify exposed instances. Alert on any match, even if marked 'remediated' — patch lag is the killer here.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Attempts (Web Access Logs)
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Must detect attempts to traverse ColdFusion directories before exploitation succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search web server and WAF logs for HTTP requests targeting ColdFusion paths with ../ sequences, URL-encoded traversal (e.g., %2e%2e), or common ColdFusion admin paths (cfadmin, CFIDE). High-confidence if request succeeds (HTTP 200) and logs show unusual file access.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution in ColdFusion Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Path traversal that reaches successful execution. Must detect when ColdFusion spawns child processes or loads/executes external binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous process creation under ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, java.exe if using Lucee). Flag unexpected child processes, especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or scripts spawned from web-accessible paths. Correlate timing with path-traversal web attempts.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Due Date Risk: CVE-2026-48282 (2026-07-10)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10. Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors / regulators.' Compliance/risk reporting required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track patch status of CVE-2026-48282 against 2026-07-10 deadline. Flag any systems still unpatched as of due date. Generate compliance report for audit trail. This is both a technical and regulatory gap.

suggestion.title: Detect Ransomware Encryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on BlackCat ransomware attacks causing 'encryption' of victim systems; pipeline failed to map T1486 or suggest detection for bulk file encryption patterns characteristic of ransomware impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes performing high-volume file modifications with encryption-like signatures (rapid writes to .lock, .encrypted, or ransom-note-named files; correlate with parent process indicative of ransomware families like BlackCat variants).

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Harvesting Prior to Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: BlackCat attacks described in prosecution articles typically involve credential theft (T1087, T1555, T1111) to move laterally; no detection logic for discovery or credential-access phases was surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of credential-dumping tools (mimikatz, ProcDump, procdump.exe with lsass target, or living-off-the-land binary misuse like reg query HKLM\\SAM) or suspicious LSASS access prior to remote execution.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement via Remote Services
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware prosecution articles implicate lateral movement to propagate encryption; pipeline did not suggest detection for T1021 variants or suspicious RDP/PsExec/WMI usage typical of BlackCat post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious execution of psexec.exe, mstsc.exe with unusual parent processes, WMI command-line invocations, or RDP traffic to internal IP ranges from single sources targeting multiple hosts in short timeframes.

suggestion.title: Detect Data Exfiltration to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: BlackCat employs double-extortion tactics (article context implies data theft prior to encryption); pipeline did not suggest use cases for T1041 or detection of exfiltration to attacker-controlled infrastructure or cloud staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate large data transfers (>500 MB in short window) to external IPs or known attacker-operated storage/C2 domains with file access patterns preceding encryption; flag Rclone, 7zip, WinRAR spawned alongside network egress.

suggestion.title: Detect Command-Line Execution by Ransomware Processes
suggestion.rationale: BlackCat and similar RaaS variants spawn cmd.exe or PowerShell for lateral movement, data enumeration, and system reconnaissance (T1059.001, T1059.003); pipeline produced no detections for this execution phase activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned from suspicious parents (explorer.exe, winword.exe, chrome.exe, or unknown binaries) with command-line arguments targeting AD discovery (net group, dsquery), file enumeration, or disabling defenses (Defender exclusions, firewall rules).

suggestion.title: Detect Ransom Note Placement and System Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes criminal facilitation of attacks concluding in ransom extortion; pipeline did not suggest detection for ransom-note file creation or Windows startup/wallpaper modification typical of ransomware post-encryption taunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of .txt, .html, or .bmp files named with common ransom-note patterns (RECOVERY_KEY, DECRYPT_ME, etc.) in user home directories, or modification of registry keys for wallpaper/startup programs combined with file encryption indicators.

suggestion.title: Authenticated session + BazaR exploit within time window
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Authenticated PHP Object Injection.' Pipeline should correlate successful login events to the target system with subsequent POST /BazaR requests within minutes, establishing authentication-to-exploitation chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful authentication events (login, session creation) to the YesWiki application with POST requests to /BazaR/vue=importer within a 5-10 minute window. Alert on authenticated accounts performing exploit-phase activity outside normal user behavior windows.

suggestion.title: Base64-encoded serialized PHP object in HTTP POST body
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack uses 'base64_decode($entry)' and 'unserialize()' on POST parameter importfiche. Pipeline should detect base64 strings matching PHP serialization grammar ('O:' or 'Tzo' base64 prefixes) in POST bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to YesWiki endpoints for parameters containing base64-encoded strings that decode to PHP serialized object prefixes (Tzo, O:, etc.). Pair with CSVManager.php or importfiche parameter names for high-confidence detection.

suggestion.title: Doctrine gadget chain class instantiation in error logs
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Doctrine RCE1 gadget outcome.' PHP object injection exploitation via specific Doctrine versions typically triggers __destruct/__wakeup methods that log class name errors (e.g., 'Object of class Doctrine\ORM\... could not be converted').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search PHP error logs for attempts to instantiate or convert Doctrine ORM classes (Doctrine\ORM, Doctrine\Common, etc.) in contexts outside normal ORM initialization. Look for __destruct/__wakeup method invocation logs or 'could not be converted to string' errors mentioning Doctrine classes.

suggestion.title: YesWiki config file wakka.config.php modification by non-root account
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies wakka.config.php as post-exploitation persistence target. Web-server processes (php-fpm, apache) should never modify this file during normal operation; modifications indicate successful RCE and persistence attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file modifications to wakka.config.php initiated by php-fpm, apache, nginx, or web-server user accounts. Exclude legitimate system updates. Correlate with POST /BazaR requests from the previous 30 minutes for high-fidelity persistence detection.

suggestion.title: YesWiki unauthenticated request followed by authenticated exploit attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article requires authentication but does not describe whether attackers enumerate or test valid accounts first. Detection should look for failed login attempts followed by successful authenticated POST to BazaR exploit endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequences: (1) failed authentication attempts to YesWiki within 15-minute window, followed by (2) successful login, followed by (3) POST /BazaR/vue=importer within 5 minutes. Indicates credential stuffing or compromise before exploitation.

suggestion.title: web.xml / Apache reverse proxy logging of BazaR import endpoint access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes POST to /BazaR/vue=importer endpoint. Organizations running YesWiki behind reverse proxies (nginx, Apache) may log endpoint requests differently. Detection should account for proxy-layer logging patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In reverse proxy (nginx/Apache mod_proxy) logs, look for POST requests to paths matching /bazar, /BazaR, or /tools/bazar with vue=importer parameters. May be logged as encoded URLs (/bazar%2Fimport or similar). Correlate with backend PHP error logs for __destruct/__wakeup failures.

suggestion.title: YesWiki authorization bypass: write-only user invoking unrestricted delete action (CVE-2026-52766)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'no authorization check anywhere in the action body or in the page-deletion path'—the exploit is privilege escalation via action invocation without delete ACL. Missing UC to detect users with write-only permission triggering delete operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate identity/access-management logs showing user assigned write-only role with subsequent POST to erasespamedcomments action targeting pages where user lacks delete permission. Flag if user's ACL lacks delete privilege but action succeeds (HTTP 200/204).

suggestion.title: YesWiki bulk page deletion impact: mass 404 spike post-exploitation (CVE-2026-52766)
suggestion.rationale: Article states action 'deletes every wiki page whose tag appears in that array'—aftermath is accessible pages becoming inaccessible. Missing impact detection via 404/access-denial spike correlating to suppr[] array contents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden spike in HTTP 404 responses for wiki page GET requests within 5–15 minutes after POST to erasespamedcomments. Correlate deleted page names against subsequent 404 targets. Alert if 404 count exceeds baseline+3σ.

suggestion.title: YesWiki ACL misconfiguration: erasespamedcomments accessible to unauthenticated or write-only users
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause as 'allow-by-default action ACL model'—action should require delete permission but does not. Missing configuration audit to detect overly-permissive action ACL grants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query YesWiki action ACL for erasespamedcomments: flag if execute permission granted to 'all users', 'authenticated', or roles explicitly lacking delete ACL. Compare against approved baseline; alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: YesWiki suspicious write-permission grant preceding delete action (CVE-2026-52766 pre-exploitation indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation often follows rapid permission escalation. Missing detection for write-access grant immediately preceding action invocation—may indicate account compromise or misconfiguration discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequence: (1) user assigned write permission to YesWiki pages, then (2) same user POSTs to erasespamedcomments within <5 minutes. Flag if permission grant originated from unexpected admin or failed auth attempts preceded it.

suggestion.title: YesWiki suppr[] array size anomaly: bulk deletion vs single-item cleanup (CVE-2026-52766 behavioral)
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate admin cleanup typically affects 1–3 pages; exploitation abuse exploits bulk deletion. Missing volumetric detection to distinguish normal maintenance from mass-deletion abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract suppr[] array size from POST URI/body. Alert if single request deletes >10 pages or if daily deletion volume by user exceeds historical +3σ baseline. Cluster on user + source IP + deletion count to detect bulk-operation patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation - Injective SDK
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names @injectivelabs/sdk-ts v1.20.21 as malicious with 310 downloads before deprecation. Pipeline failed to generate package-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm installs for @injectivelabs/sdk-ts v1.20.21 or detection of package.json modifications that reference this version. Alert on installation of compromised version within known window (2026-06-08 to 2026-06-XX). Correlate with developer environments and CI/CD pipelines.

suggestion.title: Wallet Credential Exfiltration via SDK Function Call
suggestion.rationale: Article describes precise trigger: 'malware activates when developers use SDK functions that generate or import wallet keys' and captures 'mnemonic seed phrase and private key'. Pipeline missed this behavioral detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of code containing Injective SDK wallet functions (InjectiveWallet generation/import methods). Flag calls to mnemonic or private key functions, especially if followed by base64-encoding operations. Correlate with subsequent HTTP traffic to external endpoints.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST Exfiltration with Base64-Encoded Credentials in Headers
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'encoded the data in base64' and 'sent them' via 'HTTP POST request header' to Injective Labs endpoint, with 2-second queue batching. Pipeline provided no exfiltration detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests from npm package processes (node/npm) to external or infrastructure endpoints containing base64-encoded data in request headers. Flag requests with payloads matching patterns of wallet mnemonics (typically 12–24 space-separated words encoded) or 64-character hex private keys. Alert on batched exfiltration patterns (multiple keys in single POST).

suggestion.title: Compromised GitHub Account Publishing Malicious npm Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker compromised a GitHub account belonging to a legitimate project contributor and made the first suspicious commits on June 8'. Pipeline missed initial-access detection for GitHub account compromise and automated malicious release.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub contributor account activity for anomalies: commits from new IP/device, rapid commit-to-release cycles (hours), publishing to multiple dependent packages simultaneously, and version tags that jump or use unusual patterns. Flag accounts that push directly to main without PR review and immediately trigger CI/CD release pipeline.

suggestion.title: Multi-Package Coordinated Malicious Release
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker also published version 1.20.21 for another 17 packages associated with the project, pinning all of them to the compromised SDK version.' Single-package detection insufficient; needs correlation across dependency tree.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect simultaneous or near-simultaneous (within minutes) publishing of malicious versions across multiple npm packages from same owner/organization. Alert on coordinated version pinning to a common dependency (e.g., 17 packages all pinning to same SDK version in single release batch). Correlate with GitHub commit timestamps.

suggestion.title: Dependency Chain Poison - Transitive Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: '87 direct dependencies on npm and very likely multiple additional transitive dependencies', 'cumulative download count of a little over 112,000'. Pipeline missed transitive compromise scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan installed dependencies for presence of @injectivelabs/sdk-ts v1.20.21 anywhere in dependency tree, not just direct installs. Flag projects with 87+ direct dependencies (high transitive risk) that have installed malicious version. Generate software bill of materials (SBOM) and cross-reference against known-compromised package registry.

suggestion.title: Embedded Device Privilege Escalation via Filesystem Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unpatched flaws' in filesystem bundled into devices—filesystem vulnerabilities are canonical privilege escalation vectors, yet no elevation-detection UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor embedded device processes for direct filesystem syscalls (open, read, write, ioctl) targeting /proc, /sys, or device files from unprivileged context. Flag transitions from low to high privilege after filesystem operations.

suggestion.title: Filesystem Structure Exploitation - Abnormal Inode/Metadata Access
suggestion.rationale: Filesystem flaws often enable direct inode/metadata manipulation; article mentions flaws in 'filesystem' itself, requiring detection of low-level filesystem access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes attempting direct block-device or filesystem metadata access via ioctl, pread, or raw device operations. Alert on writes to filesystem reserved areas or unexpected calls to fsck, mkfs, or partition-manipulation tools.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Embedded Device Inventory Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'millions of embedded devices' ship with vulnerability—pipeline should map affected device OS versions, manufacturers, and product lines to enable inventory correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate embedded device OS/firmware versions against known-vulnerable filesystem builds (once CVEs/vendors identified). Enumerate devices reporting vulnerable filesystem versions via management protocols (SSH banner, SNMP sysDescr, HTTP User-Agent).

suggestion.title: Persistence via Filesystem Boot/Init Vector
suggestion.rationale: Filesystem vulnerabilities in embedded systems often persist across reboot; article's critical severity and embedded-device scope suggest persistent compromise is a threat model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to mount points, fstab, init.d, or systemd-boot configurations on embedded devices. Detect attempts to install or modify filesystem drivers, loadable kernel modules, or bootloader-stage code.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Filesystem Syscall Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Unpatched filesystem flaws in publicly available embedded firmware are immediate RCE targets; article severity 'crit' signals likely remote exploitability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect crash/OOM patterns on embedded devices after network inbound (indicating crash-based exploitation). Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by system daemons or root-owned network services after filesystem-heavy operations.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear T1190 exploitation narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion servers for HTTP requests containing directory traversal patterns (.., encoded variants) in request paths, particularly targeting administrative or file-system resources. Correlate with CVE-2026-48282 scanner alerts.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Remote Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline missed execution-phase detection despite explicit RCE impact in threat description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from ColdFusion runtime (java.exe under cfusion parent) with unexpected command-line arguments, environment changes, or file I/O to sensitive paths post-path-traversal exploitation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' in Recommended hunts section with template substitution for CVE-2026-48282. Pipeline failed to instantiate despite template guidance provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all ColdFusion instances (ports 8500/8501/8000) Internet-accessible. Correlate patch levels against CVE-2026-48282. Flag unpatched instances and cross-reference against scanner silence (patches not applied despite vulnerability awareness).

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Administrator Panel Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploitation typically precedes administrative access attempts. Article mentions execution 'in context of current user,' implying escalation from web context to privileged operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to ColdFusion Administrator paths (/CFIDE/administrator/) for authentication anomalies, failed login sequences preceding path traversal patterns, or access from non-administrative source networks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Correlation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status guarantees active exploitation. Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and recommends 'one quick check across your fleet.' Pipeline should trigger scanner-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline ColdFusion vulnerability scanner submissions for CVE-2026-48282. Flag scanner results showing 'vulnerable' status post-patch-due-date (2026-07-10). Cross-reference with network flow data for exploitation attempts to flagged instances.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Unpatched Adobe ColdFusion (CVE-2026-48282)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unpatched ColdFusion instances exposed to internet; cross-reference asset inventory against CVE-2026-48282 patch status. Flag any systems showing ColdFusion version < [vendor-specified patched version] with network-accessible admin or application ports.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt: ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'path traversal vulnerability' as attack vector; this is a detectable exploitation pattern that pipeline omitted entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints for path traversal payloads (e.g., `../`, `..\`, `%2e%2e`, `....//`); alert on sequences that access sensitive system paths or configuration files outside intended ColdFusion application directories.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Execution: ColdFusion Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user' — RCE is the impact, but pipeline captured no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new process creation or command execution spawned from ColdFusion worker processes (cfusion.exe, coldfusion service account context); especially suspicious if child processes are cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or outbound network tools immediately following exploitation timeframe.

suggestion.title: Adobe ColdFusion Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states this is 'currently being exploited' and requires federal remediation by 2026-07-10. Baseline hunt for ColdFusion web servers (port 8500, HTTP server fingerprints). Article establishes the attack surface explicitly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ColdFusion instances exposed on the network via HTTP banners (Server: Adobe ColdFusion/...), port scanning results, or vulnerability scanner confirmations. Cross-reference against patch inventory to identify unpatched versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation (CVE-2026-48282)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' that 'could lead to arbitrary code execution.' Detect exploitation attempts using directory traversal patterns in HTTP requests to known ColdFusion endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to ColdFusion web roots containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e) or attempts to access sensitive directories (WEB-INF, admin, etc.) that are consistent with CVE-2026-48282 exploitation. Filter for HTTP 200 responses indicating successful path resolution.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Post-Exploitation RCE Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Post-exploit, expect command execution, file write, or process spawn from ColdFusion application processes (cfusion.exe, jrun.exe, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful path-traversal indicators (HTTP 200 to ColdFusion traversal payloads) with subsequent spawning of child processes from ColdFusion application threads (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash). Look for unusual parent-child process relationships where ColdFusion initiates system commands.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Web Shell Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal → code execution likely results in web shell upload to ColdFusion web root. Article does not explicitly mention this, but RCE vulnerability exploitation pattern is well-established.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion web root directories (typically /<COLDFUSION_ROOT>/wwwroot and subfolders) for new file creation or unexpected modification of .cfm, .jsp, .asp files. Correlate with path-traversal HTTP requests. Alert on files with suspicious naming (shell, admin, upload, cmd, etc.) or recently modified binaries/scripts in web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Attempts Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability'—this is the core attack step. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being directly detectable: HTTP requests containing ../, ..\, and URL-encoded variants targeting ColdFusion application paths (e.g., /cfusion/, /CFIDE/).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints (URI patterns matching /cfusion, /CFIDE, /admin) containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e, unicode variants, null bytes). Correlate with ColdFusion process user privileges. Flag any 200-range responses to these patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Access from ColdFusion Process
