suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from ColdFusion.exe or cfusion process (parent PID analysis). Look for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or scripting interpreters as children of the application process.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion configuration audit: patch lag identification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'patch lag is the silent killer' and references federal due-date enforcement logic. Proactive configuration audit of ColdFusion versions required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for ColdFusion installations and version numbers. Cross-reference against vulnerable version ranges for CVE-2026-48282. Flag any system not patched before 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation file access patterns from ColdFusion context
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal exploit success leads to file access outside normal application boundaries. Endpoint telemetry should detect anomalous file access from ColdFusion process context. Article phrase: 'path traversal vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access events originating from ColdFusion process that access parent directories or sensitive paths outside the application root (e.g., Windows\System32, /etc, /var on *nix). Baseline normal application file access first.

suggestion.title: Avalon Malware Framework Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly announces 'Avalon Malware Framework' but pipeline extracted zero execution indicators. Framework naming, process spawning patterns, and command-line artifacts are baseline detections for a novel malware announcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of processes named after or associated with Avalon framework components, script interpreters launching from temporary directories with obfuscated arguments, or parent-child process chains indicative of multi-stage malware execution. Flag unusual scheduling activity (schtasks) or registry Run key modifications contemporaneous with execution.

suggestion.title: CrownX Ransomware Encryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'CrownX Ransomware Capabilities' but zero use cases address the encryption phase. Ransomware data destruction (T1486) is the defining impact and must be detectable via bulk file modification patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume file write operations across multiple directories in short timespan, bulk file extensions changes to suspected ransom marker (e.g., .crownx if used), or writes to system-protected directories. Correlate with shadow copy deletion (vssadmin delete shadows) or WBEM deletion attempts (Win32_ShadowCopy).

suggestion.title: Framework-Driven Lateral Movement & Tool Propagation
suggestion.rationale: As a 'framework,' Avalon implies multi-stage deployment and pivot capability. Article does not detail lateral spread mechanisms but framework architecture demands detection of remote execution and tool transfer across hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMB/RDP outbound connections from initially-compromised assets to other internal hosts, execution of Avalon/CrownX binaries via remote services (WMI, psexec, schtasks /S), or file copies to administrative shares. Flag lateral tool transfer patterns with executable staging.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Ransom Note Creation
suggestion.rationale: CrownX ransomware implementation requires victim communication via ransom notes. Article does not detail note naming or content but post-encryption note placement is reliable impact-phase marker absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of files matching ransom-note naming patterns (README, HOW_TO_RECOVER, DECRYPT_*, CrownX_ransom.*) across system and user directories. Correlate timing with bulk encryption events and high-volume file modification detected in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Beaconing from Avalon
suggestion.rationale: Malware frameworks require C2 for attacker control. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs (no C2 domains, IPs, or beacon patterns). Article should have yielded at minimum infrastructure indicators for blocking or detection rule tuning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP traffic from compromised hosts to known Avalon/CrownX C2 infrastructure, unusual DNS resolution patterns (DGA queries), or connections to bulletproof hosting providers. Correlate with process execution of framework components.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Security Control Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware frameworks universally disable antivirus, EDR, and system recovery mechanisms before encryption. Article implies framework sophistication but pipeline did not map defense-evasion phase or associated techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications disabling Windows Defender (DisableRealtimeMonitoring, DisableAntiSpyware), service stops (WinDefend, MsSense, MsMpEngine), scheduled task deletions, or Windows event log clearing. Correlate with Avalon process execution in the same time window.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Asset Inventory & Patching Status - CVE-2026-48282
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' for this vulnerability. Federal patch due date of 2026-07-10 and CRIT severity demand immediate inventory and compliance tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database and vulnerability scanner output for ColdFusion installations and match against known-vulnerable versions. Flag unpatched instances as of the federal due date. Correlate with network exposure scan results to identify internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts - ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'path traversal vulnerability' as the attack vector. Web application logs must capture attempts to exploit this via directory traversal payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server logs for HTTP requests containing path traversal patterns (../, ..\\ backslash, URL-encoded variants %2e%2e, %252e) targeting ColdFusion application directories. Alert on requests that return 200/206 status codes indicating successful traversal.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Traversal - ColdFusion Process Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Execution behaviors must be detected following successful traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful path traversal attempts in web logs with subsequent process creation events spawned by ColdFusion service account. Alert on child processes like cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or scripting interpreters spawned by cfusion.exe or related ColdFusion processes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match — CVE-2026-48282 on ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV 'only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild' with explicit federal patch due date. Scanner detection is the first line of inventory control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any asset in your environment flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282 by your primary vulnerability scanner (Tenable, Qualys, etc.). Cross-correlate with asset exposure (internet-facing ColdFusion instances). High confidence indicator of exploitation risk given active KEV status.

suggestion.title: Web Log Path Traversal Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability.' Exploitation attempts manifest as directory-traversal sequences (../, ..\, encoded variants) in HTTP request URIs or body parameters targeting ColdFusion endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP requests to ColdFusion (*.cfm endpoints, /cfusion, /coldfusion paths) containing path-traversal syntax: ../, ..\, %2e%2e, ..%2f, or similar encoding. Flag requests that bypass directory restrictions. Correlate with successful responses (200) after prior 404s, indicating traversal success.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Spawning from ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Successful exploitation results in child processes spawned by the ColdFusion service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual child processes spawned by ColdFusion process (java.exe, cfusion.exe, or ColdFusion runtime process depending on version). Look for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or scripting interpreters launched with suspicious arguments or parent-child relationship violations typical of the ColdFusion service account.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Service Outbound Connections Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary code execution in the 'context of the current user' enables the attacker to perform command and control. Monitor for unexpected outbound network activity from ColdFusion process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ColdFusion process initiating outbound connections to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially to C2 infrastructure or non-standard ports (8080, 8888, 443 to non-CDN hosts). Correlate timing with process-spawn events to isolate post-exploitation beacon activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-48282 affecting Adobe ColdFusion; standard asset-exposure hunt template applies. No UC generated despite this being the core detection for known-exploited CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Adobe ColdFusion instances with versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282. Cross-reference asset inventory and escalate any unpatched host; patch due date passed 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability'—this is the attack vector and must be detectable in web logs. No web-based detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion web server logs for path traversal payloads: requests containing ../, ..\, URL-encoded variants (%2e%2e, %252e), or absolute paths targeting config directories (WEB-INF, cfusion). Flag any successful HTTP 200 responses to traversal attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—this execution phase must have a detection UC. Pipeline omitted entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) from ColdFusion JVM process (java.exe, cfusion.exe). Alert on suspicious CLI arguments or network connections initiated post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Configuration or Code Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal and code execution typically enable file-system modifications for persistence. Article text supports this exploitation chain but pipeline generated no post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion installation directories and WEB-INF for unauthorized writes. Track unexpected JSP/CFM file creation, data source or scheduled-task additions via admin console, and unexpected service/registry modifications indicating backdoor persistence.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Leveraging ColdFusion Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes public-facing ColdFusion vulnerability—compromised instance is a foothold for lateral movement. No post-compromise detection logic generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections and credential usage from compromised ColdFusion host for scanning (T1046), enumeration (T1087), or SMB/WMI lateral movement attempts post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Time-Critical Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes Federal patch due-date 2026-07-10 (today). Pipeline failed to surface urgent compliance deadline or emergency remediation tracking as a distinct UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track patch deployment status for CVE-2026-48282 across ColdFusion fleet. Escalate any host past due-date to incident response; cross-reference change management for emergency authorization and verify patch success via re-scan.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal vulnerability' as the attack vector. Web access logs against ColdFusion endpoints (.cfm, .cfc) should be hunted for traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e/, unicode bypasses). This is the initial-access detection for CVE-2026-48282.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints for path traversal payloads. Filter on request URIs matching patterns: `(\.\.[\\/]|%2e%2e[\\/]|%252e%252e)` correlated with 400/403 responses or 200 responses to non-standard file paths. Baseline normal CF app traversal and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Process Execution Post-ColdFusion Traversal Request
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'. Execution phase detection: unexpected shell spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) from ColdFusion service account within 10s of traversal-pattern HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP access logs (traversal patterns) with ProcessCreationEvents. Alert when ColdFusion service account (typically NETWORK SERVICE, IUSR_*, or w3wp.exe parent) spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash. Time window 0-30s post-request; baseline normal CF process trees.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Service Account File System Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal inherently involves file discovery. Article mentions accessing files via traversal; monitor for abnormal file-access patterns from ColdFusion service account targeting System32, Windows root, or sensitive app directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track file open/read events by ColdFusion service account. Baseline normal application file access paths. Flag rapid sequential failed-access attempts followed by success on sensitive paths (e.g., C:\Windows\System32\*, registry hives). Look for directory enumeration patterns.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Error Log Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes path traversal; ColdFusion error logs will contain file-not-found, access-denied, or traversal-rejection exceptions. Error patterns are early signal of exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse ColdFusion error logs for patterns: repeated 'file not found' or 'access denied' exceptions from single source IP within short window, mixed with successful file-access results. Correlate IP source with web access logs; cluster by URI pattern to identify reconnaissance vs. exploitation.

suggestion.title: WAF/Proxy Traversal Signature Blocks
suggestion.rationale: ColdFusion is public-facing (T1190). WAF/proxy logs will show blocked traversal signatures. Article vulnerability is actively exploited (CISA KEV); WAF blocking rates inform patch urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract blocked-request logs from WAF where rule category is 'path traversal' or 'directory traversal'. Group by source IP and target URI. Track daily/hourly block rates; spike in block volume indicates active exploitation scanning. Compare to baseline; flag new source IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA KEV entry...only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild' and directs operators to use 'asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL.' Pipeline generated zero hunts despite explicit template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Adobe ColdFusion instances running vulnerable versions. Cross-reference vulnerability scan data (e.g., Tenable, Qualys) for ColdFusion versions < patched baseline against network telemetry to identify instances exposed to external networks on ports 8500, 8501, 8502 (admin), 80, 443.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts — ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'path traversal vulnerability' as attack vector. Must detect exploitation attempts (../, %2e%2e, directory escape patterns) targeting ColdFusion templates and system paths before code execution succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints for path traversal patterns (../, ..\, encoded variants %2e%2e). Correlate with response codes 200/302 to identify potential successful exploitation. Baseline ColdFusion application logging for unusual template access paths.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution in ColdFusion Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Post-exploitation signal detection required to catch successful attacks after path traversal bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation spawned from ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, java.exe with ColdFusion parent). Detect unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe) or file creation in system directories from ColdFusion context. Flag unusual outbound network connections from ColdFusion process to external IPs post-path-traversal detection.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Admin/Configuration File Access via Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal enables attackers to bypass access controls; article's emphasis on 'exploited in the wild' indicates this vector is active. Must detect attempts to access /CFIDE, cfide-bin, or config files through traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests containing path traversal sequences targeting ColdFusion administrative paths (/CFIDE, /cfide-bin, /cfadmin, web.config, cfusion.ini). Correlate with successful response codes and ColdFusion error pages. Flag repeated failed-then-successful sequences suggesting exploitation.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Tracking — CVE-2026-48282 Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10' and 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Continuous compliance hunt required to identify non-remediated systems post-deadline for federal agencies and regulated entities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner data (vulnerable ColdFusion versions to CVE-2026-48282) against patch management records. Alert on ColdFusion instances still vulnerable post-federal due date (2026-07-10). Flag organizations with exposure as non-compliant for audit/regulatory reporting.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 ColdFusion Path Traversal - Web Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Adobe ColdFusion contains a path traversal vulnerability.' This is the primary attack surface. Web access logs will contain encoded or raw directory-traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e%2f) targeting ColdFusion endpoints. Zero web-pattern UCs generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search web server access logs for HTTP requests containing path traversal patterns against known ColdFusion paths (cfusion, cfapps, administrator). Look for requests with query strings or POST bodies containing '../' or URL-encoded variants. Filter for 200/500 HTTP status codes and unusual response sizes indicating successful traversal.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 ColdFusion - Arbitrary Code Execution Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Successful exploitation spawns unexpected child processes from ColdFusion runtime. Zero process-execution use cases generated despite this being the confirmation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes launched by ColdFusion application processes (cfusion.exe, java.exe with ColdFusion classpath). Alert on unexpected spawning of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or system utilities. Include command-line argument inspection for reverse shells, file writes, or network connectivity indicators.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion CVE-2026-48282 Asset Inventory and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes active exploitation (CISA KEV status) with federal remediation deadline: 2026-07-10. Asset-exposure hunt pattern referenced in article (`_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`) mandates inventory. Zero asset-discovery use cases output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platforms for ColdFusion instances. Filter for versions in CVE-2026-48282 affected range. Cross-reference with external port scans to identify internet-facing ColdFusion services (ports 80, 443, 8500). Flag all exposed instances and compare patch dates against 2026-07-10 SLA for escalation.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Asset Inventory & Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is in Adobe ColdFusion and KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets. Pipeline must hunt for reachable ColdFusion instances before attackers do.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify exposed ColdFusion instances via port scanning (8500, 8501 for admin console, or application-specific ports), certificate enumeration, or DNS/passive DNS records. Cross-check against patch inventory for CVE-2026-48282 remediation status.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Pattern Detection in Web Access Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'path traversal vulnerability.' Pipeline must detect attempts to exploit via common traversal encodings (../, ..\, %2e%2e, Unicode encoding) in HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on URL patterns containing path traversal indicators (../, ..\, encoded variants, or null-byte sequences) in ColdFusion application paths. Correlate with 500/503 errors or successful 200 responses suggesting file-system access.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline must detect abnormal child processes spawned from ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, java.exe running as ColdFusion service account).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rare/unexpected child processes spawned by ColdFusion service account (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil, whoami). Establish baseline of legitimate ColdFusion children and alert on deviations. Correlate timing with web-log exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion JAR / Class Loading from Temp/Web Directories
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal combined with arbitrary execution suggests potential for loading malicious classes or JAR files. ColdFusion's Java integration makes this a plausible post-exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation or modification of .jar, .class, or .cfm files in ColdFusion web-root, temp directories (%temp%, /tmp), or ColdFusion-specific paths (WEB-INF/lib). Monitor ColdFusion logs for ClassLoader errors or unexpected JAR loading.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Administrator Console Access & Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal gaining RCE as 'current user' may allow pivoting to ColdFusion admin console or escalating to service account privileges. Article does not rule out privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to ColdFusion admin interface (/cfide/administrator) post-exploitation, especially from unexpected IPs or service accounts. Alert on authentication failures followed by successful admin API calls or configuration changes (data-source adds, scheduled task creation).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Patch Compliance Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date 2026-07-10 and KEV definition means this is actively exploited. Pipeline must validate patch status across fleet to identify unpatched ColdFusion versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch inventory for ColdFusion versions known vulnerable to CVE-2026-48282 and cross-reference installed instances. Alert on instances past federal due date without remediation. Capture ColdFusion version from web-server headers or admin console fingerprint.

suggestion.title: SiYuan record/cell creation with HTML breakout or event-handler patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'cell value like `` ... breaks out of its surrounding tag.' This is stored XSS creation—the payload is *persisted* before execution. No UC detects injection at storage time. Detection at this phase enables containment before victims open the record.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SiYuan database record writes (or raw JSON file modifications in data/storage/av/) containing HTML closing tags (</), img/script tags, or event handler attributes (onerror, onclick, onload). Correlate file modification timestamp with subsequent SiYuan process spawning to link storage→execution.

suggestion.title: SiYuan attribute-view panel opened on recently-modified or suspicious records
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'breaks out of its surrounding tag and runs arbitrary JavaScript in the renderer when the victim opens the block-attribute panel.' This is the execution trigger. No UC detects suspicious block access or attribute-view rendering. User interaction is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SiYuan accessing records in data/storage/av/ that contain HTML breakout patterns, followed within seconds by unsigned child process spawning or network I/O. Look for Electron process crashes or memory allocation anomalies preceding spawning.

suggestion.title: SiYuan Electron renderer executes inline JavaScript (onerror/onclick handler)
suggestion.rationale: The XSS itself is JavaScript execution via img onerror handlers. Article: 'img src=x onerror="..."'. No UC detects script execution within the renderer context before system-level process spawning.
log_sources: Sysmon Event 8 (CreateRemoteThread from SiYuan child process)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SiYuan.exe or SiYuan child processes creating temporary files with script extensions (.js, .vbs, .ps1), loading unsigned modules, or injecting code into system processes. Correlate with attribute-view database record access events.

suggestion.title: Malicious Supply-Chain Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the `exploration` crate 'attempted to download and execute a payload from a remote site.' Detect installation or compilation of this and similar malicious packages across the environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cargo build/install of packages matching known malicious crate list (e.g., `exploration`). Correlate Cargo.lock/Cargo.toml containing `exploration` with system inventory. Alert on historical deployments of this crate to assess organizational blast radius.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Lifecycle Anomaly (Publish → Removal <2 hours)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes the crate was 'published on 2026-06-02, approximately 1 hour before removal.' Detect packages published and yanked/removed within short timeframes as indicator of supply-chain poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest package repository metadata for all targeted ecosystems (crates.io, npm, PyPI, NuGet). Flag any package with <2 hour publish-to-removal interval. Cross-reference against employee/org internal package names to detect impersonation attempts.

suggestion.title: Network Egress from Build/Package Manager Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload download during crate use. Malicious crates trigger network activity at build or runtime. Detect anomalous egress from cargo, pip, npm, or similar during package operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections initiated by cargo.exe, rustc, cargo-build parent processes. Flag egress to non-package-registry IPs (e.g., not crates.io, github.com, or trusted mirrors). Correlate with recent package installations.

suggestion.title: Malicious Crate Removal Advisory Ingestion & Alerting
suggestion.rationale: GitHub Security Advisories and crate.io removal notices are the primary signal. Article states `exploration` was yanked for malicious code. Operationalize advisories by syncing removal notices to inventory systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Consume GitHub Advisories RSS (and crates.io removal notices) in real-time. For any CRITICAL advisory involving malicious package removal, immediately query package inventory for installed versions. Trigger incident response for any matches found.

suggestion.title: Suspiciously Inactive Crate with Malicious Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'no evidence of actual usage' yet contained malicious payload download/execute. Detect packages with zero organic dependency footprint but anomalous system behavior on install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track newly published packages (age < 30 days) with zero reverse-dependencies on crates.io. Cross-reference with any system events (process creation, network, file writes) during builds. High-zero-dependency + behavioral anomaly = alert.

suggestion.title: Cargo.lock / Cargo.toml Containment & Remediation Sweep
suggestion.rationale: Retrospective inventory: if `exploration` was ever installed, find all developer machines and CI/CD systems affected. Article provides concrete package name; sweep for historical usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Cargo.lock and Cargo.toml files in version control history and file-shares for presence of `exploration` crate. Enumerate all build logs and CI pipelines containing `cargo build` on affected commit ranges. Correlate with process execution history to detect if payload was executed.

suggestion.title: Forged proxy-auth header (X-Forwarded-For / X-Original-User mismatch)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'any unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server directly can impersonate any user—including admin—by sending a single forged HTTP header.' Proxy-auth headers (X-Forwarded-For, X-Original-User, etc.) must match the source IP and proxy hop chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when FileBrowser receives /api/login requests with proxy-auth headers (X-Forwarded-For, X-Original-User) that do NOT match the actual source IP or proxy chain. Look for direct TCP connections to the FileBrowser port followed by authenticated API calls—the proxy should front all traffic. Mismatches indicate header forgery.

suggestion.title: Automatic admin account creation via non-existent username
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'specifying a non-existent username causes the server to automatically create a new user account, providing an account creation primitive.' New accounts should not be auto-created on failed login; this is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for /api/login POST requests with non-existent usernames immediately followed by successful account creation (via /api/users or user management API) and subsequent successful login. Multiple distinct non-existent usernames created within a short window is high-confidence account provisioning abuse.

suggestion.title: Admin API access without prior privilege escalation (session privilege jump)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'impersonate any user—including admin—by sending a single forged HTTP header.' A non-admin session should not suddenly access admin-only endpoints (/api/settings, /api/users, /api/resources admin actions) without an explicit elevation event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP sessions: if a session accesses /api/login (auth), then immediately calls admin-only endpoints (/api/settings, /api/users with write/delete) without a prior /api/roles or /api/elevate request, flag as unauthorized escalation. Look for 200/201 status codes on admin endpoints in a session that did not demonstrate admin identity at login time.

suggestion.title: Direct FileBrowser inbound connections (proxy-auth bypass indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'when configured with proxy authentication, any unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server directly can impersonate any user.' Proxy-auth means ALL traffic should be fronted by the proxy; direct connections to FileBrowser port from external/non-proxy IPs indicate bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to the FileBrowser process/port. Flag connections from sources that are NOT in the organization's proxy server IP allowlist. A legitimate proxy-auth setup should have zero external direct connections; any direct inbound is a bypass attempt. Correlate with /api/login requests in the same time window.

suggestion.title: Session token creation anomaly (instant JWT/session issue post-login)
suggestion.rationale: Article narrative implies fast-path admin impersonation. Legitimate sessions have typical authentication latency; forged-header sessions have none. Detect JWT/session tokens issued before normal auth processing could complete.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If FileBrowser logs session token creation, look for tokens issued with zero or sub-100ms latency between login request and token grant. Compare against baseline session creation timings. Legitimate login flows involve credential validation, DB lookup, etc. Forged-header bypasses skip these; anomalously fast token issue is an exploit signal.

suggestion.title: Browser extension requesting chrome-extension:// origin to localhost API
suggestion.rationale: Article states core mechanism: 'unconditionally trusts all chrome-extension:// origins' — this is the authentication bypass. Need hunt for extensions making requests to local admin APIs without standard OAuth/bearer tokens. Article phrase: 'blanket chrome-extension:// Origin Allowlist'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests originating from chrome-extension:// scheme targeting 127.0.0.1:6806 with Content-Type application/json or API endpoints. Correlate with SiYuan auth logs showing successful admin API calls without matching authentication tokens or AccessAuthCode.

suggestion.title: Extension payload modification or CRX tampering via supply chain
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'compromised legitimate extension via supply chain attack' — need detection for CRX files or extension manifests with unexpected payloads. Article phrase: 'Compromise Software Supply Chain'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unsigned or re-signed .crx files, manifest.json files modified post-installation, or extension background scripts with embedded obfuscated code. Look for CRX extraction (7z, unzip) operations outside of browser cache directories.

suggestion.title: SiYuan admin API calls without privilege context escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'granting RoleAdministrator access to every installed browser extension without any authentication' and 'default empty AccessAuthCode' — admin operations succeeding from non-admin user. Need application-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect SiYuan kernel audit logs for administrative API calls (e.g., /api/admin/*, /api/workspace/*, data delete/export operations) originating from localhost when called by low-privilege process context or when AccessAuthCode is empty/default.

suggestion.title: Rapid credential extraction post-extension install
suggestion.rationale: Article: extension gains access then 'steal[s] web session cookies, browser login data' — temporal correlation between extension install and browser credential file access. Article phrase: 'Steal Web Session Cookie', 'Credentials from Web Browsers'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser extension installation (Registry create in \Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\) with subsequent file reads of Login Data or Cookies files within 5 minutes, especially from non-browser processes or script interpreters launched by the extension.

suggestion.title: SiYuan kernel ListeningConnectionCreated without auth interception
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'kernel HTTP server unconditionally trusts' — need host-level exposure detection that confirms vulnerable configuration. Port 6806 binding alone insufficient; need to correlate with absent/empty auth mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify SiYuan.exe listening on port 6806 (ListeningConnectionCreated), then attempt low-privilege curl/wget requests to /api/admin endpoints and confirm 200 responses without authentication headers. This validates exploitability.

suggestion.title: Storage Zone Controller Suspicious Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes 'Shut Down' directive, indicating active exploitation or post-compromise activity. Storage Zone Controllers are IIS-hosted services; child process spawns (cmd.exe, PowerShell, net.exe) from w3wp.exe or StorageZoneController service account signal RCE or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child process relationships where w3wp.exe (IIS) or a Storage Zone Controller service account spawns interactive shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or system tools (net.exe, whoami.exe, ipconfig.exe). Filter legitimate admin/backup processes. High fidelity if execution occurs with network connection to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Storage Zone Controller Unusual Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'Shut Down' implies either active exploitation in progress or post-compromise backdoor. If this is a web-facing RCE, compromised controllers will beacon to C2 or exfiltrate data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of Storage Zone Controller outbound connections (only to Progress services, internal networks, and S3/cloud storage). Flag any new external IPs, non-HTTP/HTTPS protocols, or connections to known C2 infrastructure. Prioritize connections initiated by w3wp.exe or service accounts outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Storage Zone Controller DLL Injection or In-Memory Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Critical ShareFile vulnerabilities in the web stack often involve RCE leading to in-memory backdoors or DLL side-loading. Title's urgency suggests post-compromise persistence mechanisms may already be active.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or mismatched DLL loads into w3wp.exe or StorageZoneController processes, especially from non-standard paths (temp, user directories, network shares). Alert on DLL sideloading attempts and DLL shadow copying. Baseline legitimate Progress-signed modules.

suggestion.title: ShareFile Service Restart/Stop Events at Scale
suggestion.rationale: Advisory to 'Shut Down' controllers is incident-response guidance, but attackers often restart compromised services post-exploitation to re-enable backdoors. Monitoring for coordinated service events across many hosts indicates either coordinated defense or post-compromise persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Storage Zone Controller or Progress-related service restart/stop events, especially if: (1) initiated by non-admin accounts, (2) triggered by scheduled tasks or registry modifications, (3) clustered in time across multiple hosts, (4) followed immediately by new service creation.

suggestion.title: File Upload to ShareFile with Suspicious Characteristics
suggestion.rationale: If vulnerability allows arbitrary file upload or remote code execution via file operations, adversaries may plant webshells, executables, or scripts in ShareFile directories for persistence or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new files written to ShareFile directories with executable extensions (.exe, .dll, .ps1, .aspx, .asp, .jsp) or suspicious characteristics (double extensions, no owner metadata, created at odd hours). Cross-reference with HTTP POST/PUT requests in IIS logs to identify upload source.

suggestion.title: Registry Modifications for IIS Application Pool or Service Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence in Windows web-server environments often involves registry keys controlling service startup, AppInit DLLs, or IIS module loading. Title's shutdown advisory suggests attackers may have already planted persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services (service binaries), HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows (AppInit_DLLs), and IIS-related registry keys. Flag changes not associated with known patches or admin tooling. Correlate with process execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 iCagenda Asset Discovery and Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'iCagenda contains an unrestricted upload' vulnerability with federal patch due 2026-07-13. The article references 'asset-exposure hunt' as the canonical detection strategy, but the pipeline extracted no use case for identifying exposed iCagenda instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search asset repositories, vulnerability scanners, and network baselines for iCagenda installations. Prioritize internet-facing or edge-accessible instances and verify patch status against CVE-2026-48939 remediation due date (2026-07-13). Flag any unpatched versions.

suggestion.title: Executable/Script File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability' and 'arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload.' Pipeline missed detection for dangerous MIME types being uploaded.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to iCagenda file upload endpoints for dangerous file extensions (.php, .exe, .jsp, .asp, .cgi, .pl, .py, .sh, .bat, .cmd) or multipart request bodies containing PHP magic bytes or script content types.

suggestion.title: PHP Process Execution from Web Upload Directory Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'PHP code upload and execution' as the vulnerability outcome. Pipeline provided no detection for command execution spawning from iCagenda upload/attachment directories following successful file placement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter processes (php.exe, php-cgi) spawning child processes where the parent or working directory aligns with iCagenda upload paths. Correlate process spawn timestamps with prior file upload events in web logs.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Configuration Audit — Upload Filter Misconfiguration
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'unrestricted upload' due to missing/disabled file type validation. Configuration audits can identify instances with upload validation disabled or overly permissive settings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit iCagenda configuration files for disabled MIME type blacklists, missing file extension restrictions, or overly permissive upload directory permissions. Flag configurations where PHP execution is enabled in publicly writable directories.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Unrestricted File Upload — Dangerous File Type Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload.' This is the primary attack vector; zero UCs captured it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT to iCagenda attachment endpoints for executable file extensions (PHP, .exe, .jsp, .asp). Alert on Content-Type mismatches (e.g., application/octet-stream with .php extension) or missing MIME type validation.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'PHP code upload and execution.' Post-upload execution is the exploitation phase; no UC generated for this critical step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP GET/POST requests to .php files in web-accessible upload/attachment paths. Flag process execution of PHP interpreters spawned from upload directories or with unusual parent processes.

suggestion.title: Webshell Upload Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Unrestricted PHP upload enables webshell deployment. Active CISA KEV exploitation suggests webshell post-exploitation is likely; no UC addresses persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan uploaded PHP files for webshell signatures (system, exec, passthru, shell_exec, eval, base64_decode). Correlate PHP uploads with subsequent outbound connections or unusual process spawning.

suggestion.title: Exposed iCagenda Public-Facing Instance Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190) requires target discovery. No UC for asset exposure scanning or vulnerability scanning integration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for iCagenda instances; filter for CVE-2026-48939 vulnerable versions. Cross-reference asset database for instances accessible from untrusted networks. Monitor for HTTP Server banners revealing iCagenda via header inspection.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Upload Volume to Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Unrestricted upload with no size enforcement mentioned. Attackers may upload multiple payloads or large files; baseline behavior not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline file upload count and size per source IP per time window for iCagenda attachment endpoints. Alert on 3+ sigma deviations: unusually frequent uploads, files exceeding historical max, or bulk uploads from single IP.

suggestion.title: Unrestricted File Upload to iCagenda Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability' in the 'file attachment feature'. Detection must intercept uploads that bypass type validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints for anomalous file extensions (PHP, ASP, JSP, executable types). Alert when uploaded file extension does not match declared Content-Type or when executables are uploaded to web-accessible attachment directories. Baseline on known-good file types only.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability results in 'PHP code upload and execution'. Detection must identify when PHP interpreter executes files from upload/temp directories, indicating successful exploitation post-upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe or php process spawning with command-line arguments referencing files in /uploads, /attachments, or /tmp directories. Flag inconsistent parent process chains (web server spawning PHP interpreter directly). Correlate with file creation events in upload directories within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Exposed Application Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV context indicates active exploitation against public-facing instances. Article requires asset discovery baseline to identify targets. Phrase: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date' implies exposure assessment is first detection step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query firewall/proxy logs for HTTP responses with Server header matching iCagenda patterns or User-Agent strings from iCagenda clients. Identify DNS resolution for iCagenda-related domains. Cross-reference with external-facing asset inventory to locate instances accessible from internet.

suggestion.title: Dangerous File Type Upload Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability class 'Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type' requires type-based filtering. Article: 'allows the upload of arbitrary files'. Detection must distinguish legitimate document uploads from executable/script uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected file types for iCagenda attachment feature (PDF, DOCX, JPG, PNG). Alert on uploads of .php, .exe, .dll, .sh, .bat, .asp, .jsp to attachment endpoints. Flag MIME type mismatches and multiple extension uploads from same source IP within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Management Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article directs to 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and specifies federal patch due date 2026-07-13. Structured scan-based detection is the primary asset-exposure control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results identifying CVE-2026-48939 on any host with open ports 80/443 or accessible from internet. Flag unfixed vulnerabilities after federal due date (2026-07-13). Correlate unfixed results with network segmentation failures and firewall rules allowing external access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Detection via Asset Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48939 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and references the canonical asset-exposure hunt template. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this clear guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner hits for CVE-2026-48939 on internet-exposed iCagenda instances. Priority check: instances > 30 days past 2026-07-13 federal patch deadline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' and 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type'. No UC detects malicious uploads to documented endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda /upload or /attachment endpoints for POST requests with .php, .phtml, .shtml, .jsp, .asp, .exe extensions or Content-Type mismatches (e.g., declared image but actual executable).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'PHP code upload and execution' as the attack outcome. No UC for detecting execution phase (T1059.007) post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP GET/POST requests to .php files within iCagenda upload directory with HTTP 200 status and dynamic response content. Correlate with preceding upload event.

suggestion.title: Web Server Child Process Spawning from PHP
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful PHP upload enables 'code upload and execution'. Webshell post-exploitation requires detection of w3wp/httpd spawning cmd.exe or PowerShell.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes spawned by w3wp.exe or php-fpm with parent command line containing iCagenda paths; suspicious binaries: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or living-off-land tools.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Webshell Persistence Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Upload-to-execution path naturally leads to persistence. Article omits detection of repeated webshell access patterns or malicious file modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload directory for new/modified .php files with timestamps post-exploitation. Flag files accessed via HTTP from multiple IP addresses or User-Agent strings within 24h window.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Arbitrary File Upload to RCE (CVE-2026-48939)
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' This is T1190 exploitation of public-facing app.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST requests to iCagenda file-attachment endpoints with non-image/document MIME types or .php-family extensions. Correlate with HTTP 200 responses followed by subsequent requests to the uploaded file path.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution'—detection must cover T1059.001 execution phase after successful upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor php.exe or php-cgi spawned from web-root directories or iCagenda installation paths with command-line arguments referencing recently-uploaded files or temp directories.

suggestion.title: Webshell Persistence from iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: RCE-capable file upload (stated: 'PHP code...execution') implies attacker establishes persistent shell access. T1505.003 applies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious PHP execution events with subsequent HTTP POST/GET requests containing web-shell functions (system, exec, passthru, file_get_contents on config files).

suggestion.title: iCagenda Installation Fingerprinting and Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Prerequisite to exploitation: attacker must discover exposed iCagenda instances. Article emphasizes patching urgency, implying active reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequential requests to iCagenda version-disclosure paths (/administrator/, /components/com_icagenda/) or path-traversal probes from single source IPs within short windows.

suggestion.title: Dangerous File-Type Upload Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause: 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type'—detection must flag MIME-type/extension/content mismatches at upload boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect uploads where Content-Type header conflicts with file extension (e.g., .php declared as image/jpeg) or file magic bytes contradict declared type; .php-family extensions are priority regardless of MIME.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Asset-Exposure Scan Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article template directs asset-exposure hunt for patch-lag detection. CISA KEV context means vulnerable installs are being actively exploited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner (Nessus/Qualys/Tenable) for CVE-2026-48939 findings. Flag systems reported 'not vulnerable' but running affected iCagenda versions; verify patch timestamps vs. scanner timing to detect lag.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Dangerous File Type Upload Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability…allows the upload of arbitrary files' and 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'. Pipeline missed file-type validation evasion as a core detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to iCagenda file attachment endpoints (/component/icagenda/ or similar) for uploads with dangerous extensions (.php, .phtml, .php5, .phar, .shtml) or PHP MIME types. Flag polyglot/double-extension uploads (e.g., .php.jpg) and files where MIME type mismatches declared extension.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'PHP code upload and execution'. Pipeline missed the execution phase entirely. Detection must track when PHP interpreters run files from known upload paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web server access logs showing PHP requests from upload directories with process creation logs showing php.exe/php spawning with those file paths as arguments. Look for PHP execution paths outside vendor/system directories that correlate temporally with prior upload activity.

suggestion.title: Web Application Shell Placement Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Unrestricted upload + PHP execution = likely web shell persistence. Article describes 'arbitrary files' resulting in execution; shells are the canonical persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag newly created files in web-accessible directories (DocumentRoot, /uploads, /files, /attachments) with suspicious names (shell.php, admin.php, test.php, upload.php, config.php) or zero content length followed by HTTP GET requests within minutes, indicating shell enumeration.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Attachment Feature Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'file attachment feature' as the attack surface. Generic file upload rules will miss iCagenda-specific endpoint logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints with high request frequency, rapid file replacements, or requests from unexpected IP/user-agent profiles. Track failed upload attempts (413, 415, 422 status codes) preceding successful uploads, indicating attacker probing for validation bypasses.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires vulnerability-scanning baselines. Pipeline failed to extract CVE as IOC or suggest scanning detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest Nessus, Qualys, or native scanner reports for CVE-2026-48939 presence. Alert on hosts running iCagenda versions < patched baseline (post-2026-07-13). Cross-correlate scanner-detected vulnerable instances with web server logs showing prior exploitation activity (successful uploads → PHP execution).

suggestion.title: File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'. This is the direct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file attachment upload endpoints for POST requests with suspicious file extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3, .php5, .phps, polyglot uploads) or Content-Type mismatches (e.g., declared image/* but contains PHP magic bytes). Alert on rapid successive uploads or uploads to unexpected directories.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from iCagenda Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'upload of arbitrary files... ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'. Detect the execution phase post-upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to recently uploaded files within iCagenda's attachment directory (correlation by timestamp + filename). Flag successful HTTP 200 responses to .php URIs. Watch for php.exe or php-cgi spawned by web server worker process; especially suspicious if spawned with unusual arguments or from attachment/upload directory paths.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Application Identification and Patch Audit
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation. Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-13'—organizations must identify and patch or mitigate before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for iCagenda web application presence (look for /icagenda/ paths, iCagenda-specific HTTP headers, default ports 80/443). Cross-reference discovered instances with patch management to ensure version ≥ patched build. Prioritize as tier-0 remediation per CISA KEV urgency.

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawning from Attachment Upload Handler
suggestion.rationale: PHP execution via uploaded shell typically manifests as web-server process spawning unexpected child processes. Article states execution phase implies observable process behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe, bash, cmd.exe, or powershell.exe spawned by iCagenda web process (w3wp.exe, httpd, nginx worker) with command lines containing shells, reverse-shell payloads, or base64-encoded commands. Correlate process spawn time with recent file uploads to attachment directory.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Unrestricted File Upload Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability' allowing 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—detection must flag file uploads to iCagenda endpoints with non-whitelisted extensions or MIME-type mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to iCagenda file attachment endpoints. Flag uploads of dangerous file extensions (php, phtml, php3, php4, php5, php7, pht, phar, inc) or MIME-type anomalies (e.g., application/x-php disguised as image/jpeg). Baseline expected upload patterns per environment to detect outliers.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Following iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution'—execution phase must be detected via correlation of suspicious uploads with subsequent PHP interpreter invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate iCagenda file uploads with immediate PHP execution (php-cgi, php-fpm spawning) reading from upload directories. Flag execution of newly-written files within seconds of upload. Identify HTTP 200 responses to requests targeting freshly-uploaded PHP objects in web-accessible paths.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Inventory and Public-Facing Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and emphasizes CISA KEV urgency with federal patch deadline 2026-07-13. Enterprises must enumerate all iCagenda instances to assess remediation status before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search DNS queries and proxy logs for iCagenda-related hostnames and domains. Query asset inventory for iCagenda software deployments. Monitor web server logs and WAF records for iCagenda-specific URIs (/component/icagenda, /modules/icagenda, /plugins/icagenda). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner to identify unpatched versions and internet-exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Post-Patch Verification for CVE-2026-48939 Remediation
suggestion.rationale: Article stresses 'Anything in CISA KEV is currently being exploited' with explicit federal patch deadline 2026-07-13. Post-deadline validation is critical—patch lag has historically been the vector for mass exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On or after 2026-07-14, scan all identified iCagenda instances for CVE-2026-48939 patch status. Verify application version strings match patched builds. Alert on any remaining unpatched instances. Compare pre-deadline inventory to post-deadline to identify systems that failed remediation and require escalation.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Arbitrary File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—core attack vector. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this explicit description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload endpoints (/upload, /attachment, /file handlers) for POST requests followed by file creation. Flag non-image/doc extensions (especially .php, .phtml, .php7) in web-accessible directories. Baseline legitimate upload activity first to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution on Web Root Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'—the execution phase is critical but unmapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP GET/POST to recently-uploaded .php files in web document root. Correlate file creation (T1005) + web access within 5 min window. Track PHP process spawning (SYSTEM context) triggered by web server user (apache/www-data/nginx).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scan Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-48939 as the exploited vulnerability; pipeline IOCs empty. Correlation with scanner output is fundamental.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Qualys/Nessus/Rapid7 for iCagenda instances flagged as CVE-2026-48939. Cross-reference against patch inventory. Alert on unpatched instances with inbound HTTP traffic from internet-facing boundaries (T1046 detection).

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Persistence in iCagenda Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'file attachment feature'—files uploaded must persist on disk. Detection should flag anomalous file retention/modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload/attachment directories for files modified outside normal maintenance windows. Flag executable types (.php, .exe, .sh). Alert on files created by web server processes outside of legitimate upload workflows (timestamp clustering, parent process chain).

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawning Shells Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: PHP execution implies process spawning from web server context; article indicates code execution occurs. This is post-compromise execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by apache/nginx/php-fpm with command lines indicative of shell execution (bash, sh, cmd, powershell). Baseline legitimate plugins/crons first. Correlate with recent file uploads to same iCagenda instance.

suggestion.title: HTTP Traffic Anomalies to iCagenda Upload Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—HTTP POST patterns differ sharply between legitimate and malicious uploads (size, frequency, content-type mismatches).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to iCagenda upload endpoints with Content-Type header mismatch (e.g., .php declared as image/jpeg). Alert on rapid-fire uploads from single source IP within short window. Monitor for 200/201 responses followed by GET requests to same filename within seconds.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Accessible iCagenda Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' must be deployed. This is the reconnaissance phase before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for iCagenda instances exposed to public internet. Search web logs and proxy logs for HTTP responses identifying iCagenda (version banners, favicon hash, directory paths like /administrator). Flag instances without known recent patches.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to Attachment Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload'. Direct detection of .php uploads to iCagenda's upload handler.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda attachment/upload endpoints for .php, .phtml, .php5, .phar extensions in multipart form-data or filenames. Alert on 200–201 responses indicating successful upload.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'PHP code upload and execution'—once uploaded, attacker triggers execution by requesting the file, which spawns PHP processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests to newly uploaded PHP files (within attachment storage directories) with subsequent process execution (php.exe, php-fpm spawned by web server user). Alert on command-line arguments typical of post-exploit recon (whoami, systeminfo, id, curl).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Web Shell Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: PHP web shell will execute system commands. Look for shell commands spawned by web server context immediately following file upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when web server processes (nginx, apache, php-fpm) spawn child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash) with obfuscated or suspicious arguments; baseline normal web server behavior and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Persistence in Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Uploaded PHP files persist in attachment directory for repeated access. Monitor file-write events to attachment/upload paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-write operations to iCagenda attachment/upload directories for non-standard extensions (.php, .js, .exe) or suspicious timestamps (writes outside business hours, immediately after suspicious HTTP traffic).

suggestion.title: Outbound Command-and-Control from Web Shell
suggestion.rationale: Executed PHP shell code will likely beaconing or download additional payloads. Detect outbound connections from web server context to unknown IPs/domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from web server processes (php.exe, nginx, apache) to non-whitelisted external IPs or domains. Cross-reference with DNS logs for suspicious domain lookups from web server context.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Exposed iCagenda Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [`../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`]' and requires detection before the federal patch-due date 2026-07-13. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internet-accessible iCagenda instances via HTTP response headers, error pages, or login portal fingerprinting. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner output and patch status to isolate instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-48939. Prioritize remediation by exposure window vs. patch-due date.

suggestion.title: File Upload Abuse: Non-Image/Non-Document Extensions to iCagenda Attachment Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'. Pipeline missed upload-phase detection.

suggestion.title: Post-Upload Execution: PHP Interpreter Activity from Web Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'. Pipeline did not surface execution-phase hunting despite explicit description.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Feature

suggestion.title: PHP Interpreter Spawning from Web-Writable Upload Paths

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 iCagenda Vulnerability Presence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' via template substitution and specifies CISA KEV status with federal patch deadline 2026-07-13, but pipeline generated zero vulnerability-scanner or patch-compliance detection logic.

suggestion.title: Cypher syntax keywords in Langroid prompts and LLM inputs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'query text is influenceable by prompt injection (direct user input or indirect content the agent reads back via RAG).' The injection vector is the prompt itself. Detection should identify prompts/inputs containing Cypher keywords before Neo4j execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests or application log entries where Langroid receives prompts containing Cypher syntax (DETACH DELETE, LOAD CSV, CALL apoc, CALL dbms). Correlate timestamps with subsequent Neo4j query.log entries containing same keywords to confirm prompt-to-query injection succeeded. Baseline normal prompts and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: APOC library enabled or loaded in Neo4j runtime/config
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies APOC/dbms procedures as the RCE landing pad ('APOC/dbms Cypher-to-RCE landing'). APOC must be explicitly enabled. Detection should identify when APOC procedures become available in the database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for: (1) neo4j.conf edits enabling APOC (dbms.security.procedures.unrestricted patterns), (2) Neo4j startup logs showing APOC jar/plugin loading, (3) Queries invoking apoc.* or dbms.* procedures from non-admin sessions. Flag first-time APOC invocations by service accounts.

suggestion.title: Langroid service account permission escalation in Neo4j
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes unvalidated queries with no allowlist. If Langroid service account runs read-only, injection of DETACH DELETE or APOC.execute fails at permission level—detection should flag when service account queries attempt forbidden operations or exceed assigned role.
log_sources: Neo4j query execution logs with permission context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Langroid service account's baseline role and assigned Cypher privileges. Flag queries attempting WRITE, ADMIN, or APOC operations from that account. Flag new service accounts created for Langroid access. Flag sudden permission changes to existing Langroid accounts.

suggestion.title: Langroid Neo4jChatAgent config disabling validation or allowlist
suggestion.rationale: Title notes 'config-conditional RCE'—security is config-dependent. Detection should identify deployments where query validation is explicitly disabled or statement allowlists are absent/empty.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Langroid configs for Neo4jChatAgent sections where: (1) `query_validation_enabled=false`, (2) `allow_list` or `statement_allowlist` is empty/null, (3) `disable_cypher_validation=true` or similar. Flag configs merging defaults that disable guardrails. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results and breach timelines.

suggestion.title: Mass graph data destruction via DETACH DELETE operations
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1485 (Data Destruction). DETACH DELETE can obliterate nodes/relationships at scale. Detection should flag mass deletion operations deviating from baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline DETACH DELETE volume and scope per authenticated session. Alert on: (1) single DETACH DELETE removing >1000 nodes/relationships, (2) DETACH DELETE without WHERE clauses, (3) mass deletions outside scheduled maintenance windows. Correlate timing with observed prompt injection attempts or Cypher syntax keywords in logs.

suggestion.title: APOC export operations exfiltrating data to external hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1567 (Exfiltration Over Web Service). apoc.export.* can write graph data to remote URLs. Detection should identify APOC export procedures with external destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cypher queries calling apoc.export.* functions with remote URLs (http://, https://, ftp://) in parameters. Correlate with outbound network traffic from Neo4j JVM. Establish baseline of legitimate APOC exports and alert on: new destinations, high-volume transfers, export calls outside administrative sessions, or exports occurring after suspicious Cypher activity detected.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Unrestricted File Upload Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—the core attack vector. Pipeline missed any detection for file upload attempts to iCagenda endpoints, which is the initial exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to iCagenda upload endpoints (e.g., /upload, /attachment, /files). Alert on requests with file extensions matching dangerous types (.php, .phtml, .php7, .exe, .jsp) or Content-Type mismatches (e.g., application/x-php in multipart form). Correlate against iCagenda version scanning to map vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Upload Directory

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or php-fpm process creation where parent is a web server (httpd, nginx, apache, w3wp) and command line references files in known upload directories (/var/www/uploads, /iCagenda/uploads, etc.). suggestion.title: Suspicious Executable File Creation in Web-Accessible Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes file upload leading to PHP execution—detection must cover file-system indicator of successful upload. No UC suggested for monitoring .php file creation in web directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of executable file types (.php, .phtml, .php7, .phar, .jsp, .aspx) within web-accessible directories, especially those associated with iCagenda installations (/var/www/html/iCagenda/*, /opt/iCagenda/uploads/*). Filter out legitimate updates/patches by excluding known file hashes and maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Inventory & Vulnerable Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'—pipeline should generate asset-discovery UC to identify iCagenda instances before they are exploited. No inventory or scanning detection provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-48939 matches. suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Requests to iCagenda Upload Endpoints with Dangerous MIME Types
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type'—no detection for MIME-type mismatches or content validation bypass attempts.

Flag requests where declared file extension doesn't match body content (magic bytes check). Include baseline of legitimate uploads from known administrative IPs.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Process Anomaly & Remote Command Execution Post-Upload

Monitor command-line arguments for indicators: shell invocation (sh, bash, cmd.exe), network tools (curl, wget, nc, nslookup), or process spawning (exec, system, passthru). suggestion.title: iCagenda File Upload to Web Root

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server file system writes to iCagenda upload directories for files with PHP, phtml, php3, php4, php5, phar extensions immediately following HTTP POST to /upload or /attachment endpoints. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST to iCagenda file-attachment endpoints with PHP/executable MIME types or extensions in multipart form-data. Flag when PHP files appear in web-accessible upload directories post-upload.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from User-Writable Directory

suggestion.title: iCagenda Installation Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies iCagenda as the affected product. Inventory step: locate all iCagenda instances across enterprise before targeted hunt.

suggestion.title: Exploit Kit / Scanner Traffic to iCagenda
