suggestion.title: TSDProxy management API endpoint abuse: unauthorized access to 127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1 with forwarded auth tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article states token 'is the same secret used by the management HTTP server to trust forwarded' requests. Attack surface is HTTP requests to the management API with injected x-tsdproxy-auth-token or x-tsdproxy-id headers—requires network detection, not process hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to 127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1 or equivalent localhost management endpoints that include x-tsdproxy-auth-token or x-tsdproxy-id headers originating from non-TSDProxy processes (e.g., curl, wget, browser, scripting runtimes). Legitimate requests should only come from the TSDProxy service itself or trusted callers.

suggestion.title: TSDProxy backend service token leakage: internal auth token found in backend service logs or traffic
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'internal proxy auth token forwarded to all proxied backend services.' Attacker can capture token from backend logs, configs, or network captures. Need to detect when backend services expose or log the x-tsdproxy-auth-token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor backend service logs and process memory for presence of x-tsdproxy-auth-token values. Backend services should never log or expose this header; presence indicates either misconfiguration or post-exploitation data exfiltration. Correlate with TSDProxy traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: TSDProxy configuration audit: identityHeaders enabled (vulnerable default)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly requires 'identityHeaders is enabled (the default).' Mitigation is configuration hardening. Pipeline should flag instances where this dangerous setting is left at default.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan TSDProxy configuration files (typically YAML/JSON) and process arguments for `identityHeaders: true` or absence of `identityHeaders: false`. Alert on default/permissive settings. Correlate with version to identify patched vs. vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: TSDProxy token replay: x-tsdproxy-id header injected in cross-service lateral movement requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'spoofed x-tsdproxy-id replay'; attacker captures forwarded token and replays it to access other proxied backends. Requires detection of token reuse across service boundaries and unusual callers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify requests with x-tsdproxy-id or x-tsdproxy-auth-token headers sent from sources other than TSDProxy (e.g., direct from client processes, inter-service calls). Baseline legitimate cross-service patterns and alert on deviations. Look for token reuse across time intervals (replay detection).

suggestion.title: TSDProxy privilege escalation via management API: unauthorized administrative operations issued via forwarded token
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'management API escalation.' Once attacker obtains forwarded token, they can invoke privileged API operations. Article does not detail which APIs are at risk, but POST/PUT/DELETE to /api/v1 endpoints by unprivileged accounts should be flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TSDProxy management API endpoints (/api/v1/*) for write operations (POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) originating from unprivileged or unexpected accounts. Establish baseline of authorized callers and alert on deviations. Correlate with successful authentication via forwarded x-tsdproxy-auth-token headers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious crate installation – short-TTL malicious package
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'had 1 version published on 2026-06-02, approximately 1 hour before removal' — a hallmark supply-chain marker. Detects rapid package creation and takedown patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cargo/Rust package manager logs for installations of packages published within the last 24 hours. Flag packages with short lifespan (published and removed/withdrawn within hours) or generic reconnaissance-oriented names ('exploration'). Correlate against crates.io security advisory feeds for removed malicious packages.

suggestion.title: Outbound network egress from build/compilation context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'A method within the `exploration` crate attempted to download and execute a payload from a remote site' — the payload fetch is the critical execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS lookups and outbound TCP/UDP connections initiated by build processes (cargo, rustc) or their child processes to non-whitelisted or newly registered domains. Flag any HTTPS GET/POST to external domains during dependency resolution or compilation phases. Correlate with process creation logs showing execution of downloaded payloads.

suggestion.title: Package registry abuse – malicious dependency detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes crate 'removed from crates.io for malicious code' with 'no evidence of actual usage' — captures pre-blast-radius detection of supply-chain poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package registry audit logs and advisory feeds for new packages with low download counts that contain dynamic execution payloads (shell invocation, HTTP requests in module initialization). Flag packages with obfuscated or benign-sounding names published by accounts with minimal history. Cross-reference removed/withdrawn advisories against active dependency manifests in organizational CI/CD environments.

suggestion.title: Header forgery: X-Remote-User impersonation of admin accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'any unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server directly can impersonate any user - including admin - by sending a single forged HTTP header.' Existing UCs fail to detect the header value itself. Detection must flag X-Remote-User or X-Auth headers with admin/privileged usernames sent from non-proxy sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to /api/login containing X-Remote-User: admin (or other known admin accounts) originating from IP addresses outside the configured proxy subnet. Compare source IP against expected proxy egress IPs; admin impersonation from mismatched IP indicates header forgery.

suggestion.title: Account auto-creation via proxy-bypass endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'specifying a non-existent username causes the server to automatically create a new user account, providing an account creation primitive.' No existing UC correlates new account creation with direct-IP /api/login attempts. Attackers chain header forgery + non-existent username to provision backdoor accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed /api/login attempts (HTTP 401/403 or username-not-found responses) from direct IPs to subsequent user account creation events in FileBrowser user database. Flag clusters of new user creation within 5 minutes of login attempts from the same source IP.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation: administrative API access post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attacker forges admin header, gains admin access. This UC detects the consequence: elevated API actions (/api/users, /api/settings, /api/resources DELETE/PUT) originating from the compromised session without a legitimate prior admin login. Identifies lateral movement or persistence actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track user session originating from direct IP that first authenticates as non-admin (or fails auth), then issues admin-level commands (DELETE /api/users, PUT /api/settings). Flag if this sequence occurs within 1 minute—indicates likely privilege escalation via compromised session.

suggestion.title: Reverse proxy bypass: direct access port 8085 from untrusted sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'any unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server directly' can exploit. Assumes reverse proxy deployment. UC_7_5 covers this partially but lacks context correlation. This UC should detect direct port 8085 access that should have gone through proxy based on historical traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate FileBrowser access (all from internal proxy IP). Flag direct inbound connections to port 8085 from external IPs that exceed baseline noise. Correlate with absence of corresponding reverse-proxy logs to confirm bypass.

suggestion.title: Impossible-travel admin impersonation: header source vs. account location mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Attacker forges X-Remote-User:admin while connecting from public IP. If legitimate admin logins come from internal range only, this is an impossible travel scenario. Detects the core attack: header source IP != expected location of the impersonated account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each POST /api/login request with X-Remote-User header, compare source IP geolocation/ASN to historical login locations for that user. Flag high-risk mismatches (e.g., admin login from public cloud provider IP when baseline shows internal-only). Adjust sensitivity by user role (admin = critical).

suggestion.title: Authorizer: /graphql unauthenticated client_id leakage
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An unauthenticated attacker can obtain the required client_id from the public /graphql…'—reconnaissance phase hunt. Standalone detection of /graphql returning client_id without authentication is critical for attack chain detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to /graphql endpoint that return HTTP 200 with client_id in response body, where request lacks valid authentication headers or bearer tokens. Anomaly: multiple distinct source IPs querying /graphql within short window (likely reconnaissance sweep).

suggestion.title: Implicit flow without code exchange: response_type=token in /authorize
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'response_type=token or response_type=id_token'—these force tokens into URL fragment. This is the direct cause of token leakage. Should flag all implicit-flow requests, particularly to new or unexpected redirect_uri targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect /authorize endpoints accepting response_type=token (implicit flow) redirecting to hosts outside a whitelist of registered OAuth callback origins. Implicit flow is inherently riskier than authorization_code flow; any use to off-origin hosts merits investigation.

suggestion.title: Rapid /authorize exploitation iteration: multiple redirect_uri targets from single source
suggestion.rationale: Attack escalation indicator. Attacker may try multiple attacker-controlled domains or subdomains to find one that works, or may iterate in a privilege escalation/lateral movement scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag source IPs issuing 3+ /authorize requests with distinct redirect_uri host targets within a 5-minute window. Baseline: most legitimate clients use a fixed redirect_uri per application. This hunt catches attack iteration or multi-target probing.

suggestion.title: Spike in /authorize 302 redirects to off-origin hosts (bulk exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: If CVE-2026-54072 is exploited at scale across your environment, response volume to attacker domains will spike. Volume-based detection complements query-pattern hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compute baseline for /authorize → 302 redirects to registered callback origins per hour. Alert when traffic to off-origin redirect_uri destinations exceeds baseline by >5x in a 1-hour window. This catches bulk token exfiltration attempts.

suggestion.title: Authorizer /authorize response without redirect_uri whitelist validation (configuration audit)
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: endpoint 'accepts any redirect_uri without validating it against AllowedOrigins'. This is a configuration/code review hunt, not a behavioral detection, but essential for confirming vulnerability presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Review /authorize endpoint implementation for presence of redirect_uri validation against AllowedOrigins whitelist. Confirm that response_type=token and response_type=id_token requests are rejected if redirect_uri is not in whitelist. Absence of this validation confirms the vulnerability exists.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated requests to /api/settings/database without valid JWT or CLI token
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'without any authentication requirement beyond the ALWAYS_PROTECTED middleware check'—pipeline should detect requests that bypass or lack auth tokens entirely, not just successful responses. Need to hunt requests with absent/malformed Authorization headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /api/settings/database for requests with HTTP status 200 or 2xx that lack Authorization headers, have malformed JWT claims, or show null/empty token fields. Baseline legitimate access patterns and alert on unauthorized successful responses.

suggestion.title: Large JSON credential dump exfiltration from /api/settings/database
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'credentials, API keys, OAuth tokens, and settings' in database export. Need content-aware detection for structured credential patterns in HTTP response bodies (Bearer tokens, API key formats, password hashes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt GET requests to /api/settings/database returning 200 with response Content-Type application/json and body size > 100KB. Correlate with downstream regex scanning for Base64-encoded secrets, auth bearer patterns, and 'password', 'api_key', 'token' field names in JSON.

suggestion.title: Post-exploit database state mutation—import bulk overwrite attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'full database import (complete overwrite)' as phase of attack. UC_100_4 detects POST volume; need specific hunt for content that indicates *replacement* semantics (e.g., import flag parameters, payload size matching export, schema reset indicators).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST /api/settings/database for payloads containing import-action indicators (Content-Type application/json with schema metadata fields, parameters like 'action=import' or 'mode=replace'). Correlate with prior successful GET exports from same or adjacent source to detect exfil-then-overwrite pattern.

suggestion.title: 9routers service discovery and port enumeration (TCP 20128)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents port 20128 as default 9routers listener. Pipeline should hunt probing patterns specific to this port + application signature (HTTP banners, response timing, error messages unique to 9routers).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound or outbound connections to TCP 20128 from non-approved IPs. Enrich with HTTP header analysis for Server: 9routers banners or X-PoweredBy headers. Alert on correlation of multiple scanning attempts (SYN sweeps, port probes) followed by HTTP enumeration of /api/settings paths.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Suspicious File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' to 'file attachment feature' — need to detect POST requests with executable/scripting file extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3, .phar, .inc) or MIME type mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints (typically `/upload`, `/attachment`, `/file-upload` paths) for Content-Type headers mismatched to file extension, or direct .php/.phtml file uploads. Baseline allowed types and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: iCagenda PHP Web Shell Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'PHP code upload and execution' — after upload succeeds, attacker executes the payload; detect new or modified .php files in upload directories being accessed via HTTP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file creation events in web-accessible upload directories (e.g., `/uploads`, `/files`, `/attachments` under web root) with subsequent HTTP GET/POST requests to those file paths. Flag newly-created .php files accessed within minutes of creation as likely web shell execution.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Upload Directory Suspicious Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates file attachment feature is the attack vector — monitor for processes spawned from or accessing the iCagenda upload directory that are not typical for the web application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution originating from or touching iCagenda upload/attachment directories where the parent process is php.exe, apache2, or nginx. Baseline the web app's legitimate background tasks and flag anomalies (e.g., spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or unusual binaries).

suggestion.title: iCagenda Vulnerability Scanner Detection (CVE-2026-48939)
suggestion.rationale: Standard KEV asset-exposure: scan for vulnerable iCagenda instances before exploitation occurs; correlate scanner results with web logs to confirm which exposed assets were probed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run iCagenda version scanner or check HTTP headers (Server: iCagenda/X.Y.Z) against CVE-2026-48939 affected versions (due date 2026-07-13). Cross-reference vulnerable hosts with web logs for unusual attachment upload paths or reconnaissance requests in the 7 days pre-patch.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Malicious File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability… ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' This is the core attack vector; zero use cases address it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to iCagenda attachment endpoints with suspicious file extensions (.php, .phtml, .phar) or double extensions in Content-Disposition headers; baseline normal upload patterns and correlate upload timing with subsequent web server process spawning.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution After iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes PHP code upload followed by execution but no detection use case bridges upload activity to post-execution process behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP or Apache/Nginx child process spawning (cmd.exe, /bin/bash) within 5 minutes of iCagenda file uploads; detect base64/hex-encoded payloads in HTTP POST bodies to recently-created .php files; alert on code execution context switching from web server user.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Correlation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires federal remediation by 2026-07-13; pipeline must operationalize scanner data. Article mentions federal patch due date but no scanner-aligned detection strategy was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Qualys/Nessus/Tenable logs for CVE-2026-48939 findings; flag iCagenda installations with version <[patch version] on internet-facing assets; escalate within 48 hours; cross-reference scan results with netflow to identify lateral movement from compromised instances.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Component Discovery Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article provides vendor and product names but pipeline generated no asset discovery use case. Critical for identifying unpatched instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP response headers and HTTP status page content for iCagenda version strings; scan for default iCagenda paths (/components/com_icagenda, /modules/mod_icagenda); correlate with DHCP/DNS logs for hostname patterns; maintain asset inventory of vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Beaconing Post-iCagenda Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article implies PHP web shell installation but no detection use case addresses post-exploitation command-and-control or data exfiltration patterns typical of successful RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda-hosting servers for outbound connections to non-standard ports or known command-and-control infrastructure; detect HTTP requests from web-server-user context to external URLs; alert on DNS queries originating from compromised web application process.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Malicious File Upload — Script Extensions to Upload Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files…ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Pipeline generated zero detection for .php, .phtml, .php3-5 uploads to iCagenda endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to iCagenda upload/attachment endpoints with filename or Content-Type containing .php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5, .pht, .phar, .exe, .sh, .bat. Baseline: legitimate uploads are .pdf, .docx, .jpg, .png. Attackers uploading .php signals exploitation.

suggestion.title: iCagenda PHP Web Shell Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'PHP code upload and execution' but pipeline has no detection for the actual execution phase—attacker accessing the uploaded .php file to trigger RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious POST to iCagenda upload endpoint with subsequent GET/POST to a .php file in that upload directory (typically /uploads, /attachments, /media). Look for 200-status responses to newly uploaded PHP files within minutes of upload attempt. PHP execution often follows immediately.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Upload Endpoint HTTP Error Spike — Scanning or Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Attackers probe vulnerability before exploitation, generating 400/403/404/500 errors. Article describes 'unrestricted upload' as the attack vector; scanning behavior precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ≥10 HTTP error responses (400/403/404/500) to iCagenda upload endpoints within 300 seconds from single source IP, followed by 200-status POST. High error rate + successful upload = scanning + exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Detection Alert
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries mandate federal remediation by 2026-07-13 (federal patch due date listed in article). No detection use case for vulnerability scanner findings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner plugin match for CVE-2026-48939 against iCagenda instances. Critical compliance gap: any detected but unpatched iCagenda is exploitable post-2026-07-13 federal deadline. Correlate scan results with asset inventory to identify exposed web-facing instances.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Unrestricted Upload — Oversized POST Payload to Upload Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: PHP web shells are typically 5–50 KB. Abnormally large POST requests to upload endpoints signal potential malware delivery (attacker uploading pre-built tools/shells).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to iCagenda upload endpoints with Content-Length ≥100 KB (or >3σ above baseline for that endpoint). Exclude known legitimate bulk-upload jobs (e.g., admin user, service account). Single-file .php shells are typically small; large payloads suggest staged attack or tool delivery.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Post-Exploitation Command Execution Activity
suggestion.rationale: After uploading and executing PHP shell, attacker will issue OS commands (whoami, ipconfig, dir, net user) for reconnaissance. Pipeline stops at initial access; no detection for post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by php.exe or web server (w3wp.exe, httpd.exe) with command lines containing whoami, ipconfig, systeminfo, net user, dir, or encoded PowerShell. Web shells spawn OS commands after initial foothold; this is the exploitation confirmation.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Unrestricted File Upload to iCagenda Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' Pipeline generated zero hunts for upload endpoint activity despite this being the exploit vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful POST/PUT requests to iCagenda file upload endpoints (typically /media/upload, /attachments, or similar paths) where multipart form data contains executable or script-type files. Correlate with application error logs showing 'upload' or 'attachment' messages.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web-Accessible Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'PHP code upload and execution.' Pipeline did not generate detection for execution of uploaded PHP scripts, which is the final attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to .php files in known upload directories (e.g., /uploads, /attachments, /media) with suspicious query parameters or POST bodies. Cross-reference file creation timestamps in upload directories with HTTP access logs within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Dangerous File Type Upload Attempt Blocking
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability allowing 'arbitrary files' including executables. Should detect and alert on upload attempts with .php, .exe, .jsp, .asp extensions to iCagenda.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST/PUT requests to iCagenda endpoints with Content-Type multipart/form-data where the filename contains dangerous extensions (.php, .exe, .sh, .jsp, .asp, .aspx). Distinguish between blocked (403/400) vs. accepted (200/201) responses.

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawning from Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: PHP execution implies web server process (apache, nginx, php-fpm) accessing or executing files in upload folders. No process-level hunt was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation or file access events where the web server process (php.exe, apache, nginx) touches files in known upload directories with anomalous timing (e.g., newly created .php file accessed/executed within seconds of upload).

suggestion.title: iCagenda Vulnerability Scanner Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends checking 'across your fleet' via vulnerability scanners. Pipeline should have generated baseline hunt for CVE-2026-48939 scanner results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-48939 detections. Correlate 'patch installed' vs. 'vulnerable' status against actual asset inventory. Flag assets showing 'vulnerable' status 48+ hours after patch due date (2026-07-13).

suggestion.title: POST-Exploitation Web Shell Activity on iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: Once PHP shell is uploaded, attacker will interact with it via HTTP. Article implies command execution; should detect shell webshell patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to uploaded PHP files with suspicious query strings (e.g., ?cmd=, ?shell=, ?action=, or base64-encoded payloads). Look for POST bodies containing common webshell commands (whoami, id, ls, cat, etc.) or execution patterns.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Arbitrary File Upload to Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' — core attack vector, zero detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file attachment POST endpoints (typically /attachments, /upload) for requests returning 200/201 followed by file creation on disk. Flag uploads where declared MIME type mismatches file extension or where upload clustering occurs across short time windows.

suggestion.title: PHP File Type Upload to iCagenda Attachments
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'PHP code upload' as exploitation path — pipeline missed detection of the malicious file type itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on uploads of .php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5, .phar to any iCagenda attachment storage path. Monitor for double-extension bypass attempts (.php.jpg) or null-byte injection (.php%00.jpg). Flag any uploaded file later accessed via GET to the web root.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from iCagenda Uploaded Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution' — execution phase has no detection hypothesis despite being explicitly named.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file uploads to iCagenda attachment directories with subsequent child process spawning from web server (apache/nginx/php-fpm parent PID). Flag execution of PHP processes reading recently-uploaded files from attachment storage or executing shell commands via system() / exec() / passthru().

suggestion.title: Exposed iCagenda Asset Discovery & Correlation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active wild exploitation — pipeline missed threat-hunt to correlate vulnerable instances with vulnerability scanner data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all HTTP requests to iCagenda paths (/index.php?view=*, /com_icagenda/*) with unpatched instances flagged by scanner (pre-patch-due 2026-07-13). Establish baseline for each instance and flag spike in 404s, 500s, or unusual HTTP verbs to attachment endpoints.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Indicators from iCagenda RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes code execution capability but pipeline omitted post-compromise behavioral detections (data exfil, C2, lateral movement).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP processes spawned by web server for anomalous outbound DNS queries, HTTP connections to non-CDN IPs, or SQL/SSH/RDP connections to internal hosts. Flag file read activity from /var/www or web root accessing /etc/passwd, configuration databases, or credential stores.

suggestion.title: Orchard Action proof structure anomalies in transaction validation logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious prover to produce a valid proof for an Orchard Action with an *under-constrained* base point'. Wallet/node proof validators would log constraint failures or shape mismatches; detect proof validation errors specific to base-point encoding.
log_sources: DeviceEvents with zcash/orchard proof validation logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Zcash/Orchard proof validation subsystems for errors matching 'base.*constraint', 'diversified.*fail', or 'scalar.*under-constrained'. Correlate with suspicious transaction broadcast patterns 2-5 minutes prior (fuzz testing).

suggestion.title: Diversified address integrity verification bypass in Orchard transactions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the flaw 'enforce[s] the diversified-address-integrity condition of the Orchard Action statement'. Detect transactions where address derivation fails proof verification but validation still succeeds (logic bypass).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Orchard transactions where address commitment hash does not match the base-point encoding used in the proof. Cross-reference transaction ID against known proofs from the same transaction pool to detect duplicates or variants.

suggestion.title: Blockchain ledger anomalies: double-spends or phantom transactions post-vulnerability window
suggestion.rationale: If under-constrained base points enable proof forgery, attackers could create false transactions with identical inputs to legitimate ones. Article phrase: 'under-constrained base, breaking Orchard Action circuit soundness' implies ledger integrity is compromised.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query the Zcash ledger for Orchard actions with identical inputs (nullifiers) spending to different outputs, or address derivation failures that should have been rejected. Correlate timing to vulnerable node versions observed in UC_101_2.

suggestion.title: Malicious Zcash/Orchard library installation from compromised or typosquatted registries
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires an attacker to use vulnerable halo2_gadgets/Orchard code. Detect package manager installations of these libraries from non-canonical sources or with modified signatures (supply-chain compromise vector).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cargo/npm/pip for installation of halo2_gadgets, orchard, zcash_primitives from registries other than crates.io/npmjs. Flag packages with version strings matching vulnerable ranges (< 0.5.0, etc.) installed from local/mirror registries.

suggestion.title: Proof generation failures or assertion errors in halo2 / Orchard circuit execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'missing copy constraint' in the gadget—legitimate provers using this library would encounter constraint satisfaction failures in logs. Monitor for circuits rejecting valid transactions due to underspecified constraints.
log_sources: Application logs from Zcash wallet/node software
Rust panic logs from halo2 gadget code
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on halo2 solver / Orchard gadget assertion errors mentioning 'copy constraint', 'instance column', or 'base point' within 2 hours of vulnerable node/wallet startup. Correlate with UC_101_1/UC_101_2 asset inventory to confirm vulnerable component version.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Upload Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability' through 'file attachment feature'—need baseline of upload POST/PUT traffic to identify the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to iCagenda upload endpoints (typically /upload, /attachment, /file endpoints). Correlate with response codes 200-201 and file size anomalies. Flag multiple failed uploads followed by success as potential bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: PHP Webshell Upload in Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP code upload and execution'—detection must catch .php, .phtml, .php3 files appearing in web-accessible directories post-upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of PHP files in web document root or upload directories. Correlate file-created timestamps with iCagenda upload endpoint HTTP 200s within 5 seconds. Use file signature analysis to catch polyglot or obfuscated PHP (double extensions, null bytes, case variations).

suggestion.title: iCagenda Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires asset scanning—article names 'iCagenda' product but provides no version bounds. Need asset discovery UC to identify installed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for iCagenda installation paths (/var/www/icagenda, common plugin directories) and HTTP Server headers/responses that leak version. Cross-check against CVE-2026-48939 vulnerability matrix to flag exposed instances. No version limits provided in article—assume all versions below patch date are at risk.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Extension Upload Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'dangerous type' and 'arbitrary files' but does not specify which extensions are weaponized. Need detection for polyglot uploads and double-extension bypasses (.php.jpg, .htaccess, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP uploads with executable or server-directive extensions in filename (.php, .phtml, .php3, .jsp, .asp, .exe, .sh, .htaccess). Also catch polyglot techniques: double extensions, null byte injection, case mismatch (.PHP, .pHp). Baseline allowed types by iCagenda config and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Post-Upload HTTP Request Execution Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article describes upload leading to 'execution'—need correlated detection of HTTP GET/POST to newly uploaded file + non-standard user agent / short time delta suggesting automated exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful file upload (HTTP 201/200 to upload endpoint) with subsequent HTTP request to the uploaded file path within 10 seconds. Flag requests with automated user agents (curl, wget, Python-requests) or encoded payloads in GET params. This indicates immediate post-upload execution by attacker tooling.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vuln Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV, federal patch due 2026-07-13—only UC provided in article is a scanner check. Pipeline must emit scanner-based detections as baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-48939 findings. Filter by asset criticality and exposure (internet-facing, DMZ). Prioritize iCagenda instances with patch date < 2026-07-13. Triage by days-to-breach (patch due date minus today) to drive remediation urgency.

suggestion.title: Detect Unrestricted File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' — no generated detection for upload endpoint abuse or dangerous file-type ingestion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda file-attachment endpoints for anomalous file extensions (PHP, PHTML, PHP3-PHP7, PHAR, PHPS) or Content-Type/filename mismatches. Flag uploads where filename extension contradicts declared MIME type (e.g., Content-Type: image/jpeg with .php extension).

suggestion.title: Detect PHP Code Execution Following File Upload to iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution' — no use case for PHP file creation in web roots or HTTP access to uploaded files within execution window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PHP file-write events to web-accessible directories (uploads/, attachments/, /var/www/html/*, C:\inetpub\*) with HTTP GET/POST requests to those files returning 200 status within 60 seconds. Escalate if request payload or response body contains shell metacharacters or eval patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Scanner Correlation and Asset Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV = active exploitation + federal patch deadline (2026-07-13). Article names CVE but no inventory hunt or scanner-correlation workflow generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scanners (Qualys, Nessus, Rapid7, Tenable) for CVE-2026-48939 detections. Cross-reference with asset inventory to locate all iCagenda installations (process names, open ports, HTTP headers). Escalate any critical finding not yet patched by federal deadline to incident queue.

suggestion.title: Detect Web Shell Post-Exploitation Behavior (PHP Execution Context)
suggestion.rationale: Post-upload PHP shells typically spawn reconnaissance processes (whoami, ls, cat /etc/passwd, ifconfig). Article does not describe post-shell activity, but upload-to-RCE chain warrants detection of child process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when web server processes (w3wp.exe, apache, php-fpm, httpd) spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh as children, especially following recent PHP file creation. Monitor for PHP system() / shell_exec() / passthru() calls with arguments containing whoami, id, uname, dir, ls, env, or /etc/passwd reads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Upload to iCagenda Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Pipeline missed the execution vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda attachment upload endpoints for POST requests with .php or .phtml payloads, or double-extension obfuscation (e.g., .php.jpg). Correlate with HTTP 200 responses indicating successful upload. Cross-reference with subsequent GET requests to the uploaded file path.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Web Shell Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain concludes with 'PHP code upload and execution' but pipeline omitted post-compromise detection. Web shells enable command execution.

suggestion.title: Newly-Published Crate Installed Before Abuse Removal

suggestion.title: Proxy Authentication Header Injection from Unexpected Network Path
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker sends 'forged HTTP header' and 'any unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server directly can impersonate any user.' suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FileBrowser endpoints for HTTP requests containing proxy authentication headers (X-Remote-User, X-Remote-Groups, REMOTE_USER, etc.) originating from IP addresses that bypass the reverse proxy. Correlate with absence of request in proxy logs for same timestamp. Flag any direct-path connection with these headers as forged authentication attempt.

suggestion.title: Successful Admin Impersonation via Proxy Header Forgery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'impersonate any user - including admin' as primary impact. Detection must identify when admin-level operations occur from non-admin accounts or unexpected network sources via forged headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication to FileBrowser admin endpoints (/api/settings, /api/users, resource management) from a source that either: (a) previously failed authentication within 5 min, (b) shows no prior admin activity pattern, or (c) correlates with presence of proxy auth headers in direct connection. suggestion.title: Automatic User Account Creation Without Authentication Event
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'specifying a non-existent username causes the server to automatically create a new user account' — this is the persistence mechanism. Need to detect orphaned account creation events not preceded by legitimate admin action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FileBrowser logs or audit events for account creation events (POST to /api/users with HTTP 201, or equivalent account add events). Flag any creation not preceded by authenticated admin action from expected management IPs. Spike detection: more than 3 new accounts created in 1 hour from same source IP outside normal provisioning windows.

suggestion.title: Session Context Confusion: Multiple User Impersonations from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Core attack allows impersonation of 'any user' via forged headers. Behavioral detection should flag rapid user-context switching from single network source, indicating header injection rather than legitimate multi-user access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify single source IP accessing FileBrowser API endpoints as 3+ different user identities within 5-minute window. Especially high-fidelity if: (a) users include admin account, (b) normal activity for those users is segregated by IP/time, or (c) requests use same session/cookie but different auth headers.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Proxy Auth Configuration Exposure via Failed Auth Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability only exploitable when 'configured with proxy authentication (auth.method=proxy).' Attackers probe for this via direct connections and observing auth behavior differences.
