suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed iCagenda Instance Inventory and Patch Gap Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation of 'file attachment feature' in iCagenda. Federal patch due 2026-07-13. Requires rapid identification of unpatched instances before exploitation. Vulnerable instances exposed via CMDB and public reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query infrastructure CMDB for all iCagenda deployments. Cross-reference with scanner results for CVE-2026-48939 status. Supplement with external Shodan/Censys queries (HTTP response banners, /index.php fingerprints) to locate internet-exposed instances not in internal inventory.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Execution Post-Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'PHP code upload and execution' as the exploitation outcome. Successful file upload must correlate with command execution. Critical post-compromise behavioral indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful PHP file uploads to iCagenda with process execution events where www-data/apache/httpd parent spawns bash/sh/cmd.exe children. Flag time-proximate events (same second) as shell deployment indicators. Cross-reference against known bad file hashes if PoCs are published.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation File Enumeration via Web Shell
suggestion.rationale: Following shell upload and execution, attackers typically enumerate filesystem paths. Article implies post-compromise persistence/discovery activity through uploaded PHP code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt iCagenda access logs for unusual GET requests post-upload to path traversal endpoints (/../, ..\\), sensitive file patterns (/etc/passwd, /proc/self/, Windows system directories), or base64/hex-encoded shell commands in query parameters.

suggestion.title: Detect jscrambler 8.14.0 Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names compromised version 8.14.0; detection must baseline the vulnerable package version in npm audit trails and package manager logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install and package manager logs for jscrambler version 8.14.0. Alert on any successful installation of this version. Cross-correlate with DeviceFileEvents for node_modules extraction to identify affected machines.

suggestion.title: Detect Unsigned Binary Execution from npm Package Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states infostealer 'drops' and executes during install, implying postinstall script triggers a binary; Rust infostealer would be unsigned or self-signed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or non-Microsoft signed .exe/.elf execution spawned by npm/node processes with working directory in node_modules/jscrambler or npm temp directories. Alert on Rust-compiled binaries (characteristic entropy/sections) executing with network access.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious Postinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromises typically inject malicious postinstall scripts in package.json or .bin wrappers; article implies execution during install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm postinstall hook execution (node_modules/.bin executables, package.json scripts during npm install) for jscrambler. Alert on process chains: npm → node → unexpected executable (especially Rust/compiled binaries or shell interpreters downloading remote payloads).

suggestion.title: Detect Data Exfiltration from Infostealer C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Rust Infostealer' which by definition collects and exfiltrates data; identify C2 domains or IP ranges the malware beacons to.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from node_modules/jscrambler or child processes of npm install for beaconing behavior or known infostealer C2 domains. Alert on unusual TLS/DNS patterns or connections to non-standard ports from npm processes.

suggestion.title: Detect jscrambler Postinstall Script Anomalies via AST
suggestion.rationale: Compromised npm packages often obfuscate malicious postinstall code in package.json scripts field; article confirms payload delivery via install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse jscrambler package.json scripts for suspicious patterns: base64 decoding, shell command evaluation, download commands, or process spawning. Alert on deviations from legitimate jscrambler behavior (validate against clean baseline of jscrambler <8.14.0).

suggestion.title: Detect Infostealer Credential/Browser Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Rust infostealers typically target user credentials, browser cookies, SSH keys, and environment variables; article does not detail targets but supply-chain context implies broad collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file access patterns from jscrambler child processes targeting ~/.ssh, ~/.bash_history, ~/.config/chromium, APPDATA\Local\Google\Chrome, credential stores, and environment variable dumps. Alert on bulk reads of sensitive paths followed by network exfil.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawned During npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malicious preinstall binary'—preinstall hooks execute arbitrary code before package setup completes. This is the core attack vector but no execution detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation with parent process npm/node where child spawns binaries outside standard package paths. Focus on sh/powershell spawning unexpected executables during install phase (detectable via npm start/preinstall timing and environment variables).

suggestion.title: npm Registry Package Hash Mismatch or Integrity Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes registry-level compromise ('npm package publishes')—requires detection of package.json.lock mismatches, version downgrades, or checksums diverging from official registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm_audit_logs for unexpected publish events by unusual accounts; correlate local package checksums against npm registry SHA-256 hashes; flag installations from non-standard registries or mirror services.

suggestion.title: Binary Execution from npm node_modules or Cache Directory
suggestion.rationale: Preinstall downloads/stages malicious binary to filesystem. No detection for binary execution within .npm or node_modules/.bin directories, despite article's central focus on binary execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of PE/ELF/Mach-O binaries originating from node_modules/.bin, ~/.npm, or %APPDATA%/npm cache. Flag unexpected file writes to these directories during npm install, especially from preinstall-spawned processes.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connection During npm Preinstall Phase
suggestion.rationale: Malicious preinstall binary likely establishes C2 or exfiltrates data. Article title indicates 'malicious' but zero network-based detection guidance; no IOCs (C2 domains, IPs) extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and TCP/UDP connections initiated by npm, node, sh, or preinstall-spawned child processes to non-CDN destinations during package installation window. Baseline npm registry/CDN endpoints and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via npm Preinstall Running as Root/SYSTEM
suggestion.rationale: Preinstall hooks often run with elevated privileges in CI/Docker contexts. If malicious binary gains root, detection should cover system-level persistence (cron, systemd, kernel modules)—not covered despite 'malicious' payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag preinstall execution with UID 0 or NT AUTHORITY/SYSTEM. Monitor for writes to /etc/cron.d, /etc/systemd/system, /usr/bin, or SSH config from elevated preinstall processes. Correlate with package install events.

suggestion.title: Persistence Installation via cron, systemd, or launchd from Preinstall Hook
suggestion.rationale: Malicious binaries typically establish persistence. Article describes 'malicious' payload but no detection for scheduler job creation, system service installation, or launch agent modification post-install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cron job, systemd unit, or launchd plist creation during or within hours of npm package installation. Flag scheduled tasks executing binaries from user directories or npm cache. Monitor /var/spool/cron, /etc/cron.*, /etc/systemd/system, ~/.config/systemd, /Library/LaunchAgents.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution Spawned from Zimbra/Email Process
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: crafted emails 'run malicious code in user sessions'—pipeline should detect script interpreters, shells, or compiled executables spawned by mail process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when PowerShell, cmd.exe, or script interpreter launches as direct/indirect child of Zimbra mail process or web worker. Baseline legitimate email workflows; flag interactive shells, system-level commands, or encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Exploit Payload Targeting Zimbra
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability triggered by 'crafted emails'—detect email delivery containing suspicious MIME structures, script attachments, or malformed message components known to trigger Zimbra parsing vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with suspicious MIME types, double-encoded payloads, or embedded scripts (JS, VBS, PS1). Correlate email receipt timestamp with subsequent process execution or error spikes in Zimbra server logs.

suggestion.title: Post-Email Network Beaconing or C2 from Compromised User Session
suggestion.rationale: Code execution in session implies attacker obtains shell/agent within user context—expect outbound C2 or data exfiltration shortly after email delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish timeline from email ingestion to first suspicious outbound connection from affected user's host. Alert on anomalous protocols, non-whitelisted destinations, or DNS queries to known-malicious domains within 5min of email processing.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation or Lateral Movement Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once code runs in user session, attacker typically escalates or pivots. Watch for UAC bypass, token impersonation, or unexpected SYSTEM/admin-context processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege-escalation techniques (e.g., BITS jobs, scheduled tasks, COM object elevation) initiated from email-triggered process tree. Alert on process running under unexpected SID/context minutes after mail delivery.

suggestion.title: Zimbra Server MIME Parsing Error Correlated with Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability likely triggered by malformed MIME or script-interpretation logic in Zimbra—server-side error logs and execution patterns are key indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual MIME parsing failures, unexpected file writes to Zimbra folders, or script execution attempts in mailbox processing pipeline. Correlate server-side errors with client-side process execution on subscriber hosts.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Encryption Activity - Bulk File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title references ransomware operations and impact; core attack signature completely missing from pipeline output despite 'Gentlemen' being an active threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-velocity file modifications with cryptographic patterns (>.1MB/sec writes), mass extension changes to .locked/.crypt/.encrypted, and simultaneous creation of text ransom notes across multiple directories.

suggestion.title: RaaS C2 Beacon and Affiliate Management Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly include 'RaaS' and 'affiliate model'; no C2 detection provided despite this being foundational to ransomware operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS/DNS beaconing to known RaaS panels, TOR hidden services, and dead-drop resolvers; correlate with process execution from system32 and LDAP enumeration.

suggestion.title: Pre-Encryption Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Modern RaaS ops steal before encrypting; article describes 'ruthless' operations but no exfiltration detection. Should detect archive creation + egress to non-business IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large outbound transfers (>500MB) to suspicious IPs in same window as 7z/rar/zip tool execution; alert on unusual SMB share access (>1000 files/min) followed by compression.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Admin Credential Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware targeting hospitality/retail requires domain-wide pivot; no lateral-movement detections despite being kill-chain requirement for enterprise impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PSEXEC/RDP logons from non-admin-workstations using high-privilege service accounts; flag SMB signing disabled + enumeration of backup/shadow-copy paths.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion - Event Log Clearing
suggestion.rationale: RaaS operators sanitize forensic artifacts before encryption; no evasion-phase detections despite this being standard TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wevtutil/Get-EventLog deletion commands, especially targeting Security/System logs. Flag process execution shortly before ransom-note filesystem activity.

suggestion.title: Management API privilege escalation via forwarded auth token
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'enables management API escalation' but no UC detects successful privilege escalation. Gap: missing detection for management API calls (e.g., POST /api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/rbac/roles) made with injected forwarded token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor management API endpoints (/api/v1/admin/*, /api/v1/rbac/*) accessed via loopback (127.0.0.1:8080) and observe if response codes indicate privilege escalation (e.g., 200 OK responses for account creation, role assignment that would normally return 403). Correlate with non-tsdproxy process names initiating requests.

suggestion.title: Token forwarding to external/non-loopback backend services
suggestion.rationale: Article describes token forwarded 'to all proxied backend services'—misses detection of legitimate backend services that incorrectly receive x-tsdproxy-auth-token headers. Lateral movement vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for x-tsdproxy-auth-token or x-tsdproxy-id headers in HTTP requests to destinations outside loopback (RemoteIP != 127.0.0.1). Flag as suspicious if backend service requests are made by non-service accounts or from unusual source IPs. Escalate if backend service responds with success (2xx status).

suggestion.title: Default identityHeaders=true configuration reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is default-enabled; article doesn't describe how to detect if a TSDProxy instance has identityHeaders enabled. Missing UC for checking/listing endpoints that haven't patched or disabled the setting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for TSDProxy processes spawned with identityHeaders enabled (check for 'identityHeaders=true' or absence of 'identityHeaders=false' in runtime config or startup logs). Can also fingerprint by probing for predictable header presence: send request to loopback :8080 and observe if response includes echo of x-tsdproxy-auth-token header or similar identity headers.

suggestion.title: Stolen auth token replay to backend management endpoints
suggestion.rationale: T1528 (Steal Application Access Token) is mapped but no UC detects stolen token being replayed outside original context. Gap: detect when x-tsdproxy-auth-token value appears in requests to unusual destinations or at unusual times.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract x-tsdproxy-auth-token values from network traffic and monitor for reuse across multiple backend services or external systems. Flag if same token value appears in requests from different source IPs or at times inconsistent with normal proxy operation. Alert on token replay to sensitive endpoints (/admin, /rbac, /config).

suggestion.title: Proxy configuration exposure via debugging endpoints
suggestion.rationale: UC_8_2 mentions /debug/headers endpoint but doesn't explain how adversary accesses/leverages it. Gap: missing detection for access to dangerous debug/info endpoints that could leak proxy configuration and running tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to known debug endpoints (/debug/*, /info, /health, /status) on management API port (8080). Escalate if response includes proxy configuration (identityHeaders setting), active token values, or service inventory. Correlate with non-service-account source IPs or unusual hours.

suggestion.title: TSDProxy token exfiltration via HTTP logging/caching
suggestion.rationale: Article describes token forwarded in headers; tokens may be logged by intermediary services, cached by proxies, or persisted in access logs. Gap: detect token values appearing in logs/caches they shouldn't (e.g., /var/log, .bash_history, browser cache) accessible to unprivileged users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for x-tsdproxy-auth-token* values written to world-readable log files, cache directories, or temporary storage. Track file reads by non-tsdproxy processes that access logs containing the token. Alert if token value appears in /var/log, /tmp, or .bash_history accessible to non-privileged accounts.

suggestion.title: Malicious XSS Payload Content in Attribute-View JSON Store
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exact payload patterns: `
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search av/*.json files written in last 7 days, extract and parse JSON, look for cell values containing HTML escape sequences (\u003c, \u003e), script tags, event handler attributes (onerror, onload, onclick), or common XSS payloads. Flag any containing `img src` or event attributes.

suggestion.title: Electron Renderer Process Network Callback (C2 or Exfil)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'On Electron desktop the renderer...' can execute code. If XSS succeeds and attacker establishes C2 from within renderer process, outbound connection will originate from SiYuan renderer subprocess, not main process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections where InitiatingProcessFileName=SiYuan.exe AND ProcessCommandLine contains 'renderer' OR parent process is SiYuan.exe but executable is a child spawned with unusual network activity. Baseline legitimate SiYuan network activity first.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JSON Attribute-View Cell Containing HTML Breakout Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article example: cell value contains `</textarea>` or `">` that 'breaks out of its surrounding tag'. These are specific markers of attempt to escape HTML context. Detection should trigger on cell creation/modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Real-time monitoring of av/*.json file writes. Parse modified files and search all cell value strings for unencoded HTML delimiters: `<`, `>`, `"`, or common attribute patterns like ` on` (onerror, onclick, etc.). Flag any before SiYuan parses them.

suggestion.title: SiYuan Attribute-View Block Opening with Suspicious Cell Content
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires 'victim opens the block-attribute panel'. Application-level logging should track when attribute views are rendered and flag if cells contain unescaped HTML or script payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If SiYuan logging available, hunt for attribute-view block open events followed by genAVValueHTML() calls on cells containing script tags or event handlers. Can be supplemented by Electron DevTools breakpoint monitoring if available.

suggestion.title: Preload Script or NodeIntegration Configuration Access from Unexpected Process
suggestion.rationale: Electron nodeIntegration is the bridge from XSS to RCE. Article implies this is the attack surface. Detect tampering with preload files or nodeIntegration config by processes other than SiYuan installer/updater.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for read/write access to Electron preload script paths (typically in app/preload.js or main.js) and registry keys controlling nodeIntegration (HKEY_CURRENT_USER\...). Flag access by non-SiYuan processes, especially script interpreters.

suggestion.title: Attribute-View Database File Exfiltration After XSS Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE via nodeIntegration could allow attacker to exfiltrate the entire database. Monitor for mass reads of av/*.json files followed by outbound file transfer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate: file read events on av/*.json (high volume in short time) -> followed by -> network connection from SiYuan or child process to external IP (non-trusted). Look for patterns consistent with tar/zip + curl or similar.

suggestion.title: iCagenda PHP File Upload to Web Root Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution' — the file-upload endpoint is the critical attack surface for T1190 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda file attachment endpoints (identify via patched version release notes or version disclosure) for PHP code signatures: .php/.phtml/.phar extensions, <?php tags, base64-encoded PHP, polyglot image+PHP files. Flag unusual Content-Type mismatches or double-extension uploads.

suggestion.title: PHP Web Shell Execution in Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'PHP code upload and execution' — post-upload execution must be detected via access logs or process spawning patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP GET/POST requests to .php files within known iCagenda upload directories (typically ./uploads/, ./media/, ./cache/). Correlate with abnormal web server process spawning (php.exe, php-cgi creating child processes). High confidence if request follows detected file-upload attempt within seconds.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Web Shell Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Active CISA KEV exploitation typically proceeds to command execution; article describes PHP execution capability but not post-exploitation behavior — standard persistence/C2 hunting applies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests containing command patterns (GET params with shell metacharacters, base64 blobs, PowerShell/bash encoded strings). Monitor outbound connections from web server process (curl, wget, nc spawned from php). Track unusual DNS queries or reverse-DNS lookups from web server IP.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scan Coverage
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries mandate remediation by due date (2026-07-13 per article); baseline scan coverage is non-negotiable for federal/regulated environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily scans for iCagenda instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-48939. Prioritize by: (1) exposure to internet, (2) version string in HTTP headers, (3) file-attachment feature accessibility. Alert on unpatched instances within 3 days of scan date. Track remediation elapsed time against due-date policy.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-48939. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this being the entry point. CISA KEV entries are actively exploited; scanner coverage is a primary defensive response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner output for detections of CVE-2026-48939 (iCagenda unrestricted upload) across internet-facing assets. Alert on any matched systems regardless of patch status, as CISA KEV implies active exploitation in the wild and patch lag is a known risk.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets' and recommends 'asset-exposure hunt.' Pipeline failed to generate a basic web application exposure detection for iCagenda instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for iCagenda application banners, URIs (/icagenda*, /calendar*), or HTTP fingerprints in internet-facing traffic and web logs. Cross-reference asset inventory to identify unpatched or unmanaged iCagenda deployments exposed to the internet.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Upload to iCagenda
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core vulnerability: 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature.' No upload-based detection UC was generated. File upload is the exploit mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file upload endpoints for unusual file types (especially .php, .phtml, .php3, .phar, executables). Alert on uploads where file extension does not match content-type or where uploads occur outside documented maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack outcome: 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' This is the impact phase; pipeline missed this post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file uploads to iCagenda with subsequent PHP execution, process spawning, or outbound connections from the web server. Look for web server (Apache, nginx) child processes executing commands or accessing unexpected resources shortly after an upload event.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Error/Access Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV (actively exploited). Reconnaissance and attack attempts will precede successful exploitation. No proactive hunt for iCagenda access anomalies was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal access patterns to iCagenda instances and alert on deviations: unusual file upload request rates, 4xx errors on upload endpoints, requests from unexpected geolocations or IPs, or attempts to access file attachment features from non-browser user agents.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Upload to Web Root — PHP Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' and 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution'. Pipeline generated zero detection use cases for this attack flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file attachment upload endpoints for POST requests followed by HTTP 200/201 responses containing .php file writes to web-accessible directories (e.g., uploads/, media/). Correlate with subsequent PHP execution (interpreter spawning, command execution from web process context).

suggestion.title: Unexpected PHP Process Execution from Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Code execution is the exploited capability ('resulting in PHP code upload and execution'). Pipeline failed to propose detection for post-upload execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP/apache/httpd/nginx processes spawning child processes (cmd.exe, bash, sh, powershell) or accessing network sockets from paths matching typical upload directories. Correlate parent process start time with recent file modifications in those directories.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Type Restriction Bypass — Non-Image in Attachment
suggestion.rationale: 'Unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' and 'upload of arbitrary files' indicates file-type validation was bypassed. Pipeline did not propose detection for malformed uploads.
log_sources: IIS / Apache logs with Content-Type headers
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file attachment uploads where Content-Type/file extension mismatch or dangerous MIME types (application/x-php, application/x-executable, etc.) are submitted to the attachment endpoint. Baseline expected file types for legitimate use.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Exploitation Pattern — Known Vulnerable iCagenda Versions
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal patch deadline 2026-07-13. Pipeline extracted no CVE indicator despite it being primary IOC for this threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query your vulnerability scanner or asset-management system for iCagenda installations with versions ≤ [unpatched version per CISA advisory]. Correlate with network traffic to known iCagenda endpoints (e.g., /component/icagenda/). Flag any instances not yet patched as of due date 2026-07-13.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence Post-Exploitation — iCagenda Upload Dir Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: After successful PHP upload-and-execution, attacker typically maintains access via web shell. Article does not preclude persistence; pipeline ignored post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload directories for repeated access to recently-created files with suspicious naming patterns (single letters, common web-shell names like shell.php, admin.php, test.php). Detect encoded PHP or obfuscated function calls in accessible files.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Extension Upload to iCagenda Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Pipeline generated no detection for this core initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda file upload endpoints for POST/PUT requests containing dangerous file extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3-7, .phar, .inc, .jsp, .asp, .aspx, .exe, .bat, .cmd, .com, .sh) or MIME-type mismatches indicating file-type evasion. Alert on successful uploads of executable extensions to iCagenda attachment directories.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution in Web-Accessible Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution.' Pipeline did not create any detection for the execution phase, missing the second half of the attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful file uploads to iCagenda with PHP process spawning or php.exe execution within 60 seconds. Alert on execution of newly created PHP files in web-accessible directories (/uploads, /attachments, /tmp, web root) tied to recent HTTP POST requests.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Vulnerability Asset Discovery and Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries require vulnerability scanning correlation. Article specifies federal patch due date 2026-07-13. Pipeline failed to extract CVE-2026-48939 as a scannable indicator for asset-inventory correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management and asset systems for iCagenda instances. Verify all identified instances against CVE-2026-48939 patch status. Generate alerts for unpatched instances or those with unknown patch status within the federal remediation window (due 2026-07-13). Cross-reference with network footprint to identify exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Abnormal HTTP POST Activity to iCagenda Upload Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability is exploited via 'the file attachment feature' — a web-facing upload mechanism. Pipeline generated no use case targeting the initial exploitation HTTP activity itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT requests to iCagenda upload endpoints from untrusted sources (external IPs, non-corporate networks). Flag high-volume upload attempts, requests with payloads containing PHP code, or repeated requests to the same endpoint suggesting reconnaissance or exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Active Exploitation Behavior Pattern
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation means active in-the-wild exploitation. Pipeline provided no hunt templates incorporating this specific CVE's exploitation signature (file upload + executable execution pipeline).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build correlated detection: (1) POST to iCagenda upload endpoint with dangerous file extension + (2) PHP/scripting process execution in web directory within 120 seconds of upload = likely exploitation. Monitor for this behavior pattern as a composite signal of CVE-2026-48939 exploitation.

suggestion.title: iCagenda File Upload to Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature'—the core attack vector. Pipeline generated zero use cases to detect malicious uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to iCagenda upload endpoints (typically /component/icagenda/upload or /index.php?option=com_icagenda&task=upload). Alert on file creation events in web-accessible directories within seconds of upload, especially for executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .phar, .phps).

suggestion.title: PHP Execution After Upload — Webshell Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution'—execution of uploaded PHP is the impact phase. No UC targets HTTP requests to newly-uploaded PHP files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST to upload endpoint with subsequent HTTP GET/POST requests to .php files in upload directories, within same session/source IP. Alert on suspicious POST parameters or shell-like commands (cmd, exec, system, passthru) in query strings.

suggestion.title: File Type Validation Bypass — Dangerous File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type'—the vulnerability is the bypass of file type controls. This attack pattern is not covered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when .php or other executable extensions are written to iCagenda upload directories even though the Content-Type header in the POST request indicates a benign type (e.g., image/jpeg). Cross-check MIME type vs actual file extension on disk.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Asset Discovery — Vulnerable Instance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV template mandates asset-exposure hunt. Pipeline generated zero detection for unpatched iCagenda instances. Article references federal patch deadline (2026-07-13).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate web servers for iCagenda installation signatures (e.g., /administrator/index.php?option=com_icagenda, /media/com_icagenda). Correlate with vulnerability scanner results and CMDB patch status. Flag instances older than 2026-07-13 as requiring immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Web-to-Process Execution Chain — PHP Spawned Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Uploaded PHP executing arbitrary code will spawn child processes (shell, commands, reverse shells). Article states 'execution' as outcome but no UC detects this execution artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when w3wp.exe, apache2, php-cgi, or other web-service processes spawn suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, nc.exe, bash, sh, wget, curl) shortly after file-write events to iCagenda directories. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify iCagenda instances on the network via HTTP GET requests to fingerprinting paths (/administrator/index.php, /components/com_icagenda/readme.txt). Cross-reference with vulnerability-scanner output for CVE-2026-48939 matches. Alert on any unpatched instances (CVSS 9+, federal due-date 2026-07-13) as immediate remediation candidates.

suggestion.title: MIME Type Mismatch / Content-Type Bypass in Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unrestricted upload…with dangerous type'—pipeline should detect common bypass techniques (MIME-type mismatch, null-byte, case variation, htaccess upload) that evade basic upload filters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST with Content-Type mismatch vs. filename extension (Content-Type: image/png, filename: shell.php). Flag uploads of .htaccess files to web-root directories. Alert on requests with null-byte injection (shell.php%00.jpg) or case-variation attempts (shell.PHP, shell.PhP) to iCagenda upload paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Match + Unseen Patching
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with active exploitation; article provides CVE, vendor, and federal due-date but pipeline produced zero IOC linking asset-scan findings to remediation timeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner database for CVE-2026-48939 matches (iCagenda version < [patched version]). Cross-correlate with asset inventory and patch-management systems to identify systems past the federal due-date (2026-07-13). Generate high-priority ticket for any host with confirmed unpatched status.

suggestion.title: iCagenda CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerable Instance Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'iCagenda contains an unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability'—requires asset inventory of all exposed iCagenda instances via banner grabbing or version fingerprinting
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-48939 matches or identify iCagenda instances via HTTP banner matching 'iCagenda', Server header identification, or directory enumeration (/index.php?view=calendar). Baseline all public-facing iCagenda instances and compare against patch status.

suggestion.title: PHP File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload'—detection must catch .php, .phtml, .php3+ extensions in upload requests to iCagenda endpoints
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda file attachment endpoints (typically /component/icagenda/controllers/ajax* or upload handlers). Flag requests where Content-Type field contains 'application/x-php' or 'text/plain' alongside .php/.phtml/.php3/.php4/.php5/.phar extensions. Calculate upload-to-access time delta to identify immediate exploitation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Process Execution from Web-Accessible Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article concludes with 'resulting in PHP code upload and execution'—must detect process execution post-upload in web root directories, indicating successful exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe or php-fpm process spawning from /upload*, /attachment*, /tmp*, or other web-accessible directories. Correlate with recent POST requests to iCagenda endpoints. Monitor for child processes spawned by PHP interpreter indicating code execution (curl, wget, nc, cmd.exe, bash, git, etc.).

suggestion.title: iCagenda Attachment Upload Directory Traversal or Staging Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Unrestricted upload without type validation is confirmed—need detection for directory traversal payloads (../, ..\) or files staged but not yet executed
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search web server logs and WAF telemetry for POST requests to iCagenda file upload endpoints containing path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e/, URL-encoded variants). Flag multipart/form-data payloads with suspicious Content-Disposition filenames targeting directories outside intended upload path.

suggestion.title: Web Server Error Spike Following iCagenda File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Successful PHP upload should result in HTTP 2xx responses; failed exploits or detected attacks may correlate with 4xx/5xx errors indicating WAF block or execution failure
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline HTTP response codes for iCagenda upload endpoints. Alert on anomalies: sudden spike in 400/403/413 (file rejected/blocked), 500 (execution error), or suspicious 200/201 followed by unusual User-Agent, source geo, or request rate deviations.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell / Callback from iCagenda Server Post-Upload
suggestion.rationale: Once PHP code executes, attacker typically establishes persistent access—outbound connections from iCagenda server to known C2 or unexpected external IPs post-upload indicate compromise
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate iCagenda upload requests with outbound network connections from the web server within 30 seconds. Flag connections to non-approved external IP addresses, non-standard ports (targeting reverse shell ports like 4444, 5555, 9999), or DNS queries for known C2 domains originating from web server process context.

suggestion.title: Detect PHP File Upload to iCagenda Attachment Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature, ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'. Pipeline missed the upload phase entirely—.php/.phtml file creation in upload paths is the delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda attachment directories for creation of executable file types (.php, .phtml, .php3, .php5, .pht, .shtml). High fidelity requires correlation with web access logs showing POST requests to upload endpoints immediately preceding file creation.

suggestion.title: Detect Process Execution Originating from Web Application Upload Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ultimately resulting in PHP code upload and execution'. Process spawn from web-accessible upload folders (php.exe parent = web server) indicates post-exploitation code activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or apache process spawning with working directory or image path within web application upload trees. Correlate parent process identity (apache2, w3wp.exe, nginx) and command-line arguments for suspicious inclusions (system, shell_exec, passthru).

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious POST to iCagenda Component Upload Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies exploit vector as 'file attachment feature'. HTTP POST to component upload handlers followed by unexpected file creation establishes exploit chain from initial access through delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP POST/PUT requests to common iCagenda attachment endpoints (e.g., /component/icagenda/*, /images/icagenda/*) with executable-type Content-Disposition or MIME types. Correlate with 2xx HTTP response codes and subsequent file creation events to detect exploitation.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: iCagenda Instances Vulnerable to CVE-2026-48939

suggestion.title: File Upload to iCagenda with Suspicious Extension

suggestion.title: PHP Process Execution from Web Upload Directory

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST success (200 response) to iCagenda upload endpoint with PHP process creation (php.exe, php-cgi) within 5 seconds, spawned from /upload, /attachment, /files, or /temp directories. Multiple instances in short timeframe = active exploitation.

suggestion.rationale: After exploitation, attackers may remove the malicious package or force user updates. Pipeline should detect unexpected package removal or version rollback patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm uninstall or package deletion events in rapid succession after preinstall hook execution. Alert on npm cache purges or selective node_modules deletions that suggest cleanup post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Rust Binary Execution from node_modules
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload that 'drops during install'—npm supply chains commonly stage executables in node_modules or cache. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection entirely.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file creation in web-accessible upload directories with PHP process execution (php.exe, php-cgi) sourcing that file within 0–5 minutes. Alert on unexpected parent processes (w3wp.exe, httpd, nginx) spawning PHP interpreters reading from recent uploads.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Artifact Detection in iCagenda Upload Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article implies persistent execution via uploaded PHP—pipeline missed hunt for web shell indicators (base64_decode, eval, $_GET, $_POST, passthru) in upload directory post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan iCagenda upload directory for PHP files with creation timestamps post-2026-07-10, obfuscated variable names ($a, $_, base64_), and known webshell signatures. Flag files with <200 bytes of recognizable source or large base64 blocks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-48939 as exploit IOC—pipeline failed to create baseline hunt: vulnerability scanner flagging iCagenda as unpatched for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any asset inventory entry identifying iCagenda product with CVE-2026-48939 unpatched status. Cross-reference with web proxy logs for iCagenda-specific signatures or known admin paths from external sources.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Endpoint Probing and Upload Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'unrestricted upload'—attackers probe endpoints before exploit. Pipeline missed detection for failed uploads (403, 405, 413) followed by successful upload, indicating bypass enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor iCagenda upload endpoints for sequences of failed HTTP responses (405 Method Not Allowed, 413 Payload Too Large, 403 Forbidden) followed by success (200/201). Flag repeated requests with variant file extensions (.php, .php5, .phtml, .phar) in same session.

suggestion.title: iCagenda Arbitrary File Upload to Web Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'allows the upload of arbitrary files in the file attachment feature' — this is the initial exploitation vector and must be detected at the upload boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to iCagenda file-upload endpoints (*/uploads/*, */attachments/*, */media/*) for suspicious file extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3, .phar) or MIME type mismatches (e.g., application/x-php uploaded as image/jpeg).

suggestion.title: PHP Webshell Creation via iCagenda Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'PHP code upload and execution' — detection must capture the file-system write of executable PHP to web-accessible paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of .php, .php3, .phtml files in document root or iCagenda subdirectories (esp. */uploads/*, */cache/*) within seconds of POST requests to upload endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48939 Exploitation Attempt Pattern
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries are in-the-wild exploitation; pattern-based detection on known exploit attempts or vulnerable endpoint signatures is standard for actively-exploited vulns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline iCagenda file-attachment request patterns and flag requests matching known exploitation signatures (e.g., multipart uploads with executable MIME types, POST payloads from public exploit PoCs).

suggestion.title: Post-Upload PHP Execution via HTTP GET
suggestion.rationale: After webshell upload, attacker invokes it via GET; detecting the HTTP request + subsequent child-process spawn closes the execution detection loop.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP GET requests to recently-uploaded .php files (within last 5 min) with child-process spawning (bash, curl, powershell) by the web server process (httpd, apache2, php-fpm).

suggestion.title: iCagenda Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-13' — asset detection and patch-status validation must run immediately for actively-exploited vulns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and banner-grab iCagenda instances to confirm version >= [patched]; flag unpatched instances for immediate remediation and enhanced monitoring.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation – Miasma Variant Hashes
suggestion.rationale: Article headline indicates npm packages were compromised; pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Should detect installation of AsyncAPI packages with known-malicious file hashes or version identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/package.json resolution for AsyncAPI package versions tagged as compromised. Correlate against known Miasma variant SHA256 hashes from advisory. Alert if package-lock.json or node_modules contains flagged hashes.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise – Malicious npm Registry Request Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states AsyncAPI packages were compromised; implies attackers modified packages on npm registry. Detect unusual registry queries or package fetch behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify npm registry requests to atypical mirrors, or package.json references to alternative registries (e.g., non-official npm.js URLs). Correlate package names against AsyncAPI CVE/advisory list.

suggestion.title: Miasma Malware Execution – Dropper / Post-Install Script Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Miasma variant introduced via npm package; likely executes via install scripts (postinstall hooks). Article likely describes execution payload but not extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install/postinstall scripts spawning PowerShell, bash, or native binaries with suspicious arguments (e.g., curl/wget to C2, file enumeration, registry access). Flag unusual child processes from node.exe.

suggestion.title: Miasma C2 Beaconing – Exfiltration to Known Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Malware family name 'Miasma' implies specific TTPs; article likely identifies C2 domains/IPs not extracted by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from processes spawned by npm postinstall to known Miasma C2 domains/IPs. Flag DNS queries to infrastructure associated with threat actor.

suggestion.title: Sanctioned VPN Service C&C Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'VPN Service' involvement in ransomware support operations. Pipeline extracted no C&C or network-anonymization detections. Phrase: 'Sanctions First VPN Service...Over Ransomware Support'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections to known-sanctioned VPN provider domains or ASNs with ransomware-typical patterns (sustained connection during high disk I/O, correlation with file-read loops). Flag VPN tunnel establishment followed by bulk network discovery.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Encryption Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Malware Cryptor Seller'—a supplier of encryption utilities for ransomware deployment. Pipeline produced no cryptography-tool or ransomware-execution detections despite 'crit' severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of known cryptor binaries (e.g., rclone, legitdisk) or unsigned process spawn of file encryption utilities. Correlate with high-volume sequential file opens, .exe/.dll file enumeration, and child-process chains from data-staging tools.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note Creation & Bulk File Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware attacks inherently produce ransom notes and encrypted file masses. Article emphasizes ransomware-support infrastructure; pipeline missed both the impact phase and pre-impact staging. Phrase: 'Ransomware Support'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass file creation of .txt or .html ransom notes alongside rapid file extension changes (legitimate-to-.ransomware-ext) in user profile or shared drives. Alert on >10% of drive encrypted in <1 hour; correlate with VSS deletion and backup-mount enumeration.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Network Discovery Pre-Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware-as-a-service operations require network reconnaissance before encryption. Pipeline omitted discovery-phase detections. Article context implies multi-stage attack for maximizing ransom.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child chains: net.exe/quser/systeminfo followed by file-share enumeration (dir \\*\c$, net view \\*). Flag Get-ChildItem recursion on network paths, concurrent SMB 445 handshakes to multiple subnets, and WMI queries (Win32_Share, Win32_LogicalDisk).

suggestion.title: Sanctioned Entity Infrastructure Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article is about sanctions enforcement; pipeline should flag infrastructure IOCs (domains, ASNs, payment wallets) associated with the named VPN and cryptor sellers. No IOCs extracted at all.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain a sanctioned-provider blocklist (VPN domains, cryptor-seller hosting, payment infrastructure) and alert on any direct connection attempts, DNS queries, or HTTP requests. Cross-reference with known ransomware-affiliate infrastructure for early warning.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Untrusted Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages were 'disguised as student proxies'—malicious npm packages installed via dependency resolution. Article phrase: '148 npm Packages Disguised as Student Proxies'. Pipeline missed detection for supply-chain compromise entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install / yarn / pnpm execution for packages with malicious indicators: names mimicking proxy tools, zero/minimal download history, registry timestamps inconsistent with user history. Alert on suspicious package manifests referencing external scripts or postinstall hooks reaching unknown C2.

suggestion.title: NodeJS Process Establishing Unexpected Outbound Connections
suggestion.rationale: DDoS botnet requires C2 communication. Article: 'Turned Browsers Into a DDoS Botnet' implies command-and-control callbacks from browser/node contexts. Pipeline did not model C2 detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate node_modules network egress. Alert on node.exe, node processes spawned by browsers, or script engines opening connections to non-standard ports, international IPs (especially if not correlating to CDN), or repeated re-connection attempts characteristic of botnet heartbeats.

suggestion.title: Browser JavaScript Injection and Malicious Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes browser transformation into DDoS bot. Malicious code injected via npm→browser. Article phrase: 'Turned Browsers Into a DDoS Botnet'. Pipeline missed behavioral signatures of JavaScript execution and injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser processes (Edge, Chrome, Firefox) for suspicious child process spawning, WebSocket or XMLHttpRequest to attacker C2, or in-memory injection patterns. Cross-reference with npm package installation timeline to correlate postinstall hooks with browser compromise timing.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound HTTP/S Traffic from Browser DDoS Bot
suggestion.rationale: Compromised browsers executing DDoS on external targets. Article: 'Turned Browsers Into a DDoS Botnet'. Pipeline did not suggest impact/exfiltration detection (traffic volume, request patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous traffic volume or rate from single browser instances: sustained > 1000 req/s, target-agnostic flooding patterns, or Request headers identical across floods (fingerprint of script-driven botnet vs. user traffic). Correlate with known DDoS victim IPs or subnets.

suggestion.title: npm Registry or Package Repository Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: 148 packages uploaded or modified by attacker. Article: 'npm Packages Disguised as Student Proxies' implies account compromise or registry injection. Pipeline missed registry-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn package repository access logs for: new package uploads by inactive or suspicious accounts, version bumps with changed package size / hash not matching source repo, metadata injection (homepage, repository URLs pointing to attacker infrastructure), or rapid publish-unpublish cycles indicative of testing malicious artifacts.

suggestion.title: Compromised npm Account Behavioral Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attack likely required compromised maintainer accounts or new attacker-owned accounts with rapid org/team membership escalation. Pipeline did not model auth/account layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm account logins from new geographic regions, new API tokens generated and immediately used for package publish, bulk package publishing by low-reputation or newly-created accounts, or accounts suddenly shifting from consumer (install) to publisher (release) profile.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Salesforce API Token Creation or Unauthorized API Access
suggestion.rationale: ShinyHunters campaigns consistently pivot through API tokens to maintain persistence and escalate access within SaaS targets. Article describes 'three Salesforce attack paths'—API abuse is standard for Salesforce-focused threat actors. Look for: 'Three Salesforce Attack Paths' implies API-centric exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API token creation events outside normal maintenance windows, API calls from IPs/geolocations inconsistent with user baseline, and token usage spikes within minutes of creation. Flag OAuth tokens generated by service accounts during non-business hours or with overly permissive scopes (data:read, data:write on sensitive objects).

suggestion.title: Salesforce Mass Data Export or Unusual SOQL Query Volume
suggestion.rationale: ShinyHunters operates as a data-theft-for-hire group; article title highlights year-long campaign implying sustained exfiltration. Salesforce breaches typically manifest as bulk queries or exports of customer/opportunity records.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SOQL queries returning >10k rows in single session, data exports initiated by non-Admin accounts, or API calls to /services/data/v**/query or bulk API endpoints returning unexpectedly large result sets. Correlate with off-hours access patterns.

suggestion.title: Phishing or Credential Harvest Targeting Salesforce Admins/Users
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'year of ShinyHunters Activity'—initial access for Salesforce compromises typically relies on phishing or credential reuse. No IOCs or phishing indicators extracted despite critical severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails containing Salesforce-lookalike domains, requests for MFA codes or session tokens, and credential submission to non-Salesforce endpoints. Cross-correlate with Salesforce login failures followed by successful logins from new IP/device within hours.

suggestion.title: MFA Bypass or Session Hijacking via Stolen Cookies/Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Salesforce-targeting campaigns routinely bypass MFA through token theft or session fixation. Article states 'three attack paths'—MFA evasion likely comprises at least one pathway for sustained access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Salesforce logins with MFA disabled or bypassed, session_id reuse across non-adjacent IPs, or successful logins immediately after failed MFA attempts. Flag browser/device fingerprint changes within same session.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Within Salesforce: Privilege Escalation to Admin or Custom Roles
suggestion.rationale: Once inside Salesforce, threat actors escalate to admin or high-privilege roles to access sensitive data and modify audit logs. Year-long campaign indicates sustained lateral movement within the platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on role assignment changes (especially to Admin or custom high-privilege roles) from non-HRIS automation accounts, permission set group additions by unexpected users, and sharing rule modifications enabling org-wide access to sensitive objects.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Audit Log Deletion or Modification Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated actors disable or delete audit logs to cover tracks. Article describes 'year of activity'—any campaign lasting >3 months without log tampering is rare. No defensive indicators extracted by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for login history record deletions, audit trail export or archival to unexpected destinations, disable of audit logging features (if permissions allow), or gaps in audit timestamps suggesting tampering. Cross-check against immutable cloud logging backups.

suggestion.title: Kimai: Successful Authentication Without Credential Entry
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'forge HMAC-signed cookies' and achieve 'account takeover.' This is the core exploitation path—detect authentication events (session creation, privilege escalation actions) that occur without corresponding password entry or login process. Cite: 'forge HMAC-signed cookies'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful Kimai authentication to admin or privileged accounts when the session bearer token (Symfony PHPSESSID or equivalent) appears in access logs without a preceding login event in the Kimai auth log or without password submission captured in web proxy.

suggestion.title: Kimai: Deployment with Unmodified Default APP_SECRET
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'Docker entrypoint does not override or validate' the default secret value. Detect containers deployed with default configuration. Cite: 'Docker image ships with APP_SECRET=change_this_to_something_unique... does not override'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Kimai container image deployments for missing or unset APP_SECRET environment variable override. Compare deployment manifests, container runtime config, and image metadata against hardened baselines that require explicit APP_SECRET configuration.

suggestion.title: Kimai: Suspicious Web Session Bulk Operations Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker forges cookie and gains 'account takeover,' they will perform lateral movement or data exfiltration. Monitor for bulk timesheet modifications, user creation, or configuration changes tied to hijacked sessions. Cite: 'account takeover' and Kimai's time-tracking purpose.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate session IDs with bulk write operations (mass timesheet edits, user/project creation, rate changes). Flag sessions showing off-hours or impossible-travel bulk modifications inconsistent with the legitimate account holder's behavior.

suggestion.title: Kimai: Impossible Travel Detection on Authentication Sessions
suggestion.rationale: Forged cookies can originate from attacker-controlled infrastructure. Detect session IPs and user-agents that violate geographic/temporal plausibility. Cite: 'unauthenticated attacker' forging cookies from arbitrary network locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Kimai session IPs, user-agents, and source locations per account. Flag sessions from IPs thousands of kilometers apart within seconds, or sessions from countries/ASNs never accessed by the account previously.

suggestion.title: Kimai: HTTP Cookie Header Anomalies (Known-Secret Signatures)
suggestion.rationale: If Kimai logs or proxies capture full cookie headers, HMAC-forged cookies may exhibit patterns (timestamps, signature structure) consistent with the known APP_SECRET. Cite: 'forge HMAC-signed cookies' using 'publicly-known Symfony kernel.secret'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Collect and parse Symfony session cookies (if readable in logs). Correlate cookie HMAC signatures against the known default APP_SECRET hash to identify forged cookies in web traffic.

suggestion.title: Kimai: Docker Image Scanning for Hardcoded Default Secrets
suggestion.rationale: Article's root cause is default secret in the official Docker image. Proactive detection should scan images pre-deployment. Cite: 'official Kimai Docker image ships with APP_SECRET=change_this_to_something_unique'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Kimai container images (registry names, tags matching Kimai) for hardcoded environment variables, .env files, or config artifacts containing the string 'change_this_to_something_unique' or Kimai's documented default secrets.

suggestion.title: TOTP Brute-Force via Unauthenticated 2FA Endpoint (UC_10_1 corrected)
suggestion.rationale: Article states endpoint 'accepts unauthenticated POST containing only fsNick and fsTwoFactorCode' with TOTP that is 'brute-forceable'; pipeline generated no detections for the core exploit. Article references UC_10_1 but pipeline output was empty. Original UC_10_1 detection hunts for hardcoded poc_2fa_brute.py tool (hallucinated/undocumented), bypassed by custom scripts. Should hunt behavior instead.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to /login?action=two-factor-validation from same source with 5+ distinct fsTwoFactorCode values in <300 seconds. Flag if request lacks prior session password authentication. Look for 401/403→200 response cascade indicating brute-force success. Correlate with immediate downstream authentication or sensitive operations.

suggestion.title: Session Creation Without Password Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states handler 'does not verify the password' yet 'issues full fsNick + fsLogkey session cookie pair'; anomalous authentication flow bypass should be detected at credential creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on session cookie issuance (fsLogkey created) from 2FA endpoint (/login?action=two-factor-validation) when no password-authentication event (hash check, password field submission, or MFA prompt initiation) appears in same session within prior 5 minutes. Indicates bypass of normal login flow.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Account Abuse After 2FA Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation grants full account access; pipeline should include hunt for behavioral divergence from baseline following suspicious 2FA activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate anomalous 2FA session creation with subsequent atypical user activity: invoking admin functions, exporting sensitive data, creating API tokens, modifying account settings, accessing resources outside baseline geography/time-of-day. Flag if baseline profile or geographic travel is impossible.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance: Enumeration of FacturaScripts /login Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in public /login endpoint; attackers must first discover FacturaScripts instances. Pipeline provided no reconnaissance-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 200/302 responses to /login endpoints from script-like user-agents (curl, Python-requests, Nmap, etc.) with rapid sequential probing. Flag sources explicitly querying /login?action=two-factor-validation, indicating targeted reconnaissance for this CVE endpoint.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Web Interface CSRF Exploitation via /level/15/exec/ URIs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names exploit URIs: '/level/15/exec/-' and '/level/15/exec/-/configure/http'. States these enable 'arbitrary commands' execution. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite clear HTTP-based attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP GET/POST requests to Cisco IOS web interface on ports 80, 443, or device management ports targeting /level/15/exec/* paths. Correlate with Cisco device configuration/command logs for unexpected execution within seconds of suspicious HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Remote Arbitrary Command Execution Post-CSRF
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via (1) show privilege (2) alias exec commands'. No execution-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco device logs for privilege-level-15 command execution without corresponding SSH/console login sessions. Flag atypical source IPs issuing commands via web interface (check syslog for HTTP-originated sessions).

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 Vulnerability Indicator Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'match against your vulnerability scanner'. Pipeline produced no IOC output. Vulnerability CVE is the primary detection anchor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanner results for CVE-2008-4128 in Cisco IOS 12.4. Cross-reference affected assets with network exposure (untrusted access paths, internet-facing ACLs). Escalate any matches given CISA KEV status and 2026-07-16 remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS 12.4 Public-Facing Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Standard asset-exposure hunt—the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' pattern. Zero exposure-focused use cases generated despite T1190 (public-facing exploitation) applicability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco IOS 12.4 devices with HTTP/HTTPS management ports (80, 443, 8080, 8443) routable from internet or DMZ. Prioritize by asset criticality. Verify patch status immediately given federal due date.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 — Cisco IOS 12.4 Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and names CVE-2008-4128 as the target: 'Cisco IOS 12.4 contains multiple cross-site forgery vulnerabilities.' CISA KEV means active exploitation; federal patch due 2026-07-16.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query endpoint/network inventory for Cisco IOS version 12.4 or CVE-2008-4128 matches. Alert on unpatched systems. Correlate against patch management DB — patch lag is 'the silent killer' per article guidance.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests to Cisco IOS Privileged URI Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack URIs: '/level/15/exec/-' and '/level/15/exec/-/configure/http'. These are concrete exploitation routes that should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests (POST/GET) to Cisco IOS management interface URIs ending in /level/15/exec or /configure/http, especially those carrying 'show privilege' or 'alias exec' commands in parameters or body. Flag external/untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS CSRF — Arbitrary Command Execution Signals
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via (1) a certain "show privilege" command' and '(2) a certain "alias exec" command.' These are the actual attack primitives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco IOS devices for sudden privilege escalation (esp. to level 15), alias command definitions, or config changes correlated with HTTP access to the vulnerable URIs. Flag changes outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Web Interface CSRF Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: CSRF exploitation typically involves crafted requests without valid session tokens. Article describes web-based attack surface (/level/15/exec URIs) that can be probed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to vulnerable URIs that lack expected CSRF tokens, session cookies, or auth headers. Look for repeated/scanning patterns, anomalous User-Agents, or requests from external/public IP ranges to internal Cisco IOS management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Cisco IOS 12.4 — Post-Exploitation Command Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: After gaining execution via T1190, attacker will run commands. Article promises 'arbitrary commands' — detection should monitor for anomalous command execution on unpatched devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Cisco IOS 12.4 systems flagged as vulnerable/unpatched, alert on: (a) unexpected command execution via HTTP/HTTPS session; (b) privilege level changes to 15; (c) configuration changes tied to privilege escalation commands.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Timeline Compliance — CVE-2008-4128 Patch Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-16.' CISA KEV imposes hard deadline; organizational compliance is measurable and auditable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated alerting: Any Cisco IOS device flagged for CVE-2008-4128 still unpatched as of 2026-07-16 triggers escalation. Track remediation progress against CISA deadline for regulatory/audit reporting.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 Vulnerable Device Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Cisco IOS 12.4 contains multiple cross-site forgery vulnerabilities' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL'. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan or query asset inventory for Cisco IOS versions matching 12.4.x running exposed management interfaces. Cross-reference patch compliance database against 2026-07-16 federal due date. Flag any unpatched instances as immediate exploitation risk given CISA KEV status.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests to Cisco IOS Privilege Escalation URIs
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable endpoints: '/level/15/exec/-' and '/level/15/exec/-/configure/http'. Exploitation requires HTTP requests to these exact URIs on exposed Cisco devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco IOS management interfaces containing URI patterns '/level/15/exec/' followed by command injection payloads. Correlate source IPs with internet-facing Cisco IOS devices. Flag any requests originating from external networks.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Unauthorized Privilege Level Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via 'show privilege' command and privilege level manipulation. Successful exploitation would result in arbitrary command execution at level 15 (highest privilege).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco IOS syslog for privilege level transitions to level 15 without corresponding authorization records. Look for 'alias exec' command installations paired with administrative URI access. Baseline normal privilege escalation timing and source—flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Management Interface Web Access from Untrusted Networks
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerabilities require CSRF capability and HTTP access to management URIs. Article implies public-facing exploitation vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cisco IOS devices with HTTP/HTTPS management interfaces reachable from external networks (non-RFC1918 sources). Correlate with patch status. Alert on any outbound CISA KEV exploitation signatures or cross-site forgery payloads in HTTP headers.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Configuration Backup Changes Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful arbitrary command execution (stated in article) would allow attackers to modify running-config or startup-config. Detection via backup drift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline hashes of Cisco IOS running and startup configs from pre-patch inventory. Monitor for unexpected modifications to these configs outside of change-control windows. Particularly flag additions of new 'alias exec' commands or privilege level entries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2008-4128 Cisco IOS Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2008-4128 — match against your vulnerability scanner' in the IOC section and cites standard asset-exposure hunt methodology. Pipeline generated zero detections for this known-exploited CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any successful CVE-2008-4128 vulnerability scan match or Cisco IOS 12.4 identification against internal or external-facing assets. Cross-check against patch baseline. Federal patch due-date 2026-07-16 is SOC escalation trigger.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS HTTP Management Interface CSRF Attack Vector Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes specific exploitation vectors: 'show privilege command to /level/15/exec/- URI' and 'alias exec command to /level/15/exec/-/configure/http URI'. No detection for HTTP requests matching these CSRF paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco IOS management interfaces (port 80/443) with URI patterns containing /level/15/exec/- or /level/15/exec/-/configure/http, especially those with command parameters like 'show privilege' or 'alias exec' from untrusted sources. CSRF attacks often have anomalous Referer headers or missing session context.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Arbitrary Command Execution Post-CSRF
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'execute arbitrary commands' post-exploitation. No detection for command execution artifacts in device logs following CSRF attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected 'show privilege' or 'alias exec' commands in Cisco IOS audit logs, especially if temporally correlated with suspicious HTTP requests to management interface. Flag configuration changes or privilege escalations without corresponding authorized change tickets.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing Cisco IOS Exposure Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active reconnaissance of exposed assets. Article references 'standard asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated no hunt for identifying vulnerable Cisco IOS on internet-facing networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference internet-wide scan data (Shodan, Censys, Project Sonar) for Cisco IOS HTTP management interfaces. Correlate with internal asset inventory to identify unaccounted exposures. Every exposed instance is exploitation-ready per active KEV catalog status.

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS 12.4 Patch Compliance and Version Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Cisco IOS 12.4 contains multiple cross-site forgery vulnerabilities'. Recommended hunt should include baseline inventory for patch-level risk detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Cisco IOS deployments for version 12.4 or equivalent unpatched variants. Identify systems not updated by federal due-date 2026-07-16. Generate remediation worklist ranked by exposure level (internet-facing > DMZ > internal).

suggestion.title: Cisco IOS Configuration Tampering via Alias Exec Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'alias exec' command exploitation to /configure/http URI as method to modify device behavior. No detection for unauthorized config changes post-CSRF attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco IOS configuration commit logs for unexpected 'alias' commands or HTTP-related config changes. Baseline known aliases; alert on new ones.
